outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.
outlooksByWeek.4: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.
outlooksByWeek.5: James Cook will likely require volume to exploit a Rams defense when the Bills face them in their Week 5 Monday night affair. Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.
outlooksByWeek.6: James Cook will seek the end zone for the fifth straight week when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. While Cook hasn't been heavily targeted in the passing game, he's posted 100-plus yard rushing efforts in three of his last four outings, garnering at least 21 carries at the same rate. Buffalo is a run-first offense, and the Week 6 matchup is very appealing; Las Vegas allows 5.2 yards per carry, again setting up Cook to be a top-tier option.
outlooksByWeek.8: James Cook needs heavy volume in Week 8 to bolster Buffalo's offense against the Ravens. That hasn't been a problem, as he's amassed 20-plus touches in four of the Bills' first six outings, and he's continued scoring, finding the end zone in each of his last five games. Prior to a Week 7 bye, Cook had his best game as a receiver, possibly elevating his floor even higher. Baltimore is a stout defense against the run, allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, the eighth-lowest total in the league, but they have surrendered 86 yards or more to an opposing back three times. Barring an unexpected change in usage, Cook should be able to flirt with those numbers in Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: James Cook brings a six-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 9 matchup against a stingy Vikings defense. He topped 20 carries in three straight contests and five of seven overall. Cook added five catches for 79 yards in his last two games after just 31 yards in his first five. Minnesota has allowed only four rushing scores through seven games, but a healthy 4.6 yards per carry in a blitz-heavy scheme. With Cook assured of heavy usage, he appears poised for solid production.
outlooksByWeek.10: James Cook's high volume creates a high floor and ceiling heading into the Bills' Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Cook amassed a season-high 31 carries in Week 9, his sixth game in eight outings with 20-plus touches, and has topped 100 total yards at the same ratio while scoring in seven straight games. While the Bills have a short week coming off a Monday night game, nothing has been shown to suggest Cook's role will be reduced. This suggests he'll run wild on a Jets defense that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs and one he posted 132 yards and two touchdowns against in one healthy outing in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.11: James Cook brings an eight-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He has at least 18 carries in five straight games and has topped 100 rushing yards in five of nine outings overall. Cook hasn't caught a pass in two weeks, an area where Miami has been vulnerable, allowing five touchdown receptions to running backs, the same number of rushing touchdowns they've surrendered. A quick turnaround to a Week 12 Thursday night game is the only concern for Cook's workload and high-end production.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ashton Jeanty continues to garner a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers. Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ashton Jeanty scored his first rushing touchdown of the season in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, but it was otherwise another lackluster performance for the second-year running back. Jeanty is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry, and the inefficiency is costing him volume, as he hasn't handled 20-plus touches in a game since Week 4. He remains involved as a pass catcher, however, hauling in at least three passes in every game this year while compiling a 26-251-2 line on 36 targets through six contests. Jeanty could contribute through the air in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 29th in receiving yards per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground while making an impact as a pass catcher. In the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams, the second-year player gained a season-low 15 rushing yards on eight carries, but caught all eight of his targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Jeanty has gotten at least six targets in six of seven games so far in 2026, turning that volume into a 34-312-3 line on 44 looks. but his 3.1 yards per carry suggests he simply isn't cut out to be a No. 1 back. He'll try to bring some balance to his stat line in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ashton Jeanty is coming off another poor effort, managing just 20 scrimmage yards on 11 touches in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. This time, he wasn't overshadowed by rookie Mike Washington, who lost a total of three yards on his six carries. Jeanty maintains a shaky hold on the top spot in the backfield, but he hasn't reached 30 rushing yards in a game since Week 4, and his contributions of late have been limited to his usage as a pass-catcher. Jeanty isn't likely to turn things around in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ashton Jeanty failed to generate much production in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, gaining 18 rushing yards on nine carries and catching all four of his targets for 46 yards. It's the sixth time in the last seven games he's generated more yards through the air than on the ground, but his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield may have tightened a bit with Mike Washington struggling over the last two weeks as well. Jeanty's outlook as a pass-catcher could improve if Brock Bowers misses time due to an ankle injury. During the two games the star tight end sat out at the beginning of the season, Jeanty caught 10 of 13 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Warren hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury. He leads the Colts with 30 catches despite missing the past two games, so Warren would immediately return to the fantasy starting range if he gains clearance to return in Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. Jacksonville is holding TEs to 35 yards per game but has allowed the position to score four times in six outings, and Warren has accounted for three of the six TDs scored by Colts other than Jonathan Taylor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Warren turned 10 targets into just 18 yards in his return from a two-game absence due to a groin injury in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. That performance sums up the sorry state of Indianapolis' passing game, but Warren's volume remains elite for a TE. He's back to being a set-and-forget starting option at the position now that he's healthy, especially with a favorable Week 9 home matchup on tap against the Cowboys. Dallas' defense is allowing 51 yards per game to TEs and has given up four TDs to the position, surrendering 26.6 points per game overall.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Warren has drawn at least seven targets in five of his last six appearances. The 2025 first-round pick remains a weekly fantasy starter at TE thanks to his hefty volume, even though he's averaging just 5.2 yards per target in the Colts' low-octane passing offense. Warren and the Colts will face a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed six receiving TDs in eight games to TEs. In addition to two touchdown catches, Warren has one rushing score this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Warren had a season-low three targets in a head-scratching Week 10 performance against the Dolphins after the Colts traded away starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Even after that dud, Warren is still averaging a healthy seven targets per game, and his 276 receiving yards and two receiving TDs lead all players still rostered by the Colts. Warren had a season-high nine catches when the Colts faced the Texans in Week 3 and should be similarly busy in the Week 11 rematch against a Houston defense that ranks among the league's 10 most generous units through the air. Don't let Warren's down game in Week 10 dissuade you from continuing to deploy him as a high-floor fantasy starter at TE.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Stefon Diggs found the end zone again last game for Washington. Diggs snagged three balls for 38 yards and the score in the 27-10 win over the Commanders. Diggs has scored in back-to-back outings, and five times overall in 2026. However, in Week 9, Diggs will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Stefon Diggs had a two-game scoring streak snapped last game for Washington. Diggs caught three passes for 51 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Diggs will look for a return to the end zone in Week 10 versus the Giants. New York has given up 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 20th in the league. However, do not expect much in the way of yardage, as the G-Men are yielding just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Stefon Diggs has scored in three of his last four games played for Washington. Diggs scored the game-winning touchdown last Thursday versus the Giants to bring his season total for receiving touchdowns to six. Diggs also posted a season-high 83 receiving yards for the game. He was targeted 10 times for the game, and should continue to see increased looks in the absence if Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a bad-weather win over the Bears in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his PATs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13.0) so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,
outlooksByWeek.7: Will Reichard remains a high-volume option once again as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 5 before Minnesota's bye, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts and two XPAs. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last four games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Colts squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to kickers (10.3) this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Will Reichard should remain a high-usage option as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Reichard stayed busy in Week 7 against the Colts, but he did miss his first kick of the season going 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts. Even so, the third-year boot has now gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, and nailed all nine of his XPAs this season. Detroit has ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Will Reichard will aim to get back on track as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Reichard didn't get much usage in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, missing a field goal attempt from 57 yards and converting his sole extra-point try. Even with a field goal miss in each of the last two weeks, the third-year kicker still sits at 18 of 20 on the year, and he's gone a perfect 10-for-10 on XPAs. Buffalo has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Will Reichard will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Reichard got back on track in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, making both of his two field-goal attempts. The kicker has now made two or more field goals in all but two of his eight outings this campaign, but the efficiency of the Vikings' offense could improve with Kirk Cousins taking over as the starting QB, turning some of his FG volume into PATs. Green Bay has also ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Will Reichard will seek to stay hot as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Reichard was perfect in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, nailing all six of his kicks with three field-goal makes. The third-year kicker has now converted 23 of 25 field-goal attempts and made all 13 of his XPAs across nine showings. The 49ers have allowed a middle-of-the-pack 8.0 points per game to kickers this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55.2 percent completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gunslinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return date uncertain. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Love will look to deliver a big win for the Packers in Week 5 against the Bears. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT in a close win over Tampa Bay in Week 4. The veteran quarterback has now completed a career-low 56 percent of passes for 1,041 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season, with 300 or more passing yards in two of four outings. Love will take on a Chicago defense that's ranked 12th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Love will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Love was on fire in a blowout win over the Bears in Week 5, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. After a shaky but still touchdown-heavy start to the season, he's now completed 73 percent or more of his passes in back-to-back weeks and totaled 564 passing yards with a 4:1 TD:INT ratio in that stretch. Love will have the perfect opportunity to replicate his greatness again, as Dallas has ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks (23.8) so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Love will look to keep an electric stretch going as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Love was solid in another Packers win in Week 6, completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, and he also made some noise on the ground with two rushes for 14 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year starter has now thrown for more than 275 yards in four of six games this season, and he's thrown two touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll enter another favorable matchup as the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks on the year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Love will aim to get the Packers back in the win column in Week 8 versus the Panthers. Even with Josh Jacobs back on the field at Detroit in Week 7, Green Bay still leaned on the passing game, with Love completing 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for two touchdowns in all but one game this season, but he's still totaled two in every outing. Love should have no problem continuing his success against a Carolina defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Love will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Love stayed hot in a Week 8 win over the Panthers, completing 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards with a 3:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for 250-plus yards in six of eight games and recorded two or more touchdowns in every outing of the season. Love will face a New England defense that ceded 211 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to his former backup, Malik Willis, this past weekend.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the Jaguars in Week 4. The rookie receiver caught three of five targets for 29 yards during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss, stepping up with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) out due to injuries. Meyers tied Mike Gesicki for third on the team in receptions, though he garnered two more targets than the tight end. He's still firmly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the passing game, but he's showing signs of being a reliable option in a banged-up WR room. Meyers will look to contribute against Jacksonville, whose defense ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed (527) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals visit the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He caught both of his targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both healthy, Meyers returned to a supporting role, supplying 91 yards on three kick returns and another 13 yards on two punt returns. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) could also return from a two-game absence, so both receivers could struggle to make much of a contribution against the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are at home in Week 8 to square off against Tennessee. He failed to catch either of his two targets in Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Meyers was unable to take advantage of Joe Burrow's productive day, as he threw for 292 yards and four TDs. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying a massive target share despite a solid matchup versus the Titans.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are in Spain to square off against the Falcons in Week 9. He caught all three of his targets for 34 yards during Cincinnati's thrilling overtime victory in Week 8. Meyers also accumulated 119 yards on five kick returns and 31 yards on two punt returns, as the Bengals clearly value his speed and versatility. However, with Ja'Marr Chase (11-141-1) and Tee Higgins (10-155-2) commanding most of Joe Burrow's attention in the passing game, Meyers' contributions will likely remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers in Week 10. He caught two of three targets for 47 yards and had a 16-yard carry during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Meyers also returned four kicks for 100 yards and finished second on the team in receiving yardage. The Bengals like to get the ball in his hands, but with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying the majority of Joe Burrow's attention, Meyers should remain on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals pay Washington a visit on Monday Night Football. He caught both targets for 20 yards and his first career touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 10 win. Meyers was on the receiving end of one of Joe Burrow's four passing scores while finishing fifth in receptions and yardage. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches despite playing in a very pass-friendly offense, as his role is simply capped with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dominating the target share.

player.seasonOutlook: Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Branch has received two targets in each of his last three games, even out-targeting Olamide Zaccheaus over the last two weeks (four to three). Additionally, Branch played a career-high 23% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 4 win over the Saints, suggesting his offensive role may be growing. He's also in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 734 receiving yards to wideouts through four contests this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zachariah Branch will likely play a complimentary role in Atlanta's receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Branch has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching all four of his targets for 25 yards. He appears to have overtaken Olamide Zaccheaus in the wide-receiver room but likely won't have much fantasy value without scoring a touchdown. That being said, Branch could succeed against a Bears defense that's giving up 10.4 yards per target to opposing WRs this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow as the Falcons' face the 49ers in Week 7. Branch has caught all six of his targets over the last three weeks, accumulating 34 receiving yards. He appears to have emerged as Atlanta's No. 3 wideout, as Olamide Zaccheaus hasn't caught a pass since the Week 3 win over the Packers. Regardless, Branch will likely struggle in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has given up just 8.9 yards per completion through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Branch played a career-high 37% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 7 win over the 49ers. Despite this, he logged just two touches for 17 yards and will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. That could be difficult against a strong Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just five receiving touchdowns to WRs all season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will likely play a reserve role in Atlanta's wide receiver room if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Branch was unable to practice all of last week after sustaining a hamstring injury in the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, so he'll definitely need to make some progress to suit up Sunday. On the season, the rookie wideout has caught 10 of 12 targets for 64 yards and rushed once for eight yards, contributing primarily on special teams. If Branch plays in Week 10, he'll likely struggle against a Kansas City secondary that's allowed just 9.9 yards per completion this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.7: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.
outlooksByWeek.8: Adonai Mitchell has a minimal role in the Jets' limited passing attack entering a Week 8 clash with the Raiders. Returning from a four-week absence in Week 7, Mitchell failed to record a catch on his three targets. Omar Cooper's emergence paired with Garrett Wilson's steady presence won't leave a plethora of opportunities for the remaining Jets' receivers in a run-first offense, giving Mitchell too few chances to exploit a defense that's allowing a generous 8.9 yards per target through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Adonai Mitchell faces an uphill battle if he hopes to repeat a career outing when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After being shut out since Week 2, Mitchell popped for seven catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown in Week 8, shifting the spotlight from surging rookie Omar Cooper. Mitchell has always shown big-play potential but sees inconsistent opportunities. This sets him up as a high-potential, low-ceiling option against a Chiefs secondary that's allowing just 6.9 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.10: Adonai Mitchell's roller coaster season heads into a favorable spot when the Jets face the Bills in Week 10. He failed to record a catch in Week 9 despite seven targets, his second game in three weeks without a reception. Mitchell remains a vertical option, and he's averaged 6.8 targets across five healthy appearances. With the Jets likely throwing from behind as the game progresses, he's a reasonable bet to flourish against a secondary that's allowed 28 receptions of 20-plus yards, the eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Adonai Mitchell continues to bring inefficiency through steady opportunity with the Jets set to face the Chargers in Week 11. Mitchell has 24 targets over the last three weeks but has converted them into just 10 catches, tallying a solid 201 yards. The Chargers' secondary is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts, and Mitchell figures to see consistent volume, particularly with Omar Cooper (ankle) uncertain to play. But Geno Smith's ankle injury also brings ambiguity to this passing game, making Mitchell a high-upside, low-floor option.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Ward has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game heading into the Titans' Week 8 trip to Cincinnati. The second-year QB has an ugly 4:5 TD:INT while throwing for just 168 yards per game. Cincinnati's defense has limited QBs to a 6:4 TD:INT, but the Bengals allowed Baltimore's Tyler Huntley to throw for a career-high 298 yards in a Week 7 game that the Bengals won by 22 points. Until Ward shows signs of progress as a passer, he'll remain a fantasy non-factor, even in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Ward had his best game of the season in Tennessee's 43-36 Week 8 loss to the Bengals, prior to a Week 9 bye. He threw for 300 yards for the first time in his career and delivered a pair of touchdown passes for his first multi-TD performance through the air all season. Ward has a chance to build on that effort in Week 10 against a Jaguars defense that has been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. The far larger sample of subpar football from the 2025 first overall pick prior to his strong outing last game suggests Ward remains tough to trust for now, even in superflex formats. The Jaguars are giving up the 11th-most passing yards per game, though they have more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes allowed (eight).
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Ward has taken a noticeable step forward in Tennessee's last two games, even though the Titans lost both to drop to 1-8. After throwing for a career-high 304 yards and tossing multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season against the Bengals, Ward threw for 231 yards and two TDs in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville, his second-highest passing yards total of the campaign. His four touchdown passes in that two-game stretch match Ward's total from his first seven starts of the season. The improving 2025 first overall pick has a nice opportunity to keep building momentum in Week 11 against a dreadful Dallas defense that has surrendered a 19:4 TD:INT ratio en route to allowing 28.2 points per game. Ward's underwhelming larger body of work leaves him out of the starting mix in most single-QB formats, but he's a sneaky-good Week 11 superflex option.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory over Baltimore. Gesicki extended his TD streak to four consecutive games, as he's now compiled a 13-165-5 receiving line on 18 targets in 2026. He'll try to make it five in a row versus Tennessee's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (11.1) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 interconference tilt against the Falcons. He caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. The 76 receiving yards were Gesicki's most in a game since he went for 78 in the season opener, and the 31-year-old was able to extend his streak of outings with a TD catch to five. He now owns a 17-241-6 line on 24 targets through seven contests and will try to make it six straight with a score versus an Atlanta defense allowing 14.4 fantasy points per game (T-20th) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. He corralled both of his targets for 11 yards during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Gesicki's five-game streak with a touchdown came to an end with all three of Joe Burrow's TD passes going to Ja'Marr Chase (one) and Tee Higgins (two). Gesicki's fantasy value has been reliant on TDs in 2026, so he'll try to start another streak of consecutive trips to the endzone versus a Pittsburgh defense his initial scoring stretch started against back in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Washington for a Week 11 tilt on Monday Night Football. He caught one of two targets for nine yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, unable to capitalize on Joe Burrow throwing for 409 yards and four TDs. Gesicki now sports a 3-20-0 receiving line on four targets over his last two outings after catching a touchdown in each of his five previous games. He does, however, get a favorable matchup versus a Commanders defense allowing 20.2 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Olave ranks fifth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (90.9) and sixth in receptions per game (7.0) through seven contests. Additionally, quarterback Tyler Shough is averaging a league-high 39.0 pass attempts per game, which suggests Olave will continue to produce at a high level going forward. He's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 29.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top pass catcher in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Olave added another productive outing to his impressive 2026 campaign during the Week 9 overtime win against the Browns, catching seven of 12 targets for 98 yards. On the season, Olave ranks sixth in the NFL in targets per game (10.4) and seventh in receiving yards per game (91.8). Olave's high volume will likely continue as well, with Tyler Shough tied for the most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the league through eight games. Expect Olave to succeed against a depleted Panthers secondary that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chris Olave is expected to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Olave was overshadowed by 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, as he logged season-lows in targets, receptions and yards. Despite this poor showing, Olave remains eighth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (84.9) and 10th in targets per game (9.7), so his fantasy outlook remains very positive going forward. However, he's set to face a tough Bears defense that's allowed just 29.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to look like an unstoppable force for Seattle with a Week 8 matchup against the Bears on tap. Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City this past Sunday, marking his sixth performance of 100-plus receiving yards through seven weeks. The budding superstar leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns through seven weeks. He'll next face a Chicago defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 9.51 yards per target yielded to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on a record-setting pace heading into Seattle's Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Though the Seahawks were crushed by Chicago in Week 8, Smith-Njigba put up another big game with six catches for 118 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. The star wideout is up to a league-leading 985 receiving yards through eight weeks, putting him on pace to break the NFL's all-time record for receiving yards in a season. He'll have a prime opportunity to add onto his impressive stat line in Week 9, as the Cardinals are tied for 25th in the league with 23.7 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a rare quiet game with Seattle's Week 10 matchup in Las Vegas on tap. The All-Pro wideout logged a season-low 51 yards on seven catches this past Sunday against Arizona, though he still drew a healthy 10 targets. Drew Lock (oblique) started at quarterback for the Seahawks in that contest and is expected to do so again in Week 10, as Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib) is likely to remain sidelined. Regardless, Smith-Njigba could feast against a Raiders defense that ranks 26th in the league with 23.6 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season.
