Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on multiple field goal attempts in four consecutive games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye. The standout kicker should pick up where he left off in Week 9 against the 0-7 Chargers, who have allowed 14 made field goals in seven games while giving up 25 points per game. Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season and remains a set-and-forget starter at the position. It's worth checking whether Fairbairn was dropped in your league during his Week 8 bye.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ka'imi Fairbairn has made multiple field goals in five consecutive games, going 14-for-14 over that productive stretch. Houston's standout kicker remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter for a Week 10 road game against the Browns, who are allowing 21.8 points per game. Cleveland has allowed 19 made field goals in nine games, while Fairbairn has missed just once on 19 attempts through eight games while making all 21 of his PAT tries.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ka'imi Fairbairn is 19-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-24 on PAT tries for the Texans heading into a Week 11 home game against the Colts. Indianapolis is tied for the second-most made field goals allowed (21) and is surrendering 27.1 points per game overall. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter at the kicker position, as usual, in Week 11 as the 3-6 Texans try to bolster their dwindling playoff hopes.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. In Coker's three full games this season, he's caught 22 of 31 targets for 301 yards and two touchdowns. With Young averaging 40.2 passing attempts per game, it appears as if Coker will continue to produce at a high level going forward. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay secondary that's allowed five touchdowns to wideouts through six games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jalen Coker (shoulder) is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets if active for Carolina's Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Coker underwhelmed in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of four targets for nine yards, his least productive game since Week 7 of 2025. Coker has been one of the league's best wideouts when healthy this season, averaging 5.8 receptions and 77.5 yards per game in his four full games in 2026. If active for Week 8, he could have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Packers secondary that's allowed 35.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Carolina's top receivers in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Coker has been relatively quiet since returning from injury in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching just nine of 22 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over his last three contests. Despite this, Coker ranks second on the Panthers in targets (7.3), receptions (4.5) and receiving yards per game (60.7) this season, suggesting more production could be in the near future. Coker could struggle in Week 9, however, as Denver's secondary has allowed just 6.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top receiving options in the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Coker has cooled down along with the majority of Carolina's offense over the last three weeks, catching just seven of 14 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, Bryce Young is still tied for the most pass attempts per game in the NFL (38.5), which bodes well for Coker's fantasy outlook going forward. Coker could take advantage of a New Orleans secondary that's given up 11.1 yards per completion this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jalen Coker will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. After catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns across Carolina's first two games this season, Coker has managed just 15 receptions on 35 targets for 189 yards and one touchdown over his last six contests. He remains second on the team in receptions (31), targets (53) and receiving yards (393) but likely can't be trusted after four consecutive performances of less than 10.0 fantasy points. However, Coker is in for a favorable Week 11 matchup against a Baltimore secondary that's allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts through nine contests this year.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.
outlooksByWeek.8: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Hunter Henry will need to overcome a foot injury if he's to help the Patriots loosen up a stingy Packers defense in Week 9. Henry hauled in all three of his first-half targets in Week 8 before exiting. Should he play, the challenge becomes finding holes against a Green Bay defense that's allowing just 5.8 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. Eli Raridon has shown promise and would benefit from a potential Henry absence, but the matchup concerns remain.
outlooksByWeek.10: Hunter Henry figures to be a popular option for the Patriots in Week 10 against a Lions defense that struggles against opposing tight ends. Henry has just three targets in each of his last two games and has topped 48 yards just twice all season, but Week 10 presents an inviting opportunity. Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to tight ends and 8.2 yards per target, the highest numbers across the league. With New England potentially missing its top two running backs, a pass-heavy script would set Henry up for top-end production.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games for the Eagles due to a hamstring ailment, leaving his status for Week 7 versus the Cowboys in jeopardy. Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Barkley's place, while also catching four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley can somehow suit up, he will be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Saquon Barkley returned from injury for the Eagles, only to tweak his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, though played sparingly in the second half of the game, and ultimately could be sidelined again in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If Barkley is able to suit up, he will face a Washington defense that has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026.  The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per clash, which is 14th in the league. In addition, Washington has allowed just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the league. If neither Barkley nor backup Dameon Pierce can play, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back.
outlooksByWeek.9: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, Saquon was otherwise held in check with 54 scrimmage yards in a dismal 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia does not appear likely to trade Barkley to a contender, leaving him primed for a revenge game against his former squad, the New York Giants, in Week 9. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles, but was otherwise bottled up. Barkley managed just 22 yards on the ground along with the score in the 19-11 loss to the Giants before the bye. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, Saquon will likely see a stacked box in Week 11 versus the Steelers. Pittsburgh has been stellar in defending the run in 2026 as well, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league. Likewise, Pittsburgh has yielded just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ollie Gordon will bring consistent volume into the Dolphins' Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Since taking over as the team's lead back, Gordon has at least 17 carries in four of his last five games, though he's seen a minimal amount of work in the passing game, snagging just six passes. Detroit has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs, mainly due to opponents passing on them at will, which Miami isn't equipped to do. With volume paramount for the position, Gordon is a safe bet to pile up carries, creating a nice floor that can be elevated if he finds the end zone.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ollie Gordon should log heavy volume again in an inviting Week 10 matchup when the Dolphins face the Colts. Gordon has 16 or more carries in three straight games and five of his last six, scoring four times and topping 100 yards twice. He has no major competition for carries with Jaylen Wright injured and sparingly used even when healthy. Indianapolis is allowing 4.8 yards per carry, the third-highest mark in the league, setting Gordon up to take advantage of a big workload.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ollie Gordon will have a heavy workload for as long as the Dolphins remain competitive in Week 11 against the Bills. Gordon has at least 16 carries in five straight games and caught a season-high four passes in Week 10, though Miami was in a four-quarter game against the Colts. Buffalo figures to be a far more difficult opponent, which could force a heavier pass-game script. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Gordon could be touchdown-dependent for top-end fantasy scoring.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets. After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake Maye will look to continue providing elite production when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. While his volume was low, Maye completed a season-high 80% of his passes in Week 8, tossing multiple touchdowns for the fifth straight week while running for a score for the third time in four games. The Packers figure to offer fair resistance, allowing multiple touchdown passes just twice all season, snagging as many interceptions as touchdowns (10) while surrendering just 6.2 yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashee Rice wasn't able to get healthy over Kansas City's Week 5 bye, and the wide receiver sat out a Week 6 win over the Chargers due to knee and hamstring issues. His absence didn't significantly affect the offense as Kenneth Walker dominated against the Chargers. In his three full games this season, Rice has produced a 13-190-1 line on 17 targets. If he's able to return in Week 7, he'll have a tough matchup against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashee Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring strain, missing his second straight game in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. Before getting injured in Week 4, Rice had produced an 11-171-0 line on 15 targets over the prior two games. Once he's cleared to return, he should immediately be Patrick Mahomes' top option in the passing game. If Rice does get back in the lineup in Week 8, he'll be facing a Broncos secondary that could once again be without Pat Surtain but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashee Rice returned in Week 8 from a two-game absence due to a hamstring issue and caught his second touchdown of the season in Kansas City's loss to the Broncos. In four full games this season, Rice has managed a 20-243-2 line on 25 targets as Patrick Mahomes' top downfield option, but he has yet to receive double-digit targets in any game. That's a volume he reached four times in eight contests in 2025. Rice will look to put the injury further behind him in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rashee Rice put together another quiet performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, catching five of seven passes for 49 yards. The fourth-year wide receiver has a 12-102-1 line on 15 targets over the last two weeks since returning from a two-game absence due to lower-body injuries, and his breakout potential could be limited even further if Patrick Mahomes misses any time after picking up an elbow injury against the Jets. Rice will try to make a bigger contribution in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rashee Rice's role and volume did not change much in Week 10 against the Falcons, even with trade deadline acquisition Josh Downs in the lineup for Kansas City. Rice caught five of six targets for 82 yards, the third time in seven games he's recorded at least 80 receiving yards. The fourth-year wide receiver is the top downfield option for Patrick Mahomes, but his 30-374-2 line on 38 targets is far from elite production. Rice will look to take a step forward in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian Watson will look to continue his dominance as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Watson recorded a stellar performance in Week 5 against the Bears, bringing in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout has cemented himself as Jordan Love's top option in the passing game, with a 26-474-6 receiving line through five games. Watson will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Watson will look to get back in the end zone as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Watson finished Week 6 against the Cowboys tying a season-low of three catches, but he was still able to convert them into 64 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now amassed 29 catches for 538 yards and six touchdowns this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Christian Watson will aim to return to dominance as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Watson brought in five of eight targets for a team-leading 57 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, which was his lowest yardage total since Week 4. The wideout still has a 34-595-6 receiving line through the first seven games of the season, and he's not far off from outpacing his stat totals from the 2024 and 2025 season. Carolina has ranked a stern fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian Watson will look to heal from a broken rib ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Watson injured himself in the second quarter of Week 8 against the Panthers, but he returned to the game in the third quarter after a brief trip to the hospital. Even with these setbacks, the starting wideout finished the game with an impressive stat line, hauling in eight of 10 targets for 113 yards. He's now sitting at a receiving line of 42-708-6, which is career-high in both receptions and yards. He'll face a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian Watson will look to build off a career day as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Watson put together a prolific performance in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, bringing in seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown. The wideout now holds a career-high receiving line of 49-879-7 on 74 targets. He'll face a Minnesota secondary that he tore up with 6 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns against in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will operate as the Buccaneers' signal caller if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield has been sidelined for Tampa Bay's last three contests, but head coach Todd Bowles told reporters he's "supposed to practice" Wednesday, suggesting he could return Sunday. Before the injury, Mayfield struggled in his first three games, throwing for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also losing three fumbles. However, he could bounce back against a Panthers defense that's allowed 22.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Mayfield had a very light workload in his return from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, completing seven of 11 pass attempts for 64 yards and a touchdown. In his first three games this season, Mayfield threw for an average of 205 yards, 0.7 touchdowns and 0.7 interceptions per contest. He'll look to catch fire against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' passing game into the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He was the first quarterback since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, doing so in a rainy Week 8 divisional matchup against the Falcons. Since returning from injury in Week 7, Mayfield has attempted just 14 total passes, partially due to last week's rainy conditions. However, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has heavily leaned on the ground game over the last four weeks, which is a poor sign for Mayfield's fantasy outlook. Mayfield is still in for a favorable Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that has allowed 22.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through seven contests.
outlooksByWeek.11: Baker Mayfield (foot/ankle) is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense if active for the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Mayfield sustained an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Week 9 loss to the Bears, putting his availability for Sunday's contest in jeopardy. Since returning from a thumb injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, Mayfield has completed 25 of 46 pass attempts for 307 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, suggesting his fantasy outlook is bleak going forward. However, he could find success against a Lions defense that's struggled this season, allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks (25.0) in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day return window opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans and has rejoined his teammates at practice but remains on injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to London to face the Jaguars. Considering the Texans just traded for WR Marvin Harrison, Dell seems unlikely to be a major contributor in Week 6, even if he is activated from IR. Dell isn't viable in Week 6 but could be worth stashing if you have an open bench or IR slot, as Houston's 2023 third-round pick averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to sustaining a major knee injury late in the 2024 season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day window to return from IR opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, and he has a realistic chance of being activated ahead of the Week 7 home game against the Giants after sitting out against the Titans in Week 5 and the Jaguars in Week 6. Even if Dell suits up in Week 7, he's likely to be brought along slowly in a Texans WR room that also has Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for playing time. Dell is a viable bench stash, but he isn't a recommended starting option against the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tank Dell made his season debut in Week 7, ahead of Houston's Week 8 bye. The 2023 third-round pick showcased his trademark big-play ability with a 43-yard catch on his only target. This was Dell's first game action since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign due to a knee injury. The Texans also have Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for snaps at wide receiver, which makes Dell a risky Week 9 fantasy option against the Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack at defending WRs. Dell is worth stashing on the bench, as he delivered starter-level fantasy production prior to his extended absence, but he'll need to increase his involvement to regain fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tank Dell looked like his old self in his second game back from a nearly two-year absence due to a knee injury. He caught four of nine targets for 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers after securing a 43-yard catch against the Giants in Dell's Week 8 return to action. If Dell is still floating around on waivers in your league, he's worth adding in most formats, as he was a viable fantasy WR2 prior to his injury and just turned 27 years old. Dell is a viable option in Week 10 against Cleveland's decent secondary, but he should at least be rostered even if you have safer flex options for Week 10.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tank Dell had just 21 yards on four targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after turning nine targets into 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The speedy wideout continues to offer big-play potential in Week 11 against the Colts, who give up 15.4 yards per catch to wide receivers. Dell's floor is low in Houston's deep WR room, but his ceiling is certainly high enough to warrant flex consideration, especially with surging QB C.J. Stroud having thrown 13 touchdown passes in the Texans' last four games.

player.seasonOutlook: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving tight end during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite signing with the Panthers in early August, Waller ranks first amongst the team's tight end corps in targets (19), receptions (13), yards (148) and touchdowns (two) through four games. Waller could receive fewer opportunities in Week 6, however, with Jalen Coker (quadriceps) expected to return from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a difficult matchup against an Eagles defense that's allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' primary pass-catching tight end in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite going with a catch in Carolina's Week 6 win over the Eagles, Waller still leads the TE corps in targets (18) and yards (148) through five contests. However, Waller will likely see less opportunities to score with Jalen Coker back from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that's already allowed four receiving touchdowns to TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving option at tight end in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite the Panthers' poor offensive performance in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, Waller was productive, catching one of two targets for 50 yards and a touchdown. On the season, Waller has paced Carolina's tight-end corps in touchdowns (three), targets (22) and yards (198). However, he could struggle against a strong Packers defense in Week 8 that's allowed just 9.0 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season, the second-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Darren Waller will look to bounce back from another poor performance in Carolina's Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Waller has underwhelmed over the last two weeks, catching just two of four targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Despite this, he still ranks first amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (24), yards (209) and touchdown (three), though he still likely isn't reliable enough to be a weekly starter. Waller could have success against Denver in Week 9, however, as its defense has allowed 16.9 fantasy points per game to tight ends this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Darren Waller will look to continue building on his stellar performance in the Panthers' Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Waller is coming off his best game of the season in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, catching eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. He's clearly established himself as Carolina's top receiving tight end, leading the team's TE corps in targets (34), receptions (23), yards (299) and touchdowns (four) through eight games. Additionally, Waller is in for a great Week 10 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's allowed 16.1 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Waller leading Carolina's tight end corps in receptions (25), targets (38) and receiving yards (323) through nine games this year, he's been super inconsistent as of late. The veteran has logged two-or-fewer receptions in four of his last five games, with the exception coming in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, in which he caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. Waller is likely too inconsistent to start right now, despite a strong Week 11 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed six touchdowns to opposing TEs through nine contests this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.
outlooksByWeek.5: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.6: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Carnell Tate had 70 receiving yards and his first NFL touchdown in Tennessee's Week 6 win over the Colts and broke out for 145 receiving yards against the Ravens in Week 4, but he was held to just six yards by the Texans in between. The rookie, fourth overall pick is still searching for consistency in a Titans passing game that ranks among the league's worst, but Tate has shown enough upside to warrant a lineup spot as a flex option in most formats heading into a Week 7 home game against the Browns. Cleveland has been weaker than league average at defending wide receivers, allowing 157 yards per game and seven TDs in six games to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Carnell Tate has recorded at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four games, establishing himself as a reliable fantasy option despite the ongoing struggles of Titans QB Cam Ward. Facing a Bengals defense that just allowed eight catches for 137 yards and a TD to top Ravens WR Zay Flowers, Tate is a high-end flex option for Week 8. The rookie fourth overall pick is averaging more than seven targets per game and could get plenty of opportunities if the 1-6 Titans fall behind as expected on the road against the 4-2 Bengals.
outlooksByWeek.10: Carnell Tate sat out Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals prior to a Week 9 bye due to a shoulder injury. The rookie, fourth overall pick is expected to return in Week 10 against the Jaguars and will likely reprise his role as the top option in Tennessee's underwhelming passing offense. Tate racked up at least 69 yards in three of his last four appearances, making him a strong flex play in a game that's likely to feature a negative game script for the 1-7 Titans, leading to more passes. The 6-2 Jaguars are allowing 175 yards per game to WRs, though they have limited the position to four TDs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Carnell Tate hasn't played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Prior to his absence, the rookie fourth overall pick had at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four appearances. If Tate gets the green light to play in Week 11, he would be a high-end flex option against a Dallas defense that's allowing 158 yards and a TD per game through the air to wide receivers. Titans QB Cam Ward is coming off his two best outings of the season in Tate's absence.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Washington brings a steady workload but limited yardage potential into the Dolphins' Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Washington has commanded at least five targets in all five games, three times reaching eight or more, but has topped out at 67 yards, operating mainly on short, slot routes while Miami struggles to find a vertical passing game. The Jets are allowing just 7.3 yards per target; Washington too is averaging 7.3 yards per target, setting him up for a rather predictable Week 7 outing where he'll need a heavy target share to offer anything more than bye-week replacement scoring.
outlooksByWeek.8: Malik Washington will hope for additional volume in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He collected a season-low three targets in Week 7, and volume has been the key to his fantasy relevance, having topped 56 yards once all season. It's a low-volume passing game that may be pressed into higher throw rates if Miami falls behind early, but Washington's role underneath doesn't create much upside despite facing a secondary that's surrendering a generous 8.8 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Washington's usage is on a slight decline as the Dolphins prepare to face the Lions in Week 9. Washington has just nine targets over the last two games, and while he scored his first touchdown of the year in Week 8, he's averaged under 10 yards per reception in three straight games. Detroit is allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers, but they have been far more vulnerable to tight ends. Washington will require higher volume if he's to return meaningful fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Washington's workload appears to be drying up ahead of the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup with the Colts. Washington averaged 7.2 targets in five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye but has just 12 looks over the three games since, reaching 28 yards just once. Indianapolis is allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but with Miami's passing game struggling and Caleb Douglas emerging, Washington's decreasing role will make for a risky play with minimal upside.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Washington's opportunities continue to decline as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Washington recorded three targets in Week 10, the third time in four weeks since Miami's Week 6 bye that he's failed to garner more looks. While Miami figures to throw from behind against Buffalo, Kyle McCord spread his 32 pass attempts in Week 10 across 11 different options, all while rookie Chris Bell was sidelined. With just one touchdown catch all season, Washington doesn't seem likely to pop against a defense that's allowed 11 touchdown catches to wide receivers, the fourth-highest total in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to take on the Bengals for a Week 10 AFC North showdown. He had his best showing of the season during Week 8's victory, rushing 15 times for 56 yards and his first touchdown with Pittsburgh. Dowdle battled a toe injury in the early portion of the season, but he's starting to come along, tallying 15 touches in each of his previous two outings. He will look to keep improving versus Cincinnati's 15th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.9) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an interconference tilt. He rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both targets for eight yards during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. Dowdle and Jaylen Warren (7 carries, 15 yards) both struggled to make much of an impact, as the Steelers managed just 247 total yards of offense on the night. Dowdle could be more involved against an Eagles squad that has lost seven in a row, but Philadelphia's defense is allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing RBs (19.7) in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Hubbard had his worst performance of the season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, accumulating just 60 yards on 11 touches. Across six contests this season, Hubbard has amassed 459 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six total touchdown, the 19th-most total yards in the NFL. He'll have a good opportunity to rebound in Week 8 against a Packers defense that's allowed 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain a vital piece of the Panthers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Hubbard was one of the few bright spots in Carolina's Week 8 loss to the Packers, totaling 119 yards and a touchdown on 29 touches. He ranks 10th in the NFL in touches per game (20.0) and 11th in total yards per game (98.6), which bodes well for his outlook going forward. Hubbard could thrive against a Broncos defense that's allowed 25.3 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
