outlooksByWeek.10: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain Carolina's bell-cow back during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Hubbard has now logged 20-plus touches in five of the Panthers' last six games, averaging the eighth-most touches per game (20.0) in the NFL this year. His receiving volume has jumped over the last three weeks as well, catching 15 of 18 targets for 82 yards during that span. Hubbard figures to have a huge game in Week 10 against a New Orleans defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chubba Hubbard will continue operating as the Panthers' bell-cow back in the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Hubbard put Carolina on his back during the Week 10 win over the Saints, accumulating 172 yards and two touchdowns on 32 touches. On the season, Hubbard ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.3) eighth in scrimmage yards per game (106.4), suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs as the year progresses. Despite this, he could struggle against a good Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through nine games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road for an interconference clash against the Titans in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 6. Boston tied for last in receptions but finished second in targets, as Deshaun Watson completed only 16 of his 26 pass attempts. It's still a positive sign that the Browns want to get the ball in the rookie's hands despite the meager offensive output. Boston will aim to bounce back versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: Denzel Boston and the Browns welcome the 3-5 Texans to town in Week 10. He corralled six of seven targets for 98 yards during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Boston just missed the 100-yard mark but established a new career high in receiving yards, pacing his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He showed great rapport with Shedeur Sanders, who earned his first start of the season, but Deshaun Watson (concussion) is likely to return from a one-game absence to face his former team. Boston will look to build upon this effort against a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Douglas hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week healthy and help their struggling passing game in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury and was used at varying rates when healthy: seven targets in his debut followed by just three the following week. While his 94 yards in Week 1 show potential, uncertain availability and opportunity likely keep him off the radar for lineup consideration against a slightly above-average Jets' secondary that's surrendering 7.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Douglas appears to be emerging as a big-play option in the Dolphins' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. Returning from a three-game absence in Week 7, Douglas brought in two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He's only caught two balls in two of his three healthy appearances, but is averaging 20.3 yards per catch, and his large frame makes him a potential red zone candidate. If New England jumps out to an early lead, it could help Douglas' snap share, setting him up as a low-floor, high-ceiling option against a defense allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.10: Caleb Douglas appears to be the best option among Dolphins receivers entering a Week 10 matchup with the Colts. He has 14 targets over the last two weeks as Malik Washington's role shrinks, and Douglas has 70 receiving yards in two of his last three outings despite Malik Willis' struggles. Indianapolis is more vulnerable against the run, which figures to be Miami's plan offensively, especially with Kyle McCord replacing the injured Willis, but Douglas has proven he can take advantage of whatever opportunities come his way, setting him up for a deep league play against a defense that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Caleb Douglas continues to make big plays on increased chances ahead of the the Dolphins' Week 11 game against the Bills. Douglas notched eight targets for the second-straight game in Week 10, reaching 70 yards for the third time in four outings. While new quarterback Kyle McCord threw 32 passes to 11 different teammates in his debut, Douglas remained the steady top option. Buffalo allows just 7.3 yards per target, the eighth-lowest in the league, but with Miami likely to be throwing from behind often, Douglas can be a preferred option.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian McCaffrey has had a nose for the end zone this season and will look to score again when the 49ers face the Commanders in Week 6. McCaffrey produced 83 total yards and a TD this past Sunday in a big win over Seattle, giving him at least one score four straight weeks. While his 16.0 touches per game this year are considerably lower than his 24.3 last season, he's been more efficient on the ground with 4.7 yards per carry (he averaged just 3.9 YPC during the regular season in 2025). With that said, Washington has been stingy against RBs through five weeks, yielding just 3.76 YPC and only two total touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers are on the road for a meeting against the Falcons in Week 7. He rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two TDs while losing a fumble, adding nine catches on 10 targets for 53 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 victory. McCaffrey set season highs in carries, receptions, receiving yards and targets while notching his seventh rushing TD in six games. He'll once again lead the 49ers backfield for their matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 23.3 fantasy points per game (21st) to RBs and just surrendered three rushing TDs to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian McCaffrey's hamstring issue will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 matchup against the Raiders. McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain Week 7 against Atlanta, but a well-timed Week 8 bye provided an opportunity for him to get abundant rest. Should McCaffrey be unable to suit up in Week 9, however, rookie Kealon Black is likely to take on lead RB duties for the 49ers. Whichever player leads the team's backfield has a juicy matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yielded a league-worst 5.31 yards per carry to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian McCaffrey will seek to add to his seven-game scoring streak when San Francisco faces Dallas in Week 10. With two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) this past Sunday against Las Vegas, McCaffrey has gotten into the end zone at least once in each of his past seven games. While he has been logging fewer touches per game this season, McCaffrey continues to be a workhorse for the 49ers and has averaged 4.5 yards per rush, his highest mark since 2023. He could be in for a big game against the Cowboys, who are giving up 22.0 fantasy points per game to running backs, fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Christian McCaffrey enters San Francisco's Week 11 matchup against Minnesota on the heels of one of the biggest performances of his career. In this past Sunday's win over Dallas, McCaffrey recorded a career-best 161 receiving yards en route to 223 total yards and three touchdowns. The star RB has logged at least one TD in each of his past eight games and has multiple scores in three of his past four contests, making him an elite week-to-week fantasy asset. With that said, McCaffrey is slated for a tough matchup against the Vikings, who rank eighth in the NFL by allowing 15.3 fantasy points per game to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kirk Cousins lost a fourth straight start in Week 7, but for now he'll remain the Raiders' starting quarterback ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Cousins has cooled off against tougher competition, but he's still playing well and has a 7:2 TD:INT during the losing streak while averaging 304 passing yards a game. Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker remain his only reliable targets however, and Ashton Jeanty hasn't been able to force defenses to pay more attention to the team's ground game. Cousins may not need to air it out as much in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kirk Cousins is coming off arguably his best performance of 2026, completing a season-high 73.1% of his passes and tossing three touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Jets. He also ran for his first score of the year. Cousins' 19 TD passes through eight games puts him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 20, and his 2,124 passing yards puts him third behind Matthew Stafford (2,146) and Jordan Love (2,246). As long as Cousins keeps producing at a high level and the Raiders are in the playoff picture, rookie Fernando Mendoza should remain on the bench. Cousins faces a tougher test in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kirk Cousins is coming off his worst performance of the season, getting picked off three times while throwing just one touchdown in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. With Las Vegas now 4-5, the team elected to hand the reins of the offense to rookie Fernando Mendoza by trading Cousins back to the franchise he had the most success with, the Vikings. Cousins' 20 TD passes through nine games is second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 23, and he's fifth in passing yards. Given his familiarity with Kevin O'Connell's offense, he should immediately step in as the starter for Minnesota in Week 10 against a Packers defense that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kirk Cousins will take the reins again as the Vikings take on the 49ers in Week 11. Cousins shone in his Week 10 return to Minnesota, completing 68 percent of passes for 207 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT. The veteran will look to regain his form even more with his old squad this week ahead of what could be a tough matchup in Mexico City. The 49ers have ranked 14th in fantasy points allowed to QBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chase McLaughlin will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. McLaughlin impressed during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, converting on his lone field-goal try and all three point-after attempts. He remains perfect on the season, making all 20 of his kicks this season (10 field goals and 10 extra points). He could have plenty of scoring chances against a Steelers defense that's given up 9.8 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin had an impressive showing in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Buccaneers, converting on all four of his field-goal tries, including three from 40-plus yards. The veteran kicker is perfect on the season, making 14 field goals and 11 extra points. He'll likely have multiple scoring opportunities in Week 7, as the Panthers defense has allowed 7.4 kicking points per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase McLaughlin could have few scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. McLaughlin converted on all seven of his kicks in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, making two field goals and five extra points. On the season, McLaughlin has been perfect, making all 16 of his field-goal tries and all 16 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, McLaughlin could struggle against a solid Falcons defense that's allowed just 6.4 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He made all three of his field goal attempts despite the heavy rain in the Week 8 win over the Falcons. On the season, he's converted all 19 of his field goal tries and all 17 of his point-after attempts. Despite his incredible season, McLaughlin is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that's allowed just 5.0 kicking points per game through seven weeks this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chase McLaughlin could have limited scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 11 matchup against the Lions. McLaughlin has been one of fantasy's top kickers through nine games this season, converting on all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 18 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, he could have few scoring chances in Week 11 against a Detroit defense that's given up just 5.3 kicking points per game on the season.

outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Herbert will likely operate as Atlanta's No. 2 running back if Brian Robinson (hamstring) remains sidelined for the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. While backing up Bijan Robinson in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, Herbert was productive, accumulating 28 yards on just three touches. Due to his lack of opportunities, Herbert will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to RBs all season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Khalil Herbert will serve as Atlanta's top backup running back if Brian Robinson (hamstring) remains sidelined for the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Herbert has stepped into the No. 2 RB role in Robinson's absence over the last two weeks, totaling 43 yards on eight touches. With Herbert playing behind one of the NFL's premier backs in Bijan Robinson, it's unlikely that he'll be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. This could be tough against a Cincinnati defense that's given up just five touchdowns to RBs in seven games this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Khalil Herbert is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Herbert has operated as Bijan Robinson's top backup in each of the last three weeks, but his increased offensive role has not led to much production. Through three contests, Herbert has tallied 28 rushing yards on seven carries and 24 receiving yards on four receptions. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs defense that's allowed just five total touchdowns to running backs this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards last game for the Eagles. Goedert was second on the team in targets behind DeVonta Smith. Even with Tanner McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Goedert should still have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dallas Goedert finished second on the Eagles last game in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Goedert caught five passes on seven looks for 48 yards in the 38-21 loss to the Cowboys. Goedert has at least seven targets in three-straight outings. If DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Goedert should remain a focal point of the passing attack, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dallas Goedert has caught at least four passes in four-straight games for the Eagles. He has amassed 28 targets over that span. Unfortunately, Goedert is averaging less than 45 yards receiving per contest during that time period. He has also been held out of the end zone. With backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Goedert's prospects may not be getting any better. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a Giants defense allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which us third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dallas Goedert collected five catches last game for Philadelphia, and continues to operate as a steady safety valve no matter who lines up under center. Goedert has at least four catches in all but one game played in 2026. In Week 11, Goedert will have a tasty matchup against a surprisingly porous Pittsburgh pass defense. The Steelers are surrendering 242.2 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeVonta Smith returned to the Eagles lineup with a bang. Smith snagged seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown following a two-game absence from a hamstring issue. Even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Smith was targeted a staggering 14 times. As a result, even with McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Smith should have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: DeVonta Smith missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky hamstring. Smith has played in just four contests in 2026 in what has been a lost season overall for 2-6 Philadelphia. If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: DeVonta Smith could return from a hamstring issue for the Eagles following their bye. Smith has missed five of the last six games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of Dontayvion Wicks, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Gibbs hit the century mark on the ground for the third time this season in Week 7 versus Green Bay, rushing the ball 29 times for 116 yards and adding five catches for 27 yards. The superstar unfortunately was held to zero touchdowns for the first time this season, with nine to his name across the first five games. He'll change focus now to a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to stay hot as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Gibbs recorded another monster performance on the ground in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, rushing the ball 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for 15 yards as well. The superstar has now surpassed 100 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's found the end zone in all but one outing this season. He'll take on a Dolphins defense that's ranked a favorable 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jahmyr Gibbs will seek to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Gibbs punched in another rushing score alongside 74 yards on the ground in Week 9 against the Dolphins, but he was unable to record a catch for the first time this season. The star ball carrier has now recorded 20 or more carries in each of his last four outings, but he's seen his receiving work decline each week in that stretch. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep up his dominance as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Gibbs had another monster performance in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, totaling 252 yards off 29 touches and tacking on two rushing touchdowns. The superstar has now amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine showings. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malik Nabers saw a staggering 20 targets last game for the Giants. Nabers parlayed those ample opportunities into 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. It was the second-straight 100-yard outing for Nabers, who also scored for the second-consecutive contest. His newfound connection with starting quarterback Jameis Winston has been evident. In Week 6, the G-Men face a New Orleans defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Saints are allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Nabers continues his torrid stretch for the Giants. Nabers snagged 12 passes for 165 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Regardless of who has lined up under center for the Giants, Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in three-straight contests. He has racked up a staggering 35 targets in his last two outings alone. In Week 7, Nabers has another favorable matchup against a leaky Texans secondary. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in four-straight contests for the Giants. Nabers has racked up a staggering 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. He has drawn an insane 51 targets during that time period, an average of nearly 13 opportunities per clash. In Week 9, the G-Men will face a scuffling Eagles squad. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Nabers had a four-game 100-yard receiving streak snapped last game for the Giants. Nabers had five catches for 43 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He was targeted eight times. He will look to rebound in Week 10 against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Nabers had a costly fumble last game for the Giants. Nabers had the ball punched out of his hands in scoring territory versus the Commanders, who ultimately defeated the G-Men by a score of 24-21. Nabers has now been held under 50 yards receiving in each of the last two outings following a dazzling four-game stretch of 100-yard outbursts. In Week 11, he will look to rebound against a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.6: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North showdown in Week 7. He missed a second consecutive game in Week 6, a 13-10 loss to Cleveland, due to an ankle injury sustained in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Jackson could potentially get back on the practice field during Week 7 prep, but Baltimore is still considering their star quarterback day-to-day. If he's unable to suit up for the third straight contest, Tyler Huntley will continue to start under center versus Cincinnati's 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.5) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. After missing the last three contests with an ankle injury, he appears to be headed in the right direction, as head coach Jesse Minter stated Jackson is "in a decent spot" to return to action against Buffalo. His practice participation bears monitoring following his limited activity prior to Baltimore's Week 7 loss. If active, Jackson will aim to snap a two-game losing streak versus a Bills defense allowing 26.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Ferguson had a two-game scoring streak snapped for the Cowboys. Ferguson managed three catches for just 11 yards in the 34-30 win over the Texans. Ferguson has just 12 catches for 83 yards through the first four games of the season, though has scored three times over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Ferguson saw a season-high six targets last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which likely contributed to the additional looks for other players, including Ferguson. However, Ferguson managed three catches for just 19 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Ferguson back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Ferguson continues to struggle to find his place in the Dallas offense. Ferguson managed just two catches for 13 yards in the dismal 23-13 loss to the Packers. Ferguson has been held out of the end zone in three-straight games, and has failed to gain even 20 yards receiving in any of those contests. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Ferguson was held without a catch last game for Dallas. Ferguson's decline has been steep this season. He has failed to find the end zone in four-straight games, and has not even gained 20 yards in any contest over that span. He will look to get back on track in Week 8 with an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Ferguson left the last game for Dallas due to an ankle injury. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus Indianapolis. Ferguson has failed to register a single catch in each of the last two contests. Brevyn Spann-Ford could see additional looks if Ferguson is sidelined. Spann-Ford snagged five passes for 31 yards following Ferguson's departure. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Wilson has settled in atop Arizona's WR depth chart heading into a Week 5 tilt against the Lions. Wilson caught seven passes on 13 targets for 95 yards against the Giants in Week 4, leading or co-leading the Cardinals in all three categories. He's drawn a whopping 30 targets over his past two contests, making it clear that QB Jacoby Brissett sees him as the top option among the team's wideouts. Wilson could be in store for a big game against a Detroit defense that has yielded 28.3 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Wilson is set to lead Arizona's wideout corps versus the Rams in Week 6. After Marvin Harrison was made inactive this past Sunday due to a pending trade, Wilson functioned as the no-doubt No. 1 WR for the Cardinals but managed just four catches for 30 yards against Detroit. He was outproduced by fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne, who posted a 5-70-0 line, but Wilson should have plenty of chances to thrive with Harrison officially off to Houston. The Rams have given up the fewest receiving yards per game to wideouts this season, but they've also surrendered seven receiving TDs to the position, tied for third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Wilson has emerged as Arizona's leading wide receiver following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure, recording 33 receptions for 320 yards and a touchdown through six games. Wilson has averaged 9.7 yards per reception, and his established role as the team's new WR1 should keep him among Jacoby Brissett's preferred targets alongside star tight end Trey McBride. However, the Cardinals' passing attack has struggled to generate explosive plays, limiting Wilson's weekly ceiling. To make things even more complicated, the Week 7 matchup against the Broncos is far from easy, as Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts in 2026. That, coupled with Brissett's inconsistent play under center, limits Wilson's fantasy appeal considerably in most formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Michael Wilson will look to get back his early-season mojo with a juicy matchup when Arizona faces the Cowboys in Week 8. After hauling in 18 passes on 30 targets for 184  yards across Weeks 3 and 4, Wilson has compiled just 12 receptions on 22 targets for 117 yards over his past three games. The downturn has some in spite of the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison to make Wilson the team's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver, though tight end Trey McBride has continued to feature as QB Jacoby Brissett's top target. Harrison will have a chance to put up big numbers versus a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in the NFL with 23.9 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.9: Michael Wilson could play in Arizona's Week 9 matchup against Seattle despite dealing with two broken ribs. The wideout suffered the injury this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, but he returned to the game after getting hurt and finished with eight catches for 111 yards and one touchdown on 15 targets. Wilson thrived with both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew under center, so the switch to Minshew as the Cardinals' starting QB shouldn't impact Wilson's production if he's able to suit up in Week 9. However, the ribs issue plus a stout Seattle pass defense that has given up the fewest fantasy points per game this season (14.3) to wideouts could hurt Wilson's production.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 divisional clash. He had 18 carries for 101 yards and corralled three of four targets for 36 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory in Paris. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle amassed 86 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, and it appears he's rounding into form after missing nearly a month with a toe injury. Warren remains atop the backfield hierarchy, but he'll face a tough test against Cleveland's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers visit their divisional-rival Bengals on Sunday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown while catching one of two targets for no gain during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 9. Warren matched his career high for rushing yards and produced his third 100-plus-yard effort in his last four games.
