In Week 3, he generated 176 scrimmage yards on 20 touches in his first matchup against Cincinnati, so he'll be hungry to put up similar numbers on the road.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Eagles in Week 11. He had seven carries for 15 yards and caught five of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Warren and the entire Steelers offense found little success until the game was already out of reach, as several backups took the field in the fourth quarter. Warren will look to shake off the tough outing, but he'll have to do so against Philadelphia's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Isaiah Likely had a surprisingly poor game for the Giants his last time on the field. Likely managed just two catches for 12 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Likely had managed double-digit targets in each of the previous three games for the G-Men, so the lack of looks was eye-opening. Still, new quarterback J.J. McCarthy was working under center and targeted star wideout Malik Nabers with reckless abandon. Likely should see more work in Week 9 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 235.4 passing yards per contest, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaiah Likely found the end zone again for the Giants last game. Likely snagged five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in the 19-11 win over Philadelphia. Likely now has scored four touchdowns in his last four contests. He is a great bet to find the end zone again versus a suspect Washington pass defense. Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season, which is tied for 25th in the league.  In addition, the Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaiah Likely notched a career-high 127 yards receiving last game for the Giants. Likely reeled in nine passes, one of which went for a 66-yard touchdown, though the G-Men fell to Washington by a score of 24-21. Still, Likely has scored in back-to-back contests, and has five scores in his last five outings.  In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacoby Brissett will aim to clean up his mistakes when Arizona hosts Detroit in Week 5. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants in Week 4 after getting picked off just once through his first three games of the season. The veteran quarterback has still been pretty productive with 818 passing yards, six touchdowns and 43 rushing yards (with one touchdown) overall this season. He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his first three-TD performance of the campaign heading into Arizona's Week 6 clash against the Rams. Two of Brissett's scores in this past Sunday's blowout loss to Detroit came after the outcome was already decided, but they count the same in the world of fantasy football. The veteran quarterbacks also threw for a season-high 292 yards and rushed for a season-best 19 yards, though he did throw his fifth interception of the campaign. Brissett could find the sledding tougher against the Rams, who have given up just 5.65 yards per attempt this season, second-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jacoby Brissett will look to build on Arizona's Week 6 victory over the Rams when the Cardinals host the Broncos in Week 7. The veteran quarterback has completed 156 of 234 passes for 1,328 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions through six games, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest. However, his 5.7 yards per attempt are the best example of the struggles Arizona's offense endures to generate explosive passing plays, and Denver represents another challenging opponent. The Broncos have allowed just 14.9 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the 12th-best mark in the NFL, limiting Brissett's appeal despite his established passing volume. He's best viewed as a lower-end QB2 in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jacoby Brissett will look to guide Arizona to more scoring in Week 8 versus Dallas. Though Brissett has thrown for a combined 490 yards over his past two games, he's tossed just one touchdown during that span. The veteran QB has taken to the air a league-high 282 times this season, so his fantasy managers have at least been able to count on consistent volume. Brissett could put up big numbers versus a Cowboys defense that ranks in the the bottom 10 of the league in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens host the Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. After being acquired via trade from the Cardinals, Brissett is expected to earn his first start for Baltimore. In eight outings with Arizona, he completed 193 of 305 pass attempts (63.3%) for 1,719 yards with a 10:7 TD:INT ratio, to go along with 29 carries for 87 yards and one score. The Ravens desperately need Brissett's veteran presence under center with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both on IR. Baltimore has scored exactly 10 points in three of their last four games, with their best mark being 13 points in a loss to the Bengals in Week 7. Brissett will get a favorable matchup versus a Chargers defense allowing 27.4 points per contest, tied for the fourth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens travel to face the Panthers in an interconference matchup. He completed 33 of 49 pass attempts for 340 yards with no TDs and one INT while rushing twice for two yards during his Baltimore debut in Week 10. Brissett connected with seven different receivers and led the Ravens to a final score above 13 points for the first time since Week 5. However, the team did lose its fifth game in a row, so Brissett will look to get into the win column versus a Carolina defense allowing 19.9 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.
outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Khalil Shakir continues to provide stability in Buffalo's passing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Shakir has recorded at least six targets in five of seven outings, going for 50 or more yards four times. It's a modest floor with only one touchdown catch, and it's even lower facing a Minnesota defense that's allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, including just four touchdowns in seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Khalil Shakir remains an efficient secondary option in the Bills' passing game ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. He caught four passes in Week 9, the fifth time in eight outings he's done so, resulting in 50 or more yards at the same rate. Shakir has only one touchdown, and the Jets' secondary has allowed just nine touchdown catches by receivers, likely limiting Shakir's potential in Week 10, but his role and usage are clear and steady, setting him up for stability as a potential streamer.
outlooksByWeek.11: Khalil Shakir is in search of a bounce-back outing in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. He logged only three targets in Week 10, the second time this season he's had such low volume, and now has four games with 38 yards or fewer in nine outings. Buffalo threw only 21 times against the Jets, and if they jump to a big lead again against Miami, a similar game flow could emerge, potentially giving Shakir too few opportunities to better a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Bass has been busy for the Bills ahead of a difficult Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. He has multiple field goals in four straight weeks, 12 in total. Bass has added upside to his stable floor in Buffalo's high-scoring offense, which has yielded 21 extra points in seven games. Minnesota has allowed only six field goals and 11 made PATs all season, putting Bass' hot streak in jeopardy.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Bass continues to see heavy volume in the Bills' prolific offense ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Seemingly always assured of a handful of PATs, making at least two in every game, Bass has at least three field goals in four straight games, creating double-digit scoring upside with consistency. The Jets are allowing the ninth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing kickers however, largely due to opponents converting drives into touchdowns, surrendering just 13 field goal attempts in nine games, which should test Bass' current form.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Bass faces unsettled scoring chances when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 11. After attempting multiple field goals in five straight games, Bass tried just one in Week 10 with Buffalo coasting to a win and converting drives into touchdowns. That script seems likely to manifest again in Week 11 against an overmatched Miami defense, so while Bass will have a multi-PAT floor, his ceiling could be capped.

outlooksByWeek.7: J.J. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt by the Giants last game. Though McCarthy's efforts fell short, he threw for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of starter Jameis Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: J.J. McCarthy comes off the bye as the starting quarterback of the first-place Giants as they head into a divisional matchup in Week 9 versus bumbling Philadelphia. The Eagles have lost six-straight contests. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL. Meanwhile, McCarthy has thrown for at least 243 yards in each of the last two games for the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.10: J.J. McCarthy is battling a hip pointer, but should be able to suit up in Week 10 for the Giants versus the Commanders. McCarthy briefly left New York's last contest versus the Eagles due to the issue, but was able to return and ultimately guide the G-Men to victory. Though McCarthy passed for a season-low 127 yards last game, he will look to rebound against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: J.J. McCarthy has thrown for at least 240 yards in three of the last four games for the Giants. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown and one interception last game versus the Commanders. The interception also came on a last-minute heave as the Giants attempted a comeback. In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Xavier Hutchinson is likely to continue sliding down the depth chart at wide receiver as Marvin Harrison and Tank Dell get acclimated in Houston. The Texans traded for Harrison prior to Week 6 and activated Dell from injured reserve prior to Week 7. Hutchinson has just 27 receiving yards in two games since Harrison's arrival, though Hutchinson scored his first TD of the season in Week 7 against the Giants, marking just his fourth TD in 56 regular-season appearances for the Texans. Following a Week 8 bye, the Texans take on the winless Chargers in Week 9. Hutchinson isn't a recommended fantasy option against a Chargers defense that has been more stout against the pass than the run.
outlooksByWeek.10: Xavier Hutchinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 10 road game against the Browns, but he has just 46 receiving yards over that span and is averaging a meager 36 receiving yards per game this season. He has maintained a prominent role in a high-ceiling Houston passing offense, drawing at least five targets in all but one game, but Hutchinson hasn't done much with those opportunities and had just three career TDs in 3.5 seasons prior to his current two-game scoring streak. Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison, and Kayshon Boutte all have higher upside among Houston's WRs for Week 10 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.11: Xavier Hutchinson has scored in three consecutive games heading into Houston's Week 11 home game against the Colts. He's averaging six targets per game, and while his paltry average of 6.4 yards per target suggests C.J. Stroud would be better off distributing those looks elsewhere, Hutchinson's volume has propelled the 26-year-old wideout into the weekly flex conversation. Perhaps Hutchinson is just a late bloomer who is finding his groove, but it's fair to remain skeptical considering his three TDs in the last three games match his total of three TDs from 55 regular-season appearances before this streak. The Colts have limited WRs to eight TDs in 10 games, though Indianapolis is allowing 149 yards per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Young has performed very well to start the season, leading the NFL in passing yards per game (317) while accounting for 10 total touchdowns. In his most recent performance, a Week 4 win over the Lions, Young threw for a whopping 329 yards and two touchdowns. He's expected to remain one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while facing an Eagles defense that's allowed 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bryce Young is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Through five games this season, Young has thrown for 1,549 yards and accounted for 12 touchdowns with just two interceptions, leading the league with 309.8 passing yards per game. He's emerged as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while leading the Panthers' offense to 29.2 points per game, the fourth-best mark in the NFL. Expect Young to remain productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Young underwhelmed for the first time all season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, completing 14 of 27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Despite this, Young has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for an average of 285.3 yards and 2.0 touchdowns per game. He'll look to rebound in Week 8 against a strong Packers defense that's given up just 17.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance in the Panthers' Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Young has really struggled over Carolina's last two contests, completing just 37 of 68 pass attempts for 372 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. Young has been playing through a knee injury since the Week 3 loss to the Browns, which could be hindering his performance. However, he could bounce back in Week 9, as Denver's defense has given up 20.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading the Panthers' offense during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Young played well despite a loss in Week 9 against the Broncos, throwing for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He remains tied for the league-lead in passing attempts per game (38.5) and fourth in passing yards per game (274.6). which are both positive signs for his outlook going forward. Additionally, Young is in for a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 21.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading the Panthers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Young had a relatively underwhelming performance in the Week 10 win over the Saints, completing 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception. Despite this outing, Young ranks sixth in the NFL in pass attempts (37.6) and yards (266.3) per game, suggesting a positive fantasy outlook moving forward. However, Young could struggle against a solid Ravens defense that's given up just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through nine games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown won't suit up for at least four weeks for the Patriots, beginning in Week 2 against the Steelers, after landing on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins figure to be New England's top three wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: A.J. Brown will continue shaking off some rust when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle injury, Brown amassed 10 targets in Week 6 but finished with just three catches for 27 yards while struggling with drops. With New England's passing game operating at a high level, featuring 10 touchdown passes in three weeks, Brown should have ample opportunity for a breakout performance against a Chicago secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.8: A.J. Brown will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown has caught three passes in each of his three outings for his new squad, failing to score or top 48 receiving yards. While Miami has surrendered 14 touchdown passes overall, only three have gone to wide receivers, resulting in the second-fewest fantasy points allowed despite an appealing 8.8 yards per target. Brown may still be a week away from a breakout in his new uniform.
outlooksByWeek.9: A.J. Brown's availability for the Patriots' Week 9 game against the Packers is uncertain due to lingering knee and ankle injuries. Brown was a late-week addition to the injury report with a knee issue that has seemingly persisted since last season, in addition to an ankle problem that previously cost him four games. When healthy, Brown has been targeted regularly but has struggled with drops, posting a season-high 48 yards in Week 7. Should he play, he'll face a Packers defense that has allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers but has been vulnerable to their opposition's top option, allowing 70 or more yards six times.
outlooksByWeek.10: A.J. Brown will look to return from a two-week absence when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Limited to just three games thus far, Brown amassed 16 targets in his last two outings and figures to again draw heavy volume if healthy. In a game where the Patriots could be down their top two running backs, a pass-heavy shootout appears possible, setting Brown up for a big game against a Lions secondary that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Skattebo had zero touches last game for the Giants. One week after losing a key fumble, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown, but managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. Houston is also allowing just 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Skattebo retained his starring role for the Giants last game, gaining 121 scrimmage yards and scoring a touchdown in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Tyrone Tracy went on Injured Reserve following the victory, leaving Devin Singletary as the only other legitimate option at running back behind Skattebo. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Skattebo did not suit up in New York's last game due to a hamstring issue. However, Skattebo pushed to play in the contest, and as a result looks primed to return to the starting lineup in Week 10 versus the Commanders. Washington has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026, though, allowing just 102.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the league. In addition, the Commanders have yielded just seven rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Skattebo scored twice last game for the Giants. He also gained over 120 scrimmage yards for the second-straight contest. Following being benched versus the Saints, Skattebo has responded with 39 touches in the subsequent two tilts, though he did miss the win over Philadelphia due to a hamstring ailment. He will have his work cut out for him in Week 11 versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zay Flowers and the Ravens return home for a divisional showdown against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught six of 11 targets for 66 yards and had one carry for one yard during Baltimore's Week 6 loss. Flowers led Baltimore in receptions, yardage, and targets, with no other player earning more than five looks from Tyler Huntley. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question for a third consecutive week, Huntley is in line for his second start under center. Regardless of who is at QB, Flowers will continue operating as the clear-cut No. 1 option in the passing game versus Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (29.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to halt a two-game losing skid when they visit the Bills in Week 8. He caught eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Flowers led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, recording the Ravens' only touchdown in the loss. There's a good chance Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return from a three-game absence in Week 8, but Flowers has proven to be a fantasy stud this season no matter who's under center. He'll face a Buffalo defense that surrenders 42.3 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zay Flowers and the Ravens host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He was held without a catch on five targets during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 loss. With Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both leaving the game with injuries, Flowers struggled mightily to get anything going. The Ravens could be forced to start Joe Fagnano (knee) against the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs, but the uncertainty at the QB position greatly lowers Flowers' fantasy appeal.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are at home to take on the Chargers in Week 10. He brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for another 17 yards during Baltimore's defeat in Week 9. Flowers and his fantasy managers are hoping the acquisition of Jacoby Brissett will provide a boost for the Ravens' passing game, as the former Cardinal will get his first Ravens start on Monday Night Football. Flowers does have a favorable matchup against a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the Panthers in Week 11. He corralled six of seven targets for 74 yards but lost a key fumble during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. Flowers turned it over with 2:11 remaining, ultimately ending his team's chance to tie or take the lead. On a brighter note, Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, meaning Flowers should have no shortage of opportunities to make up for the costly mistake versus Carolina's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (31.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Blake Corum's role as a ball carrier seems to fading ahead of the Rams' Week 6 game versus Arizona. Corum rushed just five times for 19 yards Monday against Buffalo, marking his third straight contest with six or fewer carries after averaging 11 totes across the first two weeks. However, Corum did score his first TD of 2026 and had easily his best game this season as a receiver against the Bills, catching three passes for 53 yards. Given his recent downturn in carries, Corum may need to get into the end zone to come away with serviceable fantasy production, but the Cardinals have given up only four total TDs to running backs through five weeks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Blake Corum has developed into a legitimate complementary option in the Rams' backfield to star tailback Kyren Williams, rushing 47 times for 223 yards and a touchdown while adding nine receptions for 91 yards and another score through six games. His 4.7 yards per carry almost equals Williams' 4.9 mark, but the main difference is the touches, as Corum is averaging just 7.8 carries per game compared to Williams' 13.3. Still, Corum faces an encouraging Week 7 matchup against the Raiders, who have surrendered 19.6 fantasy points per game to RBs in 2026, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL.His limited receiving involvement and secondary role make him a touchdown-dependent flex option rather than a dependable weekly starter.
outlooksByWeek.8: Blake Corum is coming off his biggest workload of the campaign with the Rams' Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers on tap. After entering Sunday with fewer than 10 carries in four straight contests, Corum rumbled for 93 yards and a touchdown on a season-high 17 totes against the Raiders. Backfield mate Kyren Williams equaled Corum with 18 touches and figures to continue to lead the team's backfield, but Corum certainly reminded fantasy managers that he's worth consideration even in the No. 2 RB role. Both Corum and Williams could find room to run against a Chargers defense that ranks 21st in the league with 4.19 yards per carry allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Blake Corum should continue to have a big role in the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against the Commanders. Corum logged five fewer carries than backfield make Kyren Williams this past Sunday versus the Chargers, but Corum led the team with 73 rushing yards and also scored a touchdown for the fourth straight contest. After taking fewer than 10 totes four straight weeks, Corum has averaged 14 carries across his past two contests and seems to have regained his role as Los Angeles' 1B option next to Williams' 1A role. Washington has been pretty tough on running backs so far this season, tying for 10th in the league with 15.5 fantasy points allowed per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Blake Corum continues to get a hefty share of work out of the Rams' backfield heading into a Week 10 visit to Arizona. Corum led Los Angeles with 58 rushing yards and scored a touchdown on 11 carries in a Week 9 win against Washington. Though he remains marginally behind Kyren Williams in the Rams' backfield, Corum has logged double-digit carries in three straight games and has scored in each of those contests. There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deebo Samuel and the 49ers travel to face the Falcons in Week 7. The veteran receiver missed San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6 with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5. Head coach Kyle Shanahan stated they would "hold off" on placing him on injured reserve with the Week 8 bye approaching, so it sounds like Samuel is in jeopardy of missing the road tilt against Atlanta. Expect him to work towards a Week 9 return, as long as he doesn't suffer any sort of setback.
outlooksByWeek.9: Deebo Samuel has a chance to return from a two-game absence for San Francisco's Week 9 tilt against Las Vegas. Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against Seattle and hasn't played since, but the 49ers' Week 8 bye allowed him time for extra rest. Mike Evans (Achilles) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) also have a chance to return to San Francisco's wideout corps following absences of their own, so the team's passing game could be getting a big boost. The outlook is positive for all of the 49ers' wide receivers given that the Raiders have allowed 10 receiving touchdowns to the position this year, tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will look to return from a four-game absence when San Francisco travels to Dallas in Week 10. Samuel hasn't been placed on IR, and the expectation is that he'll return before the end of the season, but his status for this week is hazy, at best. With No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (Achilles) missing the past two games, the 49ers acquired Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to provide additional depth. If Samuel is able to get back on the field against the Cowboys, he could find success against a defense that has given up 159.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ninth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Deebo Samuel will look to build on his best performance of the season when the 49ers  host the Vikings in Week 11. Samuel compiled 109 total yards and two touchdowns this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, with most of that yardage coming on a 70-yard rushing score. It was Samuel's first game if five weeks, as he had been sidelined due to a hamstring injury. His versatility could come in handy against a Vikings defense that is tied for the third-fewest receiving TDs (five) allowed to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jameson Williams will look to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Williams kept his touchdown streak and recent dominance alive in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, reeling in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown. The speedy wideout has now logged 11 catches for 208 yards and a whopping five touchdowns in his last three outings. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jameson Williams will look to get more volume as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Williams struggled to get touches with a stagnant passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9, recording one catch for 31 yards and one rush for nine yards. The speedy wideout has now posted a 28-468-5 receiving line on 44 targets across eight games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jameson Williams will remain a flashy option in Detroit's offense heading into Week 11 against the Buccaneers. Williams didn't benefit, like some of his teammates, from an offensive explosion in a Week 10 win over New England, but he still hauled in four of seven targets for 50 yards. The speedy wideout has now logged 32 catches for 518 yards and five touchdowns so far this season. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen will look to build on a solid opener when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Braelon Allen could be slated for bulk carries in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns with Breece Hall's (quad) uncertain availability. Filling in for Hall in Week 4, Allen was the only Jet to receive a carry, putting him in line to potentially exploit a Cleveland defense that's allowed at least 82 yards to opposing lead backs in three straight weeks and an appealing 4.8 yards per carry. If Hall returns, he can't be guaranteed a full workload, lending flex appeal to Allen.
outlooksByWeek.6: Braelon Allen's role for the Jets in Week 6 against the Patriots is in flux due to uncertainty surrounding Breece Hall (quad). Allen has dominated carries in two games with Hall out, breaking out in Week 5 with a 24-carry, 116-yard performance. New England hasn't allowed an opposing back to gain over 75 yards, and Allen hasn't been a factor in the Jets' passing game. If Hall does not return, volume will be Allen's best asset.
outlooksByWeek.7: Braelon Allen will hope to again receive the bulk of the opportunities out of the Jets' backfield in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Allen has been a workhorse over the last three weeks with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined, averaging 18.3 carries. Allen's lack of involvement in the passing game could cap his upside against a defense that's allowed five touchdown receptions to opposing running backs but only three rushing scores. Volume remains paramount to a running back's success, and Allen should have that even if Hall is back, as a full workload after three weeks wouldn't seem likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Braelon Allen's workload is unclear heading into the Jets' Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. He has shined over the last four games with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined, topping 100 total yards three times, but would likely be in a timeshare if Hall can return in Week 8. Both backs can still offer sound production as the matchup is one of the most favorable available. Las Vegas is surrendering 5.2 yards per carry and the second-most fantasy points per game, last week allowing two 90-plus yard rushers to the Rams.
outlooksByWeek.9: Braelon Allen's successful five-week run as the Jets' lead back appears set to end in Week 9 against the Chiefs with the pending return of Breece Hall (quad). Allen had at least 16 touches in every outing with Hall sidelined, capping it off with a career-high 147 yards in Week 8. While he's earned a role in the team's backfield, his workload share is unclear. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry further limits Allen's potential production.
outlooksByWeek.10: Braelon Allen has reverted to a secondary option for the Jets with Breece Hall healthy ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Bills. Allen recorded just 10 touches in Hall's return in Week 9 after 19 or more opportunities over the last five weeks. With Hall a preferred option in the passing game and facing a defense that allows just 3.8 yards per carry, Allen is unlikely to collect enough usage to be in the Week 10 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.11: Braelon Allen remains second fiddle to Breece Hall ahead of the Jets' Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. In two games since Hall's return, Allen has 16 carries compared to Hall's 26. Hall has also caught seven passes to Allen's three. Despite being more efficient than Hall, Allen's role appears clear in a matchup against a defense that's allowing a modest 4.0 yards per carry, likely rendering Allen to flex territory.

player.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins.
