Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: T.J. Hockenson remains a top option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 8 against the Lions. Hockenson found the end zone for the second time of the season in a Week 7 win over the Colts, and he complemented his score with four catches for 35 yards. The veteran tight end has now brought in 27 catches for 237 yards and two touchdowns this season. He enters a favorable matchup versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 32nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: T.J. Hockenson will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Hockenson was a key piece in Minnesota's passing game once again in a Week 8 loss to Detroit, reeling in four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The veteran has now registered five targets in back-to-back games, and he's found the end zone in each as well. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: T.J. Hockenson should remain a top option in Minnesota's passing game versus the Packers in Week 10. Hockenson led the Vikings in catches in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, which was a quiet four grabs for 33 yards. The veteran tight end has now reeled in four receptions in each of the last three weeks. The addition of Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline to be the new starting QB may not be good news for Hockenson, however, as he's more likely to targets wideouts Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz did. Hockenson will face a Green Bay defense that he posted a 4-36-1 receiving line against in Week 1, and which ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: T.J. Hockenson will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Hockenson missed his first game of the year in Week 10 against the Packers due to a wrist and chest injury. The veteran was unable to participate in practice prior to the matchup, so he'll likely need to get out there if he hopes to play in Mexico City. San Francisco has ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake London will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance when the Falcons plays the Bengals in Week 9. London struggled along with the rest of Atlanta's offense in a rainy loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of six targets for eight yards. However, he's still been one of the NFL's most productive receivers with Michael Penix at quarterback this year, averaging 5.5 receptions and 90.7 receiving yards per game. London will have a good opportunity to rebound against a Cincinnati secondary that's allowed 33.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. Additionally, London is in for a difficult Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs secondary that's allowed just 23.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: C.J. Stroud posted an 11:1 TD:INT ratio in seven games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye, but the Texans are just 2-5 heading into a Week 9 road game against the 0-7 Chargers. Pass defense hasn't been the Chargers' problem, as they're allowing the seventh-fewest yards per game through the air and have limited QBs to an 8:6 TD:INT ratio. Stroud has often been asked to carry Houston's offense with the team's two main RBs both averaging no more than 3.5 yards per rushing attempt, but the Texans may rely more on their defense and running game in Week 9 to exploit the Chargers' weaknesses. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in deeper formats, but he has a low Week 9 floor based on the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.10: C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD masterpiece in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers and has thrown 10 touchdown passes over the past three games. He has showcased an elite ceiling with four games north of 300 passing yards this season, so the surging Stroud is a start-worthy Week 10 option, even in a road game against a Browns defense that ranks among the 10 stingiest units against the pass. The Ohio State product is no stranger to playing in the Buckeye State this time of year, though it's worth noting that the Browns are 3-0 at home while allowing just 17.3 points per game at Huntington Bank Field compared to 24.0 points per game in six games elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.11: C.J. Stroud tossed three more touchdown passes in Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns, bringing his TD:INT ratio to 19:3 through nine games, with 13 of those scores coming in his last four outings. The fourth-year QB's brilliance has largely been wasted on the 3-6 Texans, as the defense and running game have both declined from last season. Houston's playoff hopes aren't extinguished yet, but Stroud can't afford a Week 11 letdown in a home rematch against a Colts defense that held him to 167 yards and one TD in Week 3, when the Texans lost 19-17 at Indianapolis. The 3-7 Colts have allowed a 16:2 TD:INT ratio, so Stroud is worth starting in this Week 11 rematch Thursday despite his poor performance in the first meeting between these AFC South rivals.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Courtland Sutton was nearly invisible in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, catching only one of six targets for a measly four yards. The veteran wideout remains firmly behind Jaylen Waddle on the depth chart, but the entire Denver offense is struggling under first-time play caller Davis Webb, and Sutton has produced a weak 9-86-0 line on 22 targets through four games. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming play-calling duties is an open question. Sutton will try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Courtland Sutton ended his touchdown drought in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, catching two of three targets for 18 yards and his first score of the season. The team's entire offense has been sluggish to begin the year, and having Sean Payton take over play-calling duties didn't pay immediate dividends, but it should bode well for Sutton in the long run. He'll face another tough challenge in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Courtland Sutton's struggles continued in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran wideout has yet to catch more than three passes in a game this season or reach 50 receiving yards, leaving him with a paltry 13-123-1 line on 28 targets through six games. With quarterback Bo Nix unable to build any momentum, Sutton and the entire passing game offer little upside. He could at least get into the end zone again in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to WRs this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Courtland Sutton had another quiet day in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, managing to catch three of five targets for 45 yards. The veteran wideout has been held under 50 receiving yards and three catches or fewer in all seven games so far this season, and he's scored just one TD after hauling in 25 over the prior three years. Sutton isn't likely to break out in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Courtland Sutton set new season highs in catches and receiving yards during the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but he still came away with just a 4-53-0 line on four targets. The struggles of quarterback Bo Nix, as well as the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, have reduced Sutton's target volume considerably from 2025, and he's on pace for only 79 targets this season after topping 120 in each of the prior two years. He'll try to make do with new role in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Courtland Sutton caught a season-high five passes in the Broncos' last game before their Week 10 bye, turning one of the receptions into his second touchdown of the season. The veteran wide receiver's target volume increased after Jaylen Waddle left the contest early due to a concussion. He has yet to reach 50 receiving yards or see double-digit targets in any game this year as the No. 2 option in a sluggish passing game. Sutton will attempt to contribute in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz's opportunities were minimal in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, converting his only extra point and his sole field-goal attempt from 31 yards. The veteran kicker had been productive in his first three years with Denver, averaging just under 30 FGs and 38 extra points per season while going 12-for-18 on field-goal attempts of 50-plus yards. In Week 2, Lutz will take on a Jaguars team that ranked eighth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wil Lutz missed his first kick of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, hitting the left upright on a 43-yard field goal attempt but connecting on both his extra points. Game flow cost him opportunities, as Denver headed into halftime down 16-0 and attempted two-point conversions multiple times as part of their comeback. Lutz has converted three FGs and five extra points through three games, and his volume may not improve substantially until his offense develops some consistency. He'll take on a 49ers team in Week 4 that's allowed just 16.7 points a game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wil Lutz continues to get little volume thanks to the struggles of the Broncos' offense. Through four games, the veteran kicker has attempted only five extra points, converting all, while going just 5-for-7 on FG attempts, with one of his misses coming from 58 yards out. Lutz is reliable, especially with most of his games coming either at altitude or indoors, but without more opportunities, he won't be able to make much of a contribution. He could get more chances in Week 5 against a Chargers team that has allowed 26.5 points per game, 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wil Lutz has missed field goal attempts in the Broncos' last two games, but he's also benefited from increased volume, going 5-for-7 on FGs and 2-for-2 on PATs. The veteran kicker has had his production dragged down by the struggles of the offense, but with Sean Payton calling plays again, Lutz's outlook has brightened a little. He'll face a Seahawks team in Week 6 that's allowed 21.0 points per game this season, eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wil Lutz played hero for the Broncos in Week 6, with his only field goal coming in overtime during a win over the Seahawks. The veteran kicker's volume is inconsistent thanks to Denver's struggling offense, and through six games, he's gone 9-for-12 on FG attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra points. Lutz could be busier than usual in Week 7 against a Cardinals team that's allowed 29.7 points per game, tied with the Saints for the worst mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Wil Lutz was busy and efficient in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, converting all three of his extra points and all three of his field-goal attempts for a season-best 12 points. The veteran kicker has booted multiple FGs in three of the last four games and multiple PATs in three straight, but the overall struggles of the Denver offense put a cap on Lutz's upside. He likely won't be able to squander any opportunities in Week 8 against a Kansas City team that ranks second in the NFL in points per game allowed.
outlooksByWeek.9: Wil Lutz hasn't missed a kick in three straight games, connecting on both his field goal attempts and both his PATs in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. The veteran kicker is a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points this season, but his 82.4% showing on FG attempts (14-for-17, including two misses from inside 50 yards) would be his worst mark in four years since following Sean Payton to Denver from New Orleans. Lutz could see plenty of opportunities to improve that performance in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator after allowing 27.6 points a game, 28th in the league, through the first half of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Wil Lutz comes out of the Broncos' Week 10 bye having converted multiple field goal attempts in three straight games and multiple PATs in five straight. The veteran kicker had a slow start to the season and still sits outside the top 20 in kicker scoring, but his recent consistency gives him a relatively stable floor, and playing his home games at altitude offers some upside. Lutz could be busy in Week 11 against a Raiders team that's allowed the most points per game in the league at 28.9, tied for 31st with the Cardinals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to bounce back from a quieter game as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. St. Brown finished Week 3 against the Jets with a touchdown, but other than that, he has just four catches for 19 yards. The eight targets he finished with did still tie  Jahmyr Gibbs for a team lead, so the volume remains for the pair of stars to both produce highly. St. Brown will face a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to find the end zone again as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. St. Brown returned to a solid eight catches for 75 yards against the Panthers in Week 4, but he also broke his three-game touchdown streak. The star pass catcher has now totaled 31 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns this season. He'll take on a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to find the end zone again as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. St. Brown has remained hot as of late with 14 catches for 144 yards in his last two outings, but he's been unable to find the end zone since Week 3. The star wide receiver will take a 37-372-5 receiving line into a big matchup versus a Green Bay secondary that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to heal from an ankle injury in time for Detroit's Week 8 matchup versus Minnesota. St. Brown played a full game in Week 7 against the Packers, finishing with nine catches for a season-high 153 yards. The star pass catcher also tweaked his ankle in the game, and while he's not expected to miss any time, his situation is worth monitoring. St. Brown will aim to expand on a 46-525-5 receiving line opposite to a Vikings defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to make a return to the end zone as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. St. Brown logged seven receptions for 46 yards and recorded one rush for 10 yards in a Week 8 win over Minnesota. The featured pass catcher has remained a dominant option week in and out, but he hasn't posted a touchdown since Week 3. He'll face a Miami defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs this season but 18th in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. St. Brown led Detroit in all receiving categories against the Dolphins in Week 9, bringing in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards. The star wide receiver is on track for another dominant year, but he hasn't logged a touchdown since Week 3. He enters a favorable matchup versus a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. St. Brown finally broke his touchdown drought in a Week 10 blowout win over New England, catching four of five targets for 98 yards and two scores. The star pass catcher has now posted a 65-755-7 receiving line on 91 targets across nine contests. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey McBride will look to remain productive for Arizona's offense in Week 6 against the Rams. McBride put up another big line against Detroit this past Sunday, catching nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end leads all NFL players with 42 receptions this season, and only Amon-Ra St. Brown (57) has more targets than McBride's 56. That should mean McBride gets plenty of opportunities against the Rams, but to find success he'll have to overcome a defense that is giving up the fewest fantasy points per game (3.2) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey McBride remains Arizona's most dependable receiving weapon, compiling 49 receptions for 361 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 49 catches lead the Cardinals by a wide margin, and his consistent involvement provides a strong PPR foundation despite the team's struggles to generate explosive plays, as he has had at least seven catches in each of his six appearances to date. McBride also led Arizona's passing attack during its Week 6 victory over the Rams, reinforcing his importance to Jacoby Brissett. He faces a relatively neutral matchup against Denver in Week 7, with the Broncos allowing 8.2 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, the 15th-best mark in the league. Given his involvement on offense, however, McBride should remain a reliable TE1 regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trey McBride has established himself as one of the NFL's top pass catchers ahead of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas. The star tight end posted season-best marks with 10 catches and 111 yards while scoring his fourth touchdown in Week 7 against Denver. McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches on the campaign, and he's tied for second with 78 targets. The Cowboys rank middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season, but McBride is as matchup-proof as any player at his position in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Trey McBride doesn't seem likely to slow down despite a quarterback change in Arizona with a Week 9 tilt in Seattle on tap. McBride logged seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in an overtime win over Dallas in Week 8, extending his streak of games with seven-plus catches to eight to begin the season. Five of his receptions (including his TD catch) and 52 of his yards came after Gardner Minshew took over at quarterback in the third quarter, so the Cardinals' switch to Minshew as the starter in Week 9 doesn't figure to slow down McBride's production. However, the Seahawks present a tough challenge, as they've given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (5.4) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Trey McBride could be extremely busy for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams. McBride has already been drawing constant attention in the Arizona passing game, recording at least seven catches and eight targets in all nine of the team's games this year. Now that top wideouts Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are likely done for the season, McBride may be even more heavily targeted. However, he'll be working with rookie QB Carson Beck for the first time due to Gardner Minshew's potentially season-ending elbow injury. McBride will also be going up against a Rams defense that is tied for second in the league in fewest fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, though he notched a fine 7-53-0 line against them in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.11: Trey McBride is set to work with rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the second time when the Cardinals travel to Kansas City for a Week 11 clash. McBride had his season-opening streak of logging at least seven receptions snapped this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, when he managed a quiet 5-37-0 receiving line on five targets. Nonetheless, every part of his line (catches, receiving yardage and targets) led the Cardinals in a game during which Beck struggled mightily to move the ball. There could be an opportunity for McBride to post better numbers against Kansas City, who have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game (9.8) to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.
outlooksByWeek.8: Breece Hall's role is uncertain if he returns from a quad injury in Week 8 when the Jets face the Raiders. Hall has not played since Week 3 and has topped 32 yards just once, while Braelon Allen has shined during his absence. Being eased back into action appears more likely than immediately commanding the Jets' backfield, but he may not require heavy volume to be an intriguing asset, as the Raiders are allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs and 5.2 yards per carry. Five opposing backs have rushed for 94 yards or more against them.
outlooksByWeek.9: Breece Hall is poised to return from a five-game absence due to a quad injury when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. In Hall's absence, Braelon Allen shined and has likely earned at least a portion of the carries, leaving Hall's role uncertain. Pairing that with a matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, Hall doesn't offer a solid floor or much upside in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Breece Hall's workload should be strong in the Jets' Week 10 matchup against a tough Bills run defense. Returning to action in Week 9 after a five-game absence, Hall collected 18 touches to Braelon Allen's 10, despite Allen's success while Hall was sidelined. Hall has logged at least 13 carries in all four games when healthy, adding 13 receptions. His viability in the passing game should allow him to be a fantasy factor despite facing a defense that's allowing just 3.8 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.11: Breece Hall brings steady volume into a somewhat challenging matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Hall has amassed at least 11 carries in both games since returning from injury while adding seven receptions, tallying 195 total yards though not reaching the end zone and continuing to share reps with Braelon Allen. The Chargers are allowing the 10th most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but just 4.0 yards per carry and an even lower 3.9 yards per reception. Hall remains a lineup mainstay and could surge in the receiving game if Cade Klubnik is forced into action over Geno Smith (ankle).

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite Carolina's offensive struggles in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, McMillan was relatively productive, catching four of six targets for 40 yards. On the season, the second-year pro has nabbed 36 of 54 targets for 511 yards (11th-most in the NFL) and two touchdowns in just six contests. He could find success in Week 8 against a Packers secondary that's given up six receiving touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Following his huge performance against the Lions in Week 4 (14-192-2), McMillan has cooled off, catching just 16 of 26 targets for 184 yards and no scores over Carolina's last three games. Despite this, McMillan ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards per game (81.1) 12th in targets per game (9.3), which suggests more production is coming in the near future. However, he's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Denver secondary that's allowed just 27.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. McMillan salvaged his fantasy day with a late score in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, catching four of six targets for 56 yards. The Arizona product has cooled down since his monstrous performance in Week 4 (14-192-2), averaging 5.0 receptions and 60.0 receiving yards per game over his last four contests. Despite this, McMillan could find success against a Saints secondary that's allowed 31.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain Carolina's top wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. McMillan was limited to just three catches on seven targets during the Week 10 win over the Saints, his fewest reception total since the Week 3 loss to the Browns. However, he ranked first on the team in targets while the rest of Carolina's receiver room combined for five targets, which is positive sign for McMillan's fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan could thrive against the Ravens in Week 11, as they have given up 34.3 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.
outlooksByWeek.5: David Montgomery has plodded to 2.7 yards per carry and has failed to find the end zone since scoring three TDs in Week 1, his Texans debut. Fellow Houston RB Woody Marks has scored twice during Montgomery's three-game touchdown drought. Montgomery and Marks will likely split carries again in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 100 rushing yards per game to RBs, though Tennessee is giving up only 3.6 yards per carry. If Houston's defense can recapture last season's elite form and stifle the underwhelming Titans offense, Montgomery could get enough volume to wear down Tennessee's defense and make up for a lack of quality with quantity. With Houston's running game stuck in first gear, Montgomery is an unexciting flex candidate for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: David Montgomery is considered week-to-week after departing Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. He's likely to sit out in Week 6 against the Jaguars, leaving Woody Marks to lead Houston's backfield against Jacksonville's league-best run defense in London. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars and is considered week-to-week. If he returns for Week 7 against the Giants, Montgomery would likely split carries with Woody Marks and possibly Jawhar Jordan. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. The Giants have struggled to defend RBs, allowing 108 rushing yards and one total TD per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's last two games prior to the Week 8 bye, and it sounds like he may not be ready to suit up in Week 9 against the Chargers. Even if Montgomery is cleared to return, he'll be a risky flex option, as he was averaging a meager 2.7 yards per carry prior to getting injured while splitting carries with Woody Marks. The Chargers rank among the league's 10 most generous run defenses, allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Running backs have scored nine total touchdowns in seven games against the Chargers, with eight of those TDs coming on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.10: David Montgomery (groin) is apparently nearing a return to practice, but he still looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 against the Browns. He hasn't suited up since exiting in Week 5, with Woody Marks leading Houston's backfield in the interim. Even if Montgomery gains clearance to play in Week 10, he'll be a risky flex option considering he was averaging just 2.7 yards per carry prior to getting injured while working in a timeshare with Marks.
outlooksByWeek.11: David Montgomery (groin) remained sidelined for Houston's Week 10 loss against the Browns despite practicing without limitations the Friday preceding the game. He hasn't played since Week 5, but Montgomery has the green light to suit up against the Colts in Week 11 and is in line for a prominent role, as Woody Marks (concussion) will miss Thursday's game on a short week after getting hurt in Week 10. No other RB besides Montgomery or Marks has more than 13 carries for the Texans this season. Despite averaging just 2.7 yards per carry prior to his injury, Montgomery has RB2 upside given the lack of competition for backfield opportunities against a Colts defense that's allowing 151 scrimmage yards and a touchdown per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trevor Lawrence profiles as a strong Week 8 fantasy starter as the Jaguars return home to host the Colts following their Week 7 bye. In two previous starts at EverBank Stadium this season, Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes. He has a 14:4 TD:INT through six outings, the last two of which came in London. Back stateside, Lawrence should keep rolling at home against a Colts secondary that has allowed an 11:2 TD:INT and could remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf).
outlooksByWeek.9: Trevor Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes across Jacksonville's last two games, so he remains a top-10 fantasy QB option ahead of a Week 9 road game against the Ravens. He has just one touchdown pass across two road games this season, but Jacksonville's offense should get plenty of opportunities with the Ravens unlikely to sustain drives in the expected absence of Baltimore's top two QBs, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Baltimore's defense has allowed an 11:4 TD:INT ratio while ranking in the middle of the pack against the pass. Despite his lackluster road production, Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on a league-high 8.6% of his passes this season en route to a 17:4 TD:INT overall.
outlooksByWeek.10: Trevor Lawrence has thrown 18 touchdown passes, leading the Jaguars to a 6-2 record heading into a Week 10 trip to Tennessee. However, he has just three touchdown passes in three road games. Jacksonville has won its last two games by a 75-17 margin, so Lawrence has been afforded the luxury of taking his foot off the gas. This has limited his production after back-to-back 300-yard passing performances in a pair of competitive games in London. Another lopsided win is likely to materialize against the 1-7 Titans, but Lawrence is capable of producing elite numbers while the game is still up for grabs. He has top-five fantasy QB upside against a Tennessee secondary that is giving up the second-most passing yards per game, but it wouldn't be surprising if he finished outside the top 15 in Week 10, either.
outlooksByWeek.11: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in three of his last four starts and topped 300 passing yards in three of his last five, firmly placing him in the fantasy QB1 range for a Week 11 road game against the Giants. The 7-2 Jaguars and 5-3-1 Giants both lead their respective divisions, but Jacksonville's plus-125 point differential is far more impressive than the Giants' plus-7 mark. Pass defense has been a strength for the Giants, as they allow the third-fewest yards per game through the air (184). However, Lawrence maintains an elite ceiling regardless of opponent and could actually benefit statistically if this game remains close throughout, forcing the Jaguars to keep their foot on the gas. This season, he has thrown for 1,430 passing yards and 13 touchdowns in first halves, compared to 854 passing yards and eight touchdowns in second halves, with Jacksonville nursing large second-half leads on multiple occasions.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tony Pollard delivered consecutive elite performances prior to Tennessee's Week 9 bye, racking up 292 scrimmage yards and five TDs across losses to the Browns and Bengals. Prior to that two-game stretch, he had just one TD through seven games and no 100-yard performances. If he isn't traded prior to Tuesday's deadline, Pollard would maintain fantasy RB2 upside for Week 10 despite a difficult matchup against a Jaguars defense that's holding RBs to 68 yards per game. Even before his recent uptick in production, Pollard had a solid floor as the clear lead back for Tennessee.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tony Pollard has racked up 391 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns over Tennessee's last three games, putting him in the fantasy RB1 conversation for a Week 11 trip to Dallas. After a pair of dominant rushing performances, Pollard struggled to find running room against Jacksonville's elite front in Week 10 but racked up 66 receiving yards and a TD on a career-high eight catches. The former Cowboys RB is locked into a workhorse role for the Titans, and Pollard's old team has given up the most fantasy production in the league to RBs, allowing 155 scrimmage yards per game, as well as a league-high 16 total TDs to the position through 10 games.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Golden remains a high-volume option ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Golden surpassed 10 targets for the fifth time this season in a Week 8 win over Carolina, and he finished the night with seven catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher has now posted a 43-619-4 receiving line on 82 targets this season. He should have plenty of opportunities to stay hot against a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Golden will look to keep his tear rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Golden logged a career-best 164 yards on 10 catches and found the end zone in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. The second-year breakout receiver also caught every one of his targets in the win, which was a huge improvement from some drop-heavy games this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he caught six passes for 95 yards against in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.10: Chimere Dike stepped up in Week 8 with five catches for 71 yards and a TD in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate is expected to return after Tennessee's Week 9 bye, which will likely bump Dike back to a bench role on offense against the Jaguars in Week 10. Dike can be ignored in standard fantasy formats but remains an elite option in leagues that reward return yards on special teams, as the 2025 fourth-round pick leads the NFL with 3,517 all-purpose yards since entering the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chimere Dike had 71 receiving yards and a touchdown catch in Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals, but that performance accounts for more than half of his 140 receiving yards this season.
