Dike could be ticketed for a larger role in Week 11 against the Cowboys if at least one of Carnell Tate (shoulder) or Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) doesn't play. The 2025 fourth-round pick has stepped up when given more opportunities before, but Dike remains a deep-league dart throw at best in most formats, even against a weak Dallas secondary that's allowing 158 receiving yards per game to WRs, considering Tennessee's passing game has ranged from putrid to inconsistent. In fantasy formats that reward punt and kickoff return yards, you're probably starting him for his special-teams contributions regardless, with any offensive output just a nice bonus.

player.seasonOutlook: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Steelers for an AFC North divisional matchup in Week 3. He remained perfect on the season after connecting on both of his field-goal attempts and both PATs during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. McPherson drilled both of his field goals from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 6-for-6 on the season, with four of his makes coming beyond 50 yards. He'll continue to earn plenty of scoring opportunities on an elite offense, even despite Pittsburgh's strong defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Evan McPherson and the Bengals host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He stayed perfect on the year after drilling both field-goal attempts and all three PATs during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. McPherson is now 8-for-8 on FGAs and extra-point tries, including five kicks from at least 50 yards out. He'll aim to stay hot against one of the league's best defenses, as Jacksonville allows just 12.0 points per game, which ranks first. Still, McPherson should continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities for a Bengals squad averaging 26.7 PPG (12th).
outlooksByWeek.5: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Dolphins for a Week 5 road tilt. He made his only field-goal attempt from 29 yards out and connected on both of his PATs during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. McPherson remained perfect on his kicks through four outings, but he'll hope to get more involved against a Miami defense that ranks 21st in the league, allowing 25.3 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to face the Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. McPherson was forced to do his damage with extra points, as the victory marked his second straight outing with only one FGA. He'll look to make more of an impact against a Baltimore defense allowing 22.0 points per game, which ranks 15th.
outlooksByWeek.8: Evan McPherson and the Bengals return home for a Week 8 showdown against the 1-6 Titans. He did not attempt a field goal but converted all five of his extra-point tries during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. McPherson is perfect through six contests this season, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 19-for-19 on PATs. However, with the Bengals offense routinely finding the endzone, his opportunities to make a big fantasy difference have suffered.
outlooksByWeek.9: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to take on the Falcons for a Week 9 interconference tilt in Spain. He made all five of his PATs for the second consecutive game during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. It was also the second time in as many weeks that McPherson did not attempt a field goal, as Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense racked up six total TDs in the win. McPherson has yet to miss a single kick in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 24-for-24 on PATs, but his fantasy ceiling is seemingly capped with Cincinnati frequently finding the endzone.
outlooksByWeek.10: Evan McPherson and the Bengals battle the Steelers for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He went 2-for-2 on field goals and made all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. McPherson is one of two kickers who are still perfect at this point in the season, and he'll look to keep that going versus a Pittsburgh defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for the fourth fewest.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Evan McPherson and the high-flying Bengals offense will travel to Washington for an interconference showdown. He went 1-for-2 on field goals while connecting on all five PATs during Cincinnati's 38-18 win in Week 10. McPherson's miss was his first of the season, so he'll be looking to get back on track versus a Commanders team allowing 24.8 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kaelon Black and the 49ers visit the Falcons for a Week 7 showdown. He had eight carries for 34 yards and caught his lone target for three yards in San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Christian McCaffrey tallied 25 touches to the rookie's nine, leaving no doubt about who the leader is in the 49ers' backfield. Black will look to make more of an impact with his limited touches versus Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kaelon Black may have an opportunity for more work in Week 9 versus the Raiders with San Francisco's top RB, Christian McCaffrey, managing a hamstring strain. McCaffrey picked up the injury in Week 7 against Atlanta, and Black ended up logging a healthy 12 carries, which he turned into 63 yards and a touchdown. McCaffrey was able to finish out that game, and the team's Week 8 bye along with optimism that the strain is mild gives him a good chance of suiting up this Sunday, but Black could be productive even if McCaffrey plays. Las Vegas has posted some of the worst numbers in the NFL against running backs, giving up 22.3 fantasy points per game to the position, fifth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kaelon Black has been running well for the 49ers of late and will look to continue to do so Week 10 versus the Cowboys. Black has rushed for at least 63 yards in each of his past two games and is averaging a hearty 5.8 yards per carry during that span. He's still not factoring into the passing game and continues to work considerably behind top RB Christian McCaffrey, but Black is proving himself to be a capable NFL back during his rookie campaign. With enough opportunities, Black could find success against a Dallas defense that has yielded 4.77 yards per carry to running backs, fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kaelon Black could be a key factor for San Francisco in Week 11 versus a tough Minnesota defense. The rookie running back has shown plenty of promise, and he's coming off a performance against the Cowboys during which he accounted for 66 total yards and a touchdown. Despite continuing to work behind superstar Christian McCaffrey, Black has recorded double-digit carries and at least 53 rushing yards in each of his past three games and has scored two touchdowns during that span. He's averaging a healthy 4.5 yards per carry on the season, which could give him plenty of importance against a Minnesota defense that is yielding an NFL-best 14.0 points per game but that ranks in the bottom half of the league with 4.26 yards per carry allowed to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery. In his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 receiving line. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy, he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to put up big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs but ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Bowers continues to make up for lost time, producing an 8-110-1 line on 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After missing the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from knee surgery, the superstar tight end has gotten into the end zone in three straight weeks, amassing 24 catches for 312 yards and three scores on 35 targets. Bowers is the clear top option for Kirk Cousins in the passing game, and that isn't likely to change even if Las Vegas eventually switches to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. Bowers will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Bowers was held somewhat in check by the Bills in Week 6, failing to get double-digit targets for the first time in 2026 and managing a 4-70-0 line on nine looks from Kirk Cousins. Fellow TE Michael Mayer popped for a big game, but Bowers probably won't stay contained for long. Over his four appearances this season, Bowers has a 28-382-3 line on 44 targets as the clear top option in the Raiders' passing game. He'll face a tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brock Bowers has been held slightly in check the last two weeks, failing to see double-digit targets in either contest and managing a 10-143-0 line on 17 targets. Those are still strong numbers for a tight end, but a mild disappointment for an elite talent like Bowers. He remains the top option in the Raiders' passing game, even as No. 2 TE Michael Mayer continues to get more work than expected. Bowers will face a tough test in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, and which has given up just one TD to the position through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Bowers produced his first multi-TD game of the season in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, turning 10 targets into seven catches for 92 yards and two scores. The star tight end remains the top downfield option for Kirk Cousins, and over six games since making his belated 2026 debut, Bowers has amassed a 41-547-5 line on 62 targets. He could be poised to make another big impact in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brock Bowers was nearly the only Raider to find any success in a Week 9 loss to the 49ers, turning eight targets into seven catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has scored six times in seven games since making a belated season debut, and Bowers delivered a 48-658-6 line on 70 targets as Kirk Cousins' clear No. 1 downfield option. He's now likely Francisco Mendoza's top option and will look to keep rolling in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brock Bowers played just 11 offensive snaps in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury, catching both his targets for 18 yards. The star tight end's injury isn't thought to be too serious, but he could miss at least a game or two, potentially opening the door for Michael Mayer to have a bigger role. If Bowers is able to suit up in Week 11 and continue building chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, he'll be taking on a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Monangai has missed back-to-back games with turf toe, and he'll need to get back to practice if he hopes to see the field in a TNF matchup. If he is active, he'll return to a favorable backfield role versus a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Monangai will aim to make a return as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Monangai has missed the last three games with a turf toe injury, but Chicago is not planning to place him on IR. This makes it likely the second-year running back at least has a chance to return in the upcoming away tilt. With two 100-yard rushing games and three touchdowns across the first four games of the season, Monangai is an intriguing option if he returns, even against a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Monangai has sat out the last four weeks with thumb and toe issues. The second-year ball carrier recording a 30-146-2 rushing line before his inactive streak makes it even more frustrating, so he'll hopefully get back to practice sooner rather than later. If he is healthy against Tampa Bay, he'll face a defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Monangai has sat out five straight games as he works back from a turf-toe injury. The second-year ball carrier's status is very likely correlated with his ability to practice, so this week should reveal his expected return timeline. He accrued 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns off 60 carries in the first four games of the season. If he returns, Monangai will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are on the road to take on Miami's third-ranked defense against wide receivers in Week 5. He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tee Higgins and the Bengals travel to Baltimore for a divisional clash in Week 7. He caught two of four targets for 22 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Higgins was able to battle through an adductor injury that kept him limited in practices leading up to the contest, and he has now had a bye week for some added rest. He draws a favorable matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 34.1 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 22nd.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an AFC showdown against the Titans in Week 8. He caught six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. Higgins tied with Ja'Marr Chase (5-62-1) in targets but paced the Bengals in receptions and yardage for the second time in three contests. Higgins will aim to keep rolling against a Titans defense allowing 35.8 fantasy points per game to WRs, which is tied for 24th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tee Higgins and the Bengals battle the Falcons in a Week 9 interconference clash in Spain. He caught 10 of 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. Higgins led the team in yardage and TDs while finishing second in both receptions and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase (11-141-1). Higgins has tallied at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four outings, and he'll aim to stay hot against an Atlanta defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tee Higgins and the Bengals welcome the Steelers to town for a Week 10 divisional clash. He caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's Week 9 victory. Higgins recorded two TDs for the second consecutive game, and he now has five receiving scores over his last three outings. He'll look to keep up the pace versus a Pittsburgh defense he cooked for a 6-90-1 line on seven targets in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He brought in five of six targets for 66 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, extending the team's win streak to five games. Higgins' consecutive outings with a TD snapped, however, as he failed to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5. Head coach Zac Taylor relayed Higgins' workload was being managed toward the end of the win over Pittsburgh, so keep an eye on his status in practice during Week 11 prep.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.9: Nico Collins is coming off a rare dud, as the Giants held Houston's star WR to six yards in Week 7, which is 50 yards fewer than Collins' previous season low. After a Week 8 bye to stew over his down game, Collins should come out motivated to bounce back in a Week 9 road game against the winless Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 132.7 yards per game to the position. Collins remains a low-end fantasy WR1 until further notice.
outlooksByWeek.10: Nico Collins has shared the wealth in recent weeks as the locked-in C.J. Stroud spreads the ball around to a deep Texans WR room that also includes Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Kayshon Boutte. Collins has been targeted five or fewer times in each of the past three games, scoring just once over that span while averaging three catches for 45 yards. He'll need to pick up the pace to reach the 1,000-yard receiving mark for a fourth consecutive season. Collins has dropped from his customary fantasy WR1 standing to the WR2 range for a Week 10 matchup with a Browns secondary that's allowing 144 yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Nico Collins has had an inconsistent season but remains a borderline fantasy WR1 for Houston's Week 11 matchup with a Colts defense that's allowing 149 yards per game to WRs and could be without top cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf). Collins drew 16 targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after being targeted 14 times over the previous three games combined. His season average of 68 yards per game is his lowest mark since 2022. He exceeded 1,000 yards in every season from 2023 through 2025 but sits at just 478 yards through Houston's first nine games, two of which he missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins has scored five times in seven appearances and continues to work as the top target for C.J. Stroud.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. He amassed 13 carries in Week 4, one fewer than TreVeyon Henderson's 14, but Stevenson found the end zone while catching three passes for the third time in four weeks. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rhamondre Stevenson could garner workhorse carries in the Patriots' Week 6 match against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an ankle issue. Stevenson had 13 carries in Week 5 for the second straight week and now has double-digit carries in three of five games while adding at least three catches four times. With double-digit touches seemingly certain, Stevenson can exploit a defense that's allowing 4.3 yards per carry and one where he posted 102 yards and two touchdowns on only 13 touches last season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't had much room to run for the Patriots in advance of a Week 7 clash with the Bears. Stevenson has logged double-digit carries in four of his first six games but is averaging a career-low 3.7 yards per carry while sharing time with TreVeyon Henderson, who surprisingly played in Week 6 despite a high-ankle sprain. Chicago has allowed only three rushing scores, and no opposing runner has topped 61 yards since Week 3, so while volume will remain Stevenson's friend, he'll likely need to find the end zone to provide fair returns.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots' passing game will keep him active in Week 8 against the Dolphins. While he is coming off his third single-digit carry game of the season, he's caught at least three passes in five games and five in two outings, an area where Miami's defense is particularly vulnerable. The Dolphins allow a moderate 4.3 yards per carry and just three rushing touchdowns to backs, yet have given up 34 catches, including five touchdown receptions, to running backs in six games. Stevenson has multiple paths to meaningful production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rhamondre Stevenson will look to lead the Patriots backfield again in Week 9 against a stingy Packers defense. Stevenson earned double-digit touches in seven of New England's first eight games and has at least 13 carries in four of his last five contests, despite sharing backfield touches with TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner. Green Bay has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns through eight games, which Stevenson may need for solid Week 9 production, as the Packers are allowing just 3.96 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rhamondre Stevenson is uncertain to suit up for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury. New England fell into a big hole in Week 9, limiting Stevenson's carries prior to the injury, and he finished with a season-low six for the third time this season. His passing game involvement included a second touchdown reception in three weeks. If he plays, Stevenson figures to again lead the Patriots' backfield since TreVeyon Henderson will also likely be sidelined. Stevenson's rushing yard expectations can be tempered against a defense that's allowing a mere 3.9 yards per carry. Corey Kiner would be in line for lead back duties assuming both Stevenson and Henderson are sidelined.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.
outlooksByWeek.5: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.
outlooksByWeek.7: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.
outlooksByWeek.8: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 showdown with first place in the AFC North on the line. He brought in two of six targets for 56 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Paris. Metcalf tied for the lead in targets while pacing the team in yardage despite his low reception count. He'll be ready to face a Cleveland defense he cooked for a season-high 115 yards on five catches in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: DK Metcalf and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for a divisional clash in Week 10. He caught just one of six targets for four yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8, giving the 28-year-old a 3-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets over his last two contests. Metcalf and the Steelers didn't have to throw much while playing most of Week 8 with a double-digit advantage, but that could change in Week 10 versus a high-powered Bengals offense on Sunday Night Football. In his first matchup against Cincinnati, Metcalf corralled three of five targets for 31 yards and his only TD of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs. In Week 10, he hauled in two of six targets for 54 yards, including a 32-yard touchdown, during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss. Metcalf found the end zone for just the second time all season and the first time since Week 3. Despite the favorable matchup, Metcalf remains an inconsistent fantasy option for a team that prefers to run the ball.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emmett Johnson continues to work his way into the Kansas City game plan as a pass-catcher. Over the last two games, the rookie has corralled four of six targets for 35 yards while the team deals with injuries to its wide receiver corps. Johnson will not challenge a healthy Kenneth Walker as the lead back, but Andy Reid is trying to find ways to get Johnson the ball in space. The result has been a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through his first six NFL games. Johnson will look to score his first career touchdown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Emmett Johnson took advantage of his opportunities again in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, scoring his first career rushing touchdown while gaining 34 yards on six carries. Kenneth Walker, who found the end zone three times in the victory, remains firmly on top of the depth chart, but Johnson is beginning to earn a steady workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield. The rookie is averaging a tidy 4.3 yards per carry on the ground, while adding a 14-237-1 line on 16 targets over eight games. Johnson could make an impact on limited touches again in Week 10 against a Falcons defense that's tied for 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Emmett Johnson was incredible in his first career NFL start in Week 10 against the Falcons, leading Kansas City to a big win with 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The opportunity came with Kenneth Walker sidelined by a groin injury, but the issue isn't expected to keep the former Seahawk sidelined for long. Johnson's performance does make a case for him to take on a bigger workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield once Walker is back. Johnson will look to exploit what volume he gets in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dalton Kincaid hopes to rediscover some early season success with the Bills coming out of a bye week to host the Ravens in Week 8. After snagging 12 of 14 targets for 225 yards in his first two games, Kincaid has not topped 38 yards or scored in his subsequent four outings, despite maintaining a higher snap share than last season. Baltimore is allowing only 39.0 yards per game to opposing tight ends, setting up Kincaid for another quiet week, but the Ravens allowed two touchdowns to the position last week and five overall, potentially helping Kincaid break his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dalton Kincaid faces a challenging matchup in Week 9 when the Bills face the Vikings. He has 11 catches over the last two weeks, scoring in Week 8 for the first time since Week 2, and finished with 86 yards after hauling in just 90 total yards in his previous four games. Minnesota has allowed the fewest points per game to opposing tight ends, surrendering only 6.2 yards per target and no touchdowns through seven games. Kincaid needs volume to be productive in the Week 9 Monday night affair, and that's not a sure thing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills offense may be sliding as they enter a Week 10 matchup against the Jets. In Buffalo's first six games, Kincaid garnered less than a 66% snap share just once, but since the team's Week 7 bye, he's been under 60% in two outings, resulting in just nine targets. The Jets have been vulnerable against tight ends, allowing at least 72 yards in three straight weeks, but Kincaid's recent workload is a concern.
outlooksByWeek.11: A lack of opportunities could keep the Bills' Dalton Kincaid from exploiting the Dolphins' defense in Week 11. He had just three targets for the second straight game in Week 10, and his snap share has declined in each of the last three games since Buffalo's Week 7 bye, reaching a season-low 46% in Week 10. Buffalo has been a run-heavy offense, often leaving Kincaid off the field in favor of more traditional blocking tight ends. With declining snaps, he will be left with too few chances to beat a defense that's allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Woody Marks is set to occupy a change-of-pace role behind David Montgomery in Week 2, when the Texans host the Bengals. Marks turned 11 touches into 40 scrimmage yards in Week 1 against the Bills, while Montgomery had 79 yards and three TDs on 23 touches. Cincinnati had the worst run defense in the league last season, but Marks' modest usage makes him no better than a deep-league flex play as long as Montgomery is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Woody Marks capitalized on a negative game flow in Week 2, out-touching David Montgomery 13-8. The 0-2 Texans will face a Colts team that's also 0-2 in Week 3, and Montgomery is likely to reclaim the lead role unless Houston falls into a multi-score hole again. Marks is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry and 4.2 yards per catch in 2026 after averaging a modest 3.6 yards per carry during his 2025 rookie season. He has RB3/flex upside in Week 3 against a Colts defense that's giving up 177 rushing yards per game, but Marks' uncertain role and poor efficiency this season cap his value despite the intriguing matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Woody Marks is the 1B option in Houston's backfield, which is enough to earn flex consideration in deeper formats for Week 4 against the Cowboys. The Cowboys are giving up 114 rushing yards per game to RBs and have surrendered four TDs to the position. Marks has 29 touches this season to David Montgomery's 44. Neither RB has found much running room behind Houston's weak offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.0 yards per carry, while Montgomery is at 2.8 yards per carry. Marks scored his first touchdown of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, while Montgomery has three TDs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Woody Marks takes a two-game touchdown streak into the Texans' Week 5 trip to Tennessee, though he has been out-touched 54-35 by David Montgomery in Houston's backfield. Marks has pulled within one touchdown of Montgomery this season, and neither running back has been efficient behind Houston's struggling offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.1 yards per carry to Montgomery's 2.7. The Titans are giving up 100 yards per game on the ground to RBs, but Marks' position on the short end of a backfield platoon makes him a deep-league flex candidate at best for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Woody Marks is set to lead Houston's backfield in Week 6 against the Jaguars, as fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) is considered week-to-week. Marks racked up 85 scrimmage yards on 19 touches in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, a game Montgomery exited in the first half. Jacksonville is allowing a league-low 63.8 rushing yards per game, but RBs are averaging 40 receiving yards per game against the Jaguars. Expectations should be tempered due to the difficult matchup, but Marks is projected to get plenty of touches, making him a high-end Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Woody Marks has averaged 18 touches and 83 scrimmage yards over Houston's last two games, leading the team's backfield since David Montgomery sustained a groin injury early in Week 5. Prior to that point, Marks averaged nine touches for 30 yards per game. If Montgomery is unable to play in Week 7, Marks would be a fantasy RB2 in the lead role against a Giants defense that has allowed three rushing scores and three receiving TDs to RBs through six games this season. Jawhar Jordan, who had six carries for 43 yards and a TD in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville, would likely work in a change-of-pace role again. If Montgomery returns, Marks would still be a viable flex option, albeit with a far lower floor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Woody Marks looks set to retain the lead role in Houston's backfield for a juicy Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, leaving him firmly in the fantasy RB2 range. David Montgomery hasn't played since getting banged up early in Week 5 against the Titans, and he may not be ready to return after Houston's Week 8 bye. Marks has averaged 18.7 touches over the past three games while recording at least 81 scrimmage yards in each of those three games. He should continue to pile up yardage against a Chargers defense that is allowing 124.6 rushing yards per game, and Marks has a nice opportunity to find the end zone for the first time since Week 4, as RBs have produced nine TDs in seven games against the Chargers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Woody Marks has recorded between 17 and 20 touches for 74-85 yards in each of Houston's last four games, working in a bell-cow role in the absence of David Montgomery (groin). Montgomery looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 at Cleveland, which should keep Marks in the fantasy RB2 range thanks to his high touch floor against a Browns defense that's allowing 115 rushing yards per game to running backs. Marks hasn't scored since Week 4, while Cleveland has given up seven TDs to RBs in nine games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Woody Marks entered concussion protocol during Houston's Week 10 loss to the the Browns. He isn't expected to be cleared in time to face the Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11. David Montgomery (groin) would likely assume the lead role in Houston's backfield if he gains clearance for his first action since Week 5. Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale are Houston's other options at RB.

player.seasonOutlook: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: J.K. Dobbins continues to struggle as the primary early-down back for the Broncos. In a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, he managed just 40 rushing yards on 11 carries. This marks the fourth straight game to begin the season he's failed to reach 50 rushing yards or get into the end zone. Dobbins' 3.5 yards per carry would be a career low; he's never had a mark below 4.6 in any year he's played at least eight games. The veteran RB has at least stayed healthy, but that hasn't led to much production. He'll try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: J.K. Dobbins scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, while also producing season highs in touches (20) and rushing yards (68). The veteran running back was one of the few players to clearly benefit from Sean Payton's return to play-calling duties, but Dobbins still managed fairly modest numbers. He's been able to stay healthy so far in 2026, but through five games he's averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, a mark that would be a career low if it doesn't improve. Dobbins will take on a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that's tied for 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but which has yet to allow any back to reach 70 rushing yards in a game.
outlooksByWeek.7: J.K. Dobbins scored a rushing touchdown for a second straight game in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran running back hasn't found much success overall in a struggling offense, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry with zero gains of 20-plus yards through six games, but his role as the goal-line back provides him with a consistent path to production. Dobbins is also more involved as a pass catcher in recent weeks, producing an 8-27-0 line while logging multiple targets in four straight weeks. He'll look to break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in rushing yards per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: J.K. Dobbins may be in danger of losing his spot in the Broncos' offense. During a Week 7 win over the Cardinals, rookie Jonah Coleman led the backfield with nine carries compared to Dobbins' six, and Coleman's 11 touches were also more than RJ Harvey's five. Both Dobbins and Harvey got into the end zone while Coleman didn't, suggesting that this could be turning into a full-blown committee. Dobbins doesn't contribute as a pass catcher the way Harvey does, so if he gets supplanted on early downs by Coleman, he may fade out of the game plan entirely. Dobbins will have trouble producing on limited volume in Week 8 versus a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: J.K. Dobbins may have lost his hold on the top job in the Broncos' backfield. In a Week 8 comeback win over Kansas City, it was rookie Jonah Coleman who got the biggest workload and who scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run. Dobbins recorded just seven carries, his second straight game getting single-digit touches, and his woeful 3.3 yards per carry doesn't make a strong case for a bigger role. With RJ Harvey on injured reserve, Dobbins should retain the No. 2 job for the next few weeks. The veteran might be able to make a splash on limited carries in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and which ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: J.K. Dobbins fell into a depth role behind rookie Jonah Coleman in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the last three games, Dobbins has 17 carries to Coleman's 37, and the youngster is also seeing the bulk of the action at the goal line. Dobbins scored a rushing TD during that span, and he hasn't completely disappeared from the game plan, but it would likely take an injury to Coleman for him to log significant volume again. Dobbins will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game.
