He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Addison will aim to do more with his targets as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Addison didn't do much again in Week 7 against the Colts, reeling in two of his three targets for 30 yards. The speedy pass catcher has put together an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, totaling just 13 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown across five games. He'll look to capitalize on a faulty Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Addison will seek to build off a team-leading performance as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Addison led Minnesota with 66 receiving yards on three catches in a Week 8 loss to the Lions. The speedy pass catcher has posted a modest 16-249-1 receiving line across six games this season. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Addison will look to get more volume in Week 10 as the Vikings play the Packers. Addison finished a Week 9 loss with two catches for 28 yards off three targets, but struggles from the QB room didn't leave much room for any pass catchers to succeed. The trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins to be Minnesota's new starting quarterback could be just the spark Addison needs, as he's recorded less than 30 yards in two of his last three games. Green Bay has ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordan Addison is set to remain out as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Addison missed a Week 10 win over Green Bay with a thumb injury, and he's likely to require a possible IR-designating surgery. Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton could all see an uptick in usage with Addison inactive.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Sanders appears in line to handle kicking duties for the Jets again in Week 4 against the Bears. Sanders has routinely been activated from the practice squad in advance of game day and has made all five of his PATs and 5-of-6 field goals. Chicago has allowed just 17 points to opposing kickers through three weeks, and with the Jets not offering a high-powered offense, Sanders seems unlikely to provide a top-end fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Sanders hasn't notched many scoring chances in the Jets' limited offense entering Week 5 against the Browns. Through four games, Sanders has eight field goal attempts and only five PATs, keeping his floor and ceiling low. Cleveland has allowed the second-most field goal attempts (12) through four games, so perhaps there's a chance at a productive Week 5 if the Jets continue to be held out of the end zone, but Sanders' overall body of work doesn't suggest fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Sanders hasn't collected ample attempts to create a floor or ceiling ahead of the Jets' Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Sanders has just seven PATs through five games, while only attempting multiple field goals in two of five outings. New England is the fourth-stingiest team to opposing kickers, allowing just six made field goals, likely again keeping Sanders out of the Week 6 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Sanders could offer bye-week replacement production for the Jets in a Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. Sanders drilled a season-high four field goals in Week 6, his third game in six appearances with multiple 3-point connections, and he's added multiple PATs at the same 50% clip. Miami's defense has allowed plenty of points to opposing kickers, surrendering three extra point attempts and two field goals per game, setting Sanders up for a potentially busy, high-scoring Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jason Sanders hasn't been a high-scoring option in the Jets' limited offense ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Through seven games, Sanders has only 10 PATs while making one or two field goals in five of those outings. The Raiders are allowing the 10th-fewest fantasy points to kickers, as opponents routinely convert drives into touchdowns (24 PATs, just 10 field goal attempts). There are likely safer kickers available for Week 8 fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jason Sanders' opportunities have been uneven for the Jets ahead of a Week 9 game against the Chiefs. For the second time in three weeks and third time overall in Week 8, Sanders attempted four field goals. Unfortunately, he has four games with just one made 3-pointer, while three times collecting one or zero PATs. Kansas City has allowed 15 field goals through seven games but only 10 PATs, so while suggesting the Jets will have stalled drives is fair, field goals likely won't keep them competitive, making Sanders a risky Week 9 option.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jason Sanders brings a high ceiling into the Jets' Week 10 game against the Bills. He has attempted at least four field goals in consecutive games and three of his last four, with the Jets' offense failing to convert drives into touchdowns, evident by just six PATs over this four-game stretch. Buffalo is allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, and field goals aren't likely to help the Jets in Week 10, but Sanders' recent run of scoring puts him in the streaming mix.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jason Sanders surged into fantasy relevance for an inefficient Jets offense ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. The Jets have been kept out of the end zone in consecutive games, forcing Sanders to kick four field goals in each outing, something he's now done in four of their last five games. Sanders has double-digit scoring potential against a defense that's allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game to opposing kickers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ryan Flournoy could not take advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. Despite Pickens being sidelined with a hamstring issue, Flournoy managed his fewest catches since Week 3. He finished with just two grabs for the contest, though did gain 53 yards total on the receptions. While Pickens may be shelved for Week 10 as well, Flournoy will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ryan Flournoy has scored in three of the last five contests for the Cowboys. Flournoy has caught at least two passes in every game this season, and has drawn at least four targets in all but one contest. In Week 11, Flournoy has a tasty matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Mayer's volume took a significant step backward in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After turning 10 targets into an 8-82-0 line in Week 4, Mayer got only one look from Kirk Cousins in New England, turning it into a two-yard gain. Brock Bowers is the unquestioned top option in the team's passing game, but a lack of established wide receivers has created an opening for Mayer to be more than just injury insurance. Through five games, he's delivered a 21-171-1 line on 25 targets, putting him on pace for career-best numbers in 2026. Mayer will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Mayer took advantage of the extra defensive attention the Bills paid to Brock Bowers in Week 6, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 95 yards. While Bowers remains the top option in the Raiders' passing attack, Mayer is on pace for a career-best year of his own, producing a 28-266-1 line on 34 targets through six games. He is eight receptions and 63 yards away from establishing new personal bests. Mayer will likely struggle to reach those marks in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Michael Mayer continues to provide consistency as a secondary option for Kirk Cousins in the Raiders' passing attack. The fourth-year tight end has caught at least three passes in seven of eight games this season, putting together a 36-351-1 line on 43 targets. Brock Bowers is the clear No. 1 option for Cousins, but Las Vegas' lack of depth at wide receiver has allowed Mayer to surge to a career season, and his 36 catches for 351 yards through eight games are already new personal bests. Mayer will take aim at a 49ers defense in Week 9 that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Michael Mayer posted modest numbers in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, catching all three of his targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has snagged at least three passes in eight of nine games this season, and he's already set new career highs with 39 receptions and 388 receiving yards. Even with Brock Bowers ahead of him on the depth chart, Mayer's role is large enough to give him some value heading into a Week 10 clash with a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Michael Mayer could be set for a significant role in the Raiders' passing game in the short term. In a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, Brock Bowers suffered an ankle injury, and while it's not thought to be serious, he could be sidelined for a game or two. Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards against Seattle, but his volume from rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza would likely increase with Bowers off the field. If Mayer's volume does increase in Week 11, it will come against a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Egbuka was sidelined for the Week 7 win over the Panthers but still leads Tampa Bay in targets (49), receptions (28) and receiving touchdowns (two) this season. With Baker Mayfield at quarterback this year, Egbuka has averaged 4.3 receptions, 47 yards and 0.3 touchdowns per game. He could find success against a Falcons defense that's given up 34.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a concussion and a foot injury. During that span, the Buccaneers completed just seven of 14 pass attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown, proving Egbuka's importance to the passing game. He's expected to lead the team's WR room against a tough Bears secondary that's allowed just 29.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through seven games this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Emeka Egbuka is expected to lead the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Egbuka has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 season, catching 31 of 54 targets for 278 yards and two touchdowns in seven games. Despite this poor start, he ranks first on the Buccaneers in receiving yards, receptions, targets and touchdowns this year, suggesting more fantasy production is imminent. Egbuka could thrive against the Lions' secondary in Week 11, as they have allowed 32.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receiver groups this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He completed 39 of 54 pass attempts for 428 yards with one TD and two INTs while rushing three times for six yards and another score during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. The Bengals leaned on Burrow while playing from behind most of the game, but with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both questionable to suit up against Miami, they're hoping a better start will allow them to rely on the ground game a bit more. The Dolphins' defense is certainly beatable, allowing 21.2 fantasy points to QBs (T-18th) and 29.7 to RBs, which ranks dead last.
outlooksByWeek.7: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. During Cincinnati's Week 5 win over Miami, he threw for 190 yards (23-for-32) with four TDs and no INTs while rushing four times for 10 yards. Now coming off their bye week, Burrow will look to find holes in a tough Ravens defense that allows 17.5 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks seventh. The good news is that he'll have his vast array of complementary skill players available following a week of rest, headlined by Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
outlooksByWeek.8: Joe Burrow and the Bengals return home to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He completed 22 of 30 pass attempts for 292 yards with four touchdowns and zero interceptions and rushed twice for 12 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. It was Burrow's second straight outing with four TDs and no INTs, as he threw all of his scores in the second half. Up next is a Tennessee defense allowing 19.2 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks 12th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. In Week 8, he completed 38 of 48 pass attempts for 462 yards with five TDs and three INTs, and he had three carries for 10 yards and another score during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win. Burrow recorded season highs in passing yards, completion percentage, TDs, and INTs, and he has posted a 13:3 TD:INT ratio over his last three outings. Burrow faces a Falcons defense allowing 18.7 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Joe Burrow and the Bengals welcome the divisional-rival Steelers to town for a Week 10 meeting on Sunday Night Football. He stayed red-hot in Week 9, completing 24 of 29 pass attempts for 271 yards and three TDs with no INTs, while rushing three times for seven yards and another score. Burrow owns a 16:3 TD:INT ratio and has two rushing TDs over his last four outings, and he continues to lead the NFL with 23 passing TDs through eight games. He'll look to avenge a Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh, when he went 28-for-37 for 282 yards and three scores but lost a fumble with 53 seconds remaining and Cincinnati down by three.
outlooksByWeek.11: Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11. His hot streak continued during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, as he threw for 409 yards with four TDs and no INTs while rushing once for eight yards. Over his last five outings, all Bengals wins, Burrow has compiled 1,624 passing yards with a 20:3 TD:INT ratio, while adding 47 rushing yards and another two scores. The NFL's leading passer in terms of TDs (27) will aim to keep rolling versus the Commanders' 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to opposing QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rome Odunze will look to do more as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Odunze brought in just three of four targets for 39 yards in Week 6, which was a bit of a bummer, with Caleb Williams throwing for 305 yards. The third-year pass catcher has been held in check in more games than not this season, catching 20 of 33 targets for 312 yards with zero touchdowns. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rome Odunze will look to capitalize on his opportunities as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Odunze was outperformed by teammate Luther Burden once again in Week 7 against the Patriots, logging four catches for 69 yards to Burden's four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown. Odunze has still been solid throughout this year, with a 24-381-0 receiving line over the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Seahawks defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rome Odunze figures to be a top option in Chicago's passing game again as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Odunze finished Week 8 with his second-highest yardage of the season, bringing in four of six targets for 87 yards. The third-year wide receiver has eight catches for 156 yards in the last two weeks, which is his most productive two-game stretch so far this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rome Odunze will aim to build on a season-best showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Odunze notched his first touchdown of the season and paired it with four catches for 60 yards in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay before Chicago's bye week. The third-year pass catcher has now logged 32 receptions for 528 yards and a touchdown across nine games this season. He'll take on a New Orleans squad that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jakobi Meyers has established himself as the No. 2 WR for the Jaguars behind Parker Washington, putting Meyers firmly in the fantasy flex conversation for a Week 8 home game against the Colts. Meyers is averaging 48 receiving yards on 4.7 targets per game, and he set season highs in both of those categories with 83 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. The veteran wideout faced the Colts three times last season. Two of those meetings came after Meyers was acquired by the Jaguars in a midseason trade, and he mustered exactly 39 receiving yards in both games while scoring a touchdown in one of those matchups. He has five TDs in 15 regular-season games with Jacksonville.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jakobi Meyers was held to two catches in Week 8 while playing through a hamstring injury. He has had an up-and-down season for the Jaguars while working as the No. 2 WR behind Parker Washington. The Jaguars visit the Ravens on Thursday in Week 9, so Meyers may not have time to regain health on a short week. The injury risk lowers his floor, but he's a passable flex option against a Ravens defense that's giving up 177.6 yards per game to wideouts. Meyers is averaging 3.1 catches for 44.1 yards per game, with two TDs in seven outings.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jakobi Meyers is a strong Week 10 flex play against a Titans defense that has struggled to cover wide receivers. Tennessee is allowing a league-high 15.3 catches for 195 yards per game to the position. Meyers has had an up-and-down season as Jacksonville's No. 2 WR but has trended in the right direction recently, notching two of his three best performances this season for both receiving yards and targets within the last three games. He's more likely to produce a peak than a valley in the first of Jacksonville's two meetings this season against Tennessee's league-worst secondary.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jakobi Meyers ranks second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington in both receiving yards (408) and targets (43), but the gap between Washington and Meyers is far larger than the gap between Meyers and TE Brenton Strange for the role of Trevor Lawrence's No. 2 target. Meyers has exceeded 65 yards just once all season and hasn't scored since Week 3, so he has been a disappointment more often than not for fantasy managers plugging him into a flex spot. He'll have a decent opportunity to end his six-game touchdown drought in Week 11 against a Giants secondary that has allowed WRs to score 11 times in nine games, though the Giants hold wideouts to just 127 yards per game. As usual, Meyers is a fine deep-league flex but not a player to get particularly excited about.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Shough will look to stay hot in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Shough was very productive in the Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for just 176 total yards but scoring four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing). Despite attempting just 30 passes in last week's win, Shough is still averaging the third-most pass attempts per game in the NFL (39.2) through six weeks. Shough could struggle against a tough Steelers defense in Week 7, as they have allowed just 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Shough is expected to leads the Saints' offense into the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Through seven contests this season, Shough has thrown for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while averaging the most pass attempts per game (39.0) in the NFL. With this high passing volume, Shough should continue to find fantasy success going forward. However, he could really struggle against a tough Browns defense in Week 9 that's given up just 17.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Shough is expected to continue leading the Saints' offense during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Shough played turnover-free football in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns, completing 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown. He remains tied for the league-lead in passing attempts per game (38.5). Additionally, 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson made his season debut in Week 9, suggesting Shough's fantasy outlook is very positive going forward. Shough could continue to thrive in Week 10 against a Carolina defense that's allowed 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Shough is set to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Shough had an underwhelming outing in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, completing 25 of 35 pass attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Despite this, he remains tied for the second-most pass attempts per game (38.1) in the NFL this season, suggesting he'll have loads of opportunities for points as the year progresses. Shough is set to face a Bears defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Mason could be in line for a workhorse role as the Vikings travel to Detroit in Week 8. Mason made his return from IR in Week 7 against the Colts and logged 15 carries for 68 yards, leading the ground game with Aaron Jones hurting his knee in the matchup. Jones' status is up in the air moving forward, so Mason's role could be even bigger if he has full command of the backfield. The Lions have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Mason should remain a part of a two-punch backfield in Week 9 as the Vikings play the Bills. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with eight carries in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, but he finished with just 20 yards compared to Aaron Jones' five carries for 22 yards. The current timeshare between the two could continue to keep both in check, but Buffalo ranking 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Mason will look to see a more favorable game script in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Mason rushed just six times for 35 yards and reeled in two of three targets for seven yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. As expected, the fifth-year ball carrier has been a part of a two-pronged backfield approach next to Aaron Jones this season, but it appears Mason might be the more efficient of the pair. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his situation as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with 16 carries for 59 yards in a Week 10 win over the Packers, but teammate Aaron Jones punched in the only touchdown from the pair. Mason has yet to record a score in four outings since returning from a thumb injury, but he's put together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry. He'll face a San Francisco defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers in Week 2. Unfortunately for the second-year pro, he's expected to miss "significant time" with a left knee injury sustained in Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The severity of his injury is still being evaluated, but there's a high chance of him being placed on IR once more information comes out.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dylan Sampson and the Browns travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He rushed six times for 45 yards and caught all three targets for another 32 yards during Cleveland's Week 7 win. Sampson made his first appearance since Week 1 due to a knee injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) also returned from a one-game absence and out-touched Sampson 18-9, but it was still encouraging for Sampson to take advantage of his opportunities. He'll look to build upon this showing versus a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dylan Sampson and the Browns return home to face off against Houston in Week 10. He had eight carries for 21 yards and caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Cleveland's Week 9 overtime loss. Sampson finished tied for second on the team in targets, and with the Browns' offense likely to play from behind most weeks, he could provide a boost as the preferred back on passing downs. Sampson will aim to contribute more facing a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brenton Strange has picked up the pace after a slow start and is a viable Week 8 starter at TE for Jacksonville's home game against the Colts. He has caught 19 of 23 targets for 207 yards over the past three games after being limited to seven catches for 72 yards on 10 targets through Week 3, though Strange hasn't scored since the season opener. Strange has a nice opportunity to snap his five-game touchdown drought against the Colts, who have allowed five TDs to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brenton Strange leads the Jaguars with 28 catches this season and has averaged 65.5 receiving yards over the past four games after averaging a meager 24 yards per game through Week 3. Despite the recent uptick in production, he hasn't scored a TD since Week 1. Strange has a nice opportunity to end his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Ravens, who have allowed six TDs to TEs, which is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Given Strange's recent involvement and the favorable matchup, he's worth starting in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brenton Strange is a viable fantasy option in Week 10 against the Titans, but he's far from a must-start. He leads the Jaguars with 30 catches through eight games but hasn't scored since the season opener and is averaging 45 yards per game, which ranks 10th among TEs. Tennessee has struggled to defend the pass in general, but the Titans have limited TEs to 43 yards per game, though they have also given up four TDs to the position through eight games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brenton Strange remains a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 11 against the Giants. He scored his first TD since Week 1 in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans but had just nine receiving yards, dropping his season average to 41 yards per game. That's right in line with the 48 receiving yards per game that the Giants allow to TEs, as they are a better-than-average defense against the position. Rookies Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol have each recorded at least one catch in three consecutive games, but Strange remains the clear No. 1 TE for Jacksonville, handling a snap share north of 75%.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Bates will look to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, nailing eight field-goal attempts and converting all 20 of his XPAs across five games. While the field-goal usage hasn't quite been there, the touchdown-scoring ability of Detroit's offense has kept Bates on the field. He'll face a Green Bay squad that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (4.2) to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Bates nailed both of his two extra-point tries and two field-goal attempts including a game winner in Week 7 against the Packers. The third-year kicker has yet to miss a kick this season, making 10 field goals and 22 XPAs. He'll face a Minnesota team that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (5.3).
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Bates will look to stay solid as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. Bates missed his first kick of the season in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, but he still converted two of three field goals and nailed his sole XPA. The second-year kicker has now gone 12-for-13 on field goal attempts and made all 23 of his extra-point tries across seven outings. The Dolphins have ranked in the middle against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jake Bates will look to benefit from high volume again as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Bates was perfect in a Week 9 win over Miami, nailing five total kicks which included four field goals. The third-year boot has now made multiple field goals for the third straight game, with Detroit's offense cooling down slightly after a crazy start to the year. New England has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jake Bates will look to stay reliable as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Bates didn't attempt a field goal in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but 5 XPAs kept his performance solid. The starting boot has now converted 16 of 17 field-goal attempts and made all 29 of his extra-point tries across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.5: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: DJ Moore continues to battle through a shoulder issue that's cost him the better part of three games as the Bills head towards a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Moore has drawn 18 targets in his two healthy games, making his shoulder the only factor to worry about when considering him in lineups. The Raiders have allowed at least 91 yards to an opposing wideout in three straight weeks, adding confidence to Moore's viability if he proves healthy.
outlooksByWeek.8: DJ Moore hopes to be fully healthy following Buffalo's bye week in advance of their Week 8 matchup with the Ravens. Moore hasn't played since a brief appearance in Week 4 due to a shoulder injury that has lingered since Week 2. When on the field, he has been Josh Allen's favorite target, collecting 18 looks in two games. Baltimore has allowed four 100-yard receivers and an attractive 9.3 yards per target, the fifth-highest in the league, making Moore an attractive option if he suits up.
outlooksByWeek.9: DJ Moore will look to overcome a knee injury and help the Bills in Week 9 against the Vikings. It's been simple: when Moore plays, he's heavily involved, amassing 25 targets in three games. Minnesota is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, surrendering just four touchdown catches and 7.4 yards per target, but if he's on the field, Moore will have the volume necessary to be a viable lineup consideration.
outlooksByWeek.10: DJ Moore will look for increased volume when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. Moore collected only five targets in Week 9, his lowest total in any healthy outing of 2026, in a game where Josh Allen had minimal time to throw. While he'll likely have more time Sunday and Moore has remained the preferred option on drop-backs, the Jets have allowed only nine touchdown receptions to wideouts, seemingly capping Moore's potential.
outlooksByWeek.11: DJ Moore will seek more big plays in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. Moore is averaging 16.3 yards per catch, the second-highest mark of his nine-year career, and gets an inviting matchup with a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target to wideouts, the sixth-highest mark league-wide. Moore will need those big yardage chances as Buffalo threw only 21 times in Week 10 while blowing out the Jets, and a similar game script is likely against Miami.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jonathan Taylor has topped 90 rushing yards four times this season and has seven TDs, while the rest of the Colts' offense has scored six touchdowns combined. The star RB remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 for Week 7, even in a difficult matchup with a stout Vikings defense that's allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game (fifth-fewest) and a league-low 12.8 points per game. Opponents have been stacking the box against Taylor with Daniel Jones struggling to make defenses pay through the air, but Taylor has overcome those difficult situations to rank among the league's most productive players at his position as usual, despite the lack of help from his teammates.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonathan Taylor has at least 92 rushing yards and a TD in five of the Colts' seven games, keeping him firmly in set-and-forget fantasy RB1 territory for Week 8 despite a difficult matchup against Jacksonville's elite front. The Jaguars are allowing a league-low 72 rushing yards per game and boast the league's third-best scoring defense at 17.3 points per game. Taylor has handled 20-plus touches in all but one game this season and should remain busy in Week 8, as long as the 2-5 Colts stay within striking distance of the 4-2 Jaguars.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonathan Taylor set season lows with 12 touches for 47 yards in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. Indianapolis got down big early and had to abandon the run. The Cowboys have enough talent on offense to repeat the scenario, but it's more likely that the Colts keep things close enough for Taylor to capitalize on facing a Dallas defense that has been among the most generous in the league to RBs, allowing 11 total TDs to the position through eight games. Taylor has eight rushing TDs in eight games, accounting for more than half of the Colts' offensive touchdowns this season. He'll be a fantasy RB1 if he's in his usual role, though it's possible Indianapolis limits Taylor's usage as trade rumors swirl around the star RB.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jonathan Taylor was not traded prior to Tuesday's deadline. He has rushed for 656 yards and eight TDs through nine games with the Colts, putting the star RB on pace for a fifth campaign with at least 1,169 rushing yards and 11 TDs.
