Taylor has a juicy Week 10 matchup against the 1-7 Dolphins. Despite staying with the Colts, he remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonathan Taylor exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in 10 tries during the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins, but he was held without a touchdown for a third consecutive game. Seth McGowan has two rushing TDs during Taylor's three-game drought, both of which came from inside the 5-yard line. The rookie seventh-round pick could remain a thorn in Taylor's side if the Colts continue to give McGowan goal-line opportunities. McGowan's emergence, coupled with the Colts' offensive struggles as a team, knocks Taylor down to the fantasy RB1/RB2 borderline moving forward, and expectations should be tempered in Week 11 against a stout Texans front that limited Taylor to just 72 yards on 25 touches for a season-low 2.9 yards per touch in their first meeting this season. You're still starting Taylor if you have him in virtually every fantasy format, but he's likely to perform closer to his floor than his superstar ceiling in Week 11.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Bryant was the Broncos' surprise target leader in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching four of six targets for 42 yards. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were both taken out of the equation by the Chiefs secondary, forcing Bo Nix to look underneath for options like Bryant and tight end Evan Engram. Bryant had a solid finish to his rookie season in 2025, posting a 26-332-1 line on 39 targets over his final eight regular-season games, and his snap count and production suggest he's moved past Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin to take over the No. 3 wideout role for Denver. Bryant will look to stay involved in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Bryant scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, connecting with Bo Nix for a five-yard strike in the third quarter. It was one of just two catches on the night for the second-year wide receiver. Through three games, he's produced a 6-86-1 line on nine targets while adding a 16-yard gain on one carry. Bryant is well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order, but he seems to have secured the No. 3 role ahead of Troy Franklin. Bryant will look to build some momentum in Week 4 against a 49ers secondary that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Bryant caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but an ankle sprain knocked him out of the contest early. The second-year wide receiver is expected to miss multiple weeks, but Denver hasn't placed him on IR yet. In Bryant's absence, Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin will get more work behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, beginning with a Week 5 matchup against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Pat Bryant has missed the last four games for the Broncos due to an ankle injury, but his time on IR could be coming to an end. Prior to the injury, the second-year wideout had put together a 9-133-1 line on 12 targets over his first four contests of the season, serving as a reliable possession receiver for Bo Nix. If Bryant is cleared to suit up in Week 9, he'll be facing a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Pat Bryant returned from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury in the Broncos' final game before their Week 10 bye, catching four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. It was his most productive outing of the season, but it also came as Jaylen Waddle left the contest early with a concussion. Bryant has shown some chemistry with Bo Nix, but assuming Waddle doesn't miss additional time, his target volume figures to remain limited. Bryant will try to return to the end zone in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Etienne (hamstring) will likely operate as New Orleans' top running back if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Etienne has been sidelined for the Saints' last five games due to a hamstring issue, but his 21-day practice window is expected to be opened soon. If active for the Week 10 divisional matchup, Etienne is expected to thrive against a Panthers defense that's already allowed 12 touchdowns to opposing running backs in just eight games this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Etienne will look to make a larger impact as the Saints' take on the Bears in Week 11. Etienne was relatively ineffective in his return from injury during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, logging 11 touches for 34 yards. Despite Etienne serving as New Orleans' top running back, Audric Estime took most of the short-yardage work, and Alvin Kamara operated as the team's top red-zone back, scoring two touchdowns. Thus, Etienne's fantasy upside may be capped if his red-zone touches don't increase in the near future. He's set to face a solid Bears defense in Week 11 that's allowed just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ladd McConkey failed to catch either of his targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, leaving the game early after aggravating a foot injury he picked up in practice during the week. The third-year wideout was already playing through a rib issue, and an absence of one or more games seems almost assured. The Chargers' passing game has struggled with or without him on the field, but if McConkey does miss time, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would become Justin Herbert's top downfield options in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ladd McConkey continues to deal with injuries, sitting out the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a foot issue after dealing with a rib injury earlier in the season. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 3, but in those first three games, McConkey managed a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets as Justin Herbert's clear No. 1 option. The rest of the team's wide receiver room is also banged up, which could give the team extra incentive to get McConkey back in the lineup as quickly as possible. Even if he suits up in Week 6, he'll struggle to contribute against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ladd McConkey has only missed one game so far in 2026, but injuries have marred the season for the Chargers' top wide receiver, and he comes out of the team's bye still in the league's concussion protocol. The offense as a whole has struggled, but McConkey's been productive when reasonably healthy, posting a 12-182-1 line on 15 targets over the first three weeks. If he's cleared to return in Week 8, he'll take on a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ladd McConkey came out of the Chargers' bye looking healthy, and he was one of the few bright spots on offense for the team in a Week 8 loss to the Rams. The third-year wideout caught four of six targets for 86 yards, and over six games this season -- only two of which he saw a full snap share in -- he's produced a 17-286-1 line on 24 targets. If McConkey can stay on the field, he figures to continue being Justin Herbert's top downfield option, on a winless team that's been trailing early and often in 2026. McConkey will face an underperforming Texans secondary in Week 9 that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ladd McConkey didn't log any snaps in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, as back spasms during pregame workouts kept him on the sideline. The third-year wide receiver has seen a full workload in just two of the seven games he's been active for, and with the team winless on the season, there's little incentive for the Chargers to take any risks with his health. McConkey has been productive when he's been in the lineup, but it's becoming harder to predict when that will be. If he manages to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ladd McConkey missed his third game of the season in Week 10, this time due to back trouble, as the Chargers' beat the Ravens for their first win of the season. McConkey's been fully healthy for only two games so far in 2026, posting an 8-152-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, and his only touchdown of the year came back in the first half of Week 1 before he suffered his initial rib injury, which was followed by a foot injury and a concussion. If McConkey is cleared to return in Week 11, he'll face a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Myers will look to remain perfect this season when the Seahawks visit Arizona in Week 2. Myers made his lone PAT try and both field-goal attempts in a season-opening win over New England, though his FGs were relative chip shots from 30 and 26 yards. Myers made nine field goals from 50-plus yards out each of the previous two seasons, however, so he has plenty of leg to convert from that distance when called upon. The Cardinals aren't expected to be a top NFL defense this year, but they performed well in limiting the Chargers to 14 points in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Myers enters Seattle's Week 4 clash against the Chargers having not missed a kick so far this season. Myers handled only relatively short kicks over his first two games, but he showed off his leg with a 57-yard field goal against Washington in Week 3. The veteran kicker is now 4-for-4 on FG tries and 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts this season. Opponents have gone 6-for-7 on field-goal attempts against the Chargers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Myers has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle on tap to host San Francisco in Week 5. After attempting a career-high 48 field goals in 2025, Myers has had just five FG tries so far this season, making all of them. He's been more active kicking extra points, making 12 of 13 PATs. Perhaps Myers will be relied upon more versus the 49ers, who have allowed just five extra-point tries as opposed to nine FG attempts so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Myers is coming off a huge fantasy performance with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in the Denver altitude on tap. Myers made all five of his field-goal tries and both of his extra-point attempts in a loss to San Francisco this past Sunday, with all five of his FGs coming from 40-plus yards. Fantasy managers who roster Myers were likely waiting for this type of performance, as the veteran kicker had attempted (and made) only five field goals combined over the first four weeks of the campaign. Opponents are 9-for-11 in FG attempts against the Broncos this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Meyers and the Seahawks are back home to face off against the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and did not attempt a PAT during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. The missed field goal was his first of the season, giving the 35-year-old a 12-for-13 (92.3%) tally through six games. Meyers and the Seahawks offense could struggle to operate versus a Kansas City defense allowing 16.6 points per game, which is the second-best mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jason Myers is in the midst of one of his most accurate NFL seasons going into Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Myers has gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries through seven games and is 16-for-17 on PAT attempts. He's made all three of his field-goal tries from 50-plus yards, with his only miss this season being a 47-yard attempt. However, the Bears haven't yielded many FG tries, allowing just 10 through seven weeks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jason Myers will look to rebound from a poor performance when Seattle faces off against Arizona in Week 9. Versus the Bears in Week 8, Myers had a field goal attempt blocked and also missed an extra-point try in a Seahawks loss. The PAT miss was just his second of the season, and Myers is a solid 15-for-17 on FG tries, so the rough game shouldn't affect his job security. He could get plenty of opportunities to kick against the Cardinals, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jason Myers will hope for more kicking opportunities when Seattle faces Las Vegas in Week 10. Myers made his lone field goal and both his extra-point tries in Week 9 against Arizona as the Seahawks scored fewer than 21 points for the fourth straight week. The veteran kicker has been good when called upon this season, though, making 16 of 18 FG tries through nine games. He could be more active against the Raiders, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.

player.seasonOutlook: The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Juwan Johnson will look to bounce back from a lackluster performance in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Johnson has struggled over the last two weeks, catching just four of seven targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he remains third on the team in targets (35), receptions (25) and yards (248) through six games, suggesting more fantasy production in the near future. Johnson is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 11.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Johnson has really underperformed in the Saints' last two games, catching just one of five targets for seven yards during that span. Despite this recent lack of production, Johnson ranks third on the team in receiving yards (255), targets (38) and receptions (26) while catching three touchdowns across seven contests. Johnson could bounce back against a Cleveland defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson saw little volume but saved his fantasy day with a score in Week 9, catching two of three targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. He's been relatively underwhelming over the last three contests, catching just three of seven targets for 41 yards and a touchdown. This is especially concerning due to the return of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson, who will likely take more receiving volume away from Johnson as the season progresses. However, Johnson could thrive against a Panthers defense that's allowed 13.5 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Johnson has really struggled over New Orleans' last four games, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. With Jordyn Tyson breaking out in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers (11-80-0), Johnson will likely receive even less opportunities going forward. He likely needs to score a touchdown to find fantasy relevance in Week 11 against a Bears defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to tight ends all season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Kamara has received seven targets in two of New Orleans' last four games, proving his value to the team's passing attack. While not the most effective rusher at this stage in his career, Kamara has averaged 43 total yards on 10.5 touches per game through six contests this season. He could struggle against a tough Browns defense that's allowed just 28 total receptions to running backs through eight games this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Kamara received fewer than 10 touches for the third time in New Orleans' last four games during the Week 9 win over the Browns, despite backfield mate Kendre Miller being release prior to the contest. Regardless, Kamara ranks first amongst Saints RBs in targets (31), receptions (25), receiving yards (150) and receiving touchdowns (one) in seven appearances this year. He could find success against a Panthers defense that's allowed 230 yards and a touchdown through the air to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Alvin Kamara will remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Kamara was limited to just five touches while Travis Etienne returned from injury in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers. However, Kamara scored two touchdowns on those touches and appeared to be operating as New Orleans' top red-zone RB. With Kamara, Etienne and Audric Estime all playing roles in the Saints' backfield, it may be hard to trust any of them going forward. Kamara could take advantage of a Chicago defense that's allowed 7.3 yards per target and two receiving touchdowns to opposing RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keenan Allen is averaging over seven targets per game and has operated as the Colts' co-No. 1 WR alongside Josh Downs since Alec Pierce went down with a heel injury. Pierce remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 8 trip to Jacksonville. Allen will be a high-floor flex candidate against a Jaguars defense that's giving up a league-high 210 yards per game to wide receivers. He's averaging 55 receiving yards per game over the past four and has scored one TD this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keenan Allen has recorded at least six receptions in four of seven appearances for the Colts this season and is likely to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against a Dallas defense that's giving up 11.9 catches, as well as 164.1 receiving yards and 1.0 TD per game to WRs. Allen leads the Colts with 34 catches despite missing a game, and his 325 receiving yards are just five shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. However, the 34-year-old Allen has scored just one TD in his last 17 regular-season games, dating back to last season with the Chargers. He remains a rock-solid, high-floor flex play for Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Keenan Allen led the Colts with 40 catches on 58 targets, and his 351 receiving yards were just three shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total, with Allen having played one fewer game. Both players were shipped out of Indianapolis at the trade deadline however, with Allen landing with a San Francisco team in dire need of wide receiver depth. If the veteran gets up to speed on Kyle Shanahan's playbook quickly, he could find himself as Brock Purdy's No. 1 WR in Week 10 against a Cowboys secondary that is tied for 25th in fantasy points were game allowed to wideouts, although Allen could also be as low as No. 3 on the chart chart if Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are both able to return from their respective injuries.
outlooksByWeek.11: Keenan Allen is coming off an impactful 49ers debut heading into a Week 11 matchup versus Minnesota. After being acquired by San Francisco at the trade deadline, Allen caught five of seven targets for 61 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. Despite having a relatively short amount of time to learn his new team's offense, Allen looked to have good chemistry with QB Brock Purdy, which is an encouraging sign for his production moving forward. His work as a possession receiver could be especially useful against the Vikings, who own the highest blitz rate in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dak Prescott has thrown four interceptions in his last two games for the Cowboys. While Dak has also thrown for over 250 yards in five-straight outings, he has passed for one touchdown apiece in four consecutive contests. Dallas has lost three of those four games. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus division foe Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dak Prescott tossed multiple touchdowns last game for Dallas for the first time since the middle of September. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Prescott now has 13 touchdowns in seven starts in 2026. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals have also given up the most points per game in the NFL overall to date.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dak Prescott scored two total touchdowns last game for Dallas. However, Prescott passed for one touchdown or fewer for the fifth time in six contests. Dak was also held under 200 yards passing for just the second time in 2026. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dak Prescott posted his third 300-yard passing outing of the season for Dallas in Week 9, throwing for 335 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Colts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in two of the last three contests. However, in Week 10, Prescott will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Francisco has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dak Prescott tied a career high with five touchdown passes last game for Dallas. Unfortunately, the Cowboys defense could not stop a nosebleed, as they fell by a staggering score of 46-40 to the 49ers. Dak also threw for a season-high 343 yards, notching his second-straight 300-yard output overall. Dak has tossed multiple touchdowns in three of the last four contests. In Week 11, Dak will look to keep rolling against a suspect Tennessee pass defense. The Titans are allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jeremiyah Love's second NFL game for the Cardinals will be a tough Week 2 matchup against Seattle. Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his status is uncertain for Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit. The rookie running back logged a full workload Week 4 against the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards and one catch for minus-8 yards. Fantasy managers who roster Love will likely keep a close eye on the Cardinals' injury reports throughout the week to get a sense of his odds of playing in Week 5. If he does suit up, Love will face a Lions defense that allowed Carolina RB Chuba Hubbard to rumble for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jeremiyah Love will look to rebound in Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries against Detroit this past Sunday, and he finished without a catch for the first time as a pro. The rookie continues to lead the Cardinals' ground attack but has managed a meager 3.7 yards per carry through five weeks. The Rams rank 12th in the NFL by giving up 15.5 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jeremiyah Love enters Week 7 with a questionable tag after missing Arizona's Week 6 game against the Rams with an ankle injury. The rookie has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score through five appearances. His 3.7 yards per carry shows room for improvement, though his involvement in the passing game adds fantasy value. Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, creating an attractive matchup if Love returns. However, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight could complicate his workload even if he's cleared to play.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashid Shaheed isn't certain to suit up for Seattle in Week 8 against the Bears. Shaheed injured his knee in Week 7 versus Kansas City, and though initial reports on the injury were promising, it's not clear if he'll need to miss time. The versatile wideout has been pretty quiet as a receiver throughout the campaign, surpassing three receptions just once through seven weeks. That makes him relatively dependent on big plays, and Chicago has given up nine receptions of 40-plus yards this season, most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashid Shaheed will look to return from a knee injury in time to suit up for Seattle's Week 9 battle against Arizona. Shaheed missed the Week 8 loss to Chicago due to the injury, and it's unclear how close he is to returning to action. Should he be able to return to face the Cardinals, he'll have a good opportunity for success against a suspect Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals have given up 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in three-straight games for the Commanders. Stevens connected on two field goals, as well as an extra point, in Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London. In Week 5, Washington will face the first-place New York Giants. New York's defense has been much-improved in 2026, allowing just 19.8 points per tilt, which is eighth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drew Stevens missed an extra point last game for Washington. With the contest resulting in a 27-27 tie, Stevens could have been viewed as the goat. However, late-game clock mismanagement by the offense failed to allow Stevens a chance at redemption, as the Commanders could not get off a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired in overtime. Stevens did hit two other field goals as well as another extra point in the contest. His job should still be safe heading into Week 6 versus the 49ers. However, his opportunities could be limited, as San Fran is yielding just 18.6 points per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in four of six games this season for Washington. However, he has made just 10 field goals the entire year overall, while missing three extra points. In Week 8, the Commanders face the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per contest, which is 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drew Stevens connected on two field goals as well as an extra point last game for the Commanders. Stevens has connected on multiple field goals in six of the last seven outings for Washington.  He has six made field goals in his last two games alone. In Week 10, Stevens will take on a Giants squad allowing 21.5 points per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Drew Stevens managed just one field goal last game for Washington. It was just the third time this season that the kicker for the Commanders failed to boot multiple field goals in a game. However, he did nail all three of his extra-points in the 24-21 win over the Giants. In Week 11, Stevens will face a Bengals squad allowing 21.4 points per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase Brown and the Bengals take on the Falcons for a Week 9 showdown in Spain. He rushed 12 times for 55 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 46 yards during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. Brown lost a fumble but managed to out-touch Samaje Perine 20-5, a good sign for Brown's fantasy outlook. Next up is a Falcons defense allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game (30th) to opposing RBs after giving up 324 rushing yards in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chase Brown and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. In Week 9, he had nine carries for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for another 18 yards to help Cincinnati win a fourth straight game. Brown's production has been somewhat underwhelming from a fantasy perspective, as he's registered just one touchdown across eight outings in 2026. He'll look to find the end zone against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed just four TDs to the position and is coming off a bye.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chase Brown and the Bengals travel to face the Commanders on Monday Night Football. In Week 10, during Cincinnati's victory, he rushed 10 times for 44 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 39 yards and two TDs. Brown finally found paydirt, doing so for the first time since Week 1, while recording his first two receiving scores of the season. He'll look to exploit a Commanders defense that gave up 78 yards and two TDs to Cam Skattebo in their previous outing.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson will look to rebound from a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Jefferson will look to return as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4.
