Jefferson exited Week 3 against the Buccaneers with an ankle injury, but there don't appear to be any concerns beyond a sprain at this point. The star wideout has totaled 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season even in just five halves, and he's been a major piece of Minnesota's 3-0 start. If he is healthy, Jefferson will face a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Jefferson will aim to make a return for Minnesota's Week 5 clash at New Orleans. Jefferson sat out of the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but the hope is that his absences will be limited to that game. The star pass catcher has totaled a quieter 13-179-2 receiving line over his first two-plus games, so he'll look to make a bang if he does return to action. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season, which could provide everything Jefferson needs to deliver.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justin Jefferson remains Minnesota's top target in Week 7 against the Colts. Jefferson put together a solid performance against the Saints in Week 5 before the Vikings' bye, recording six catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The star pass catcher looks to have a solid connection with quarterback Kyler Murray, which could be even more solid after a week of rest. Indianapolis ceded a 6-70-1 receiving line to Titans' WR1 Carnell Tate in Week 6, which could bode well for Jefferson.
outlooksByWeek.8: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Jefferson had a quiet performance out of the bye in Week 7, reeling in four of seven targets for 44 yards, which was his second-lowest yardage total of the year. The star wideout has now pieced together a 23-302-3 receiving line across five games this season. He'll have plenty of chances to carve up a Detroit secondary that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justin Jefferson will aim to ramp up his output as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Week 8 against the Lions, finding the end zone for the fourth time this season. The superstar wide receiver is on pace to finish the season with the fewest catches and yards of his career, and he's yet to record a 100-yard receiving game. Luckily, he'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Justin Jefferson will hope to see better play at the QB position in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Jefferson reeled in just three of his whopping 11 targets for 58 yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. The all-out struggles of Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), were fully seen in Jefferson's receiving line, but the trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins re-united him with the QB he's had the most success with. The talented wideout doesn't have any 100-yard games and has posted less than 60 yards in five of seven games. Jefferson will face a Packers defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Justin Jefferson could be in store for better output again as the Vikings play San Francisco in Week 11. Jefferson benefited from the addition of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, logging season highs in catches (9) and targets (13). The star wideout's 74 yards were also his best total since Week 5, further supporting that he may be in store for a return to dominance. He'll take on a 49ers defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: D'Andre Swift's role will be up in the air heading into Week 8 as the Bears travel to Seattle. Swift produced once again in Week 7, tallying 22 rushes for 78 yards and a touchdown, along with catching four passes for 12 yards. The veteran has benefited from a workhorse role with Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out the last three weeks, finding the end zone four times and averaging over 19 touches per game in that stretch. Monangai could be in line to return this week, but the pair of running backs have proven to both hold value even when both active. Either way, Swift will face a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).
outlooksByWeek.9: D'Andre Swift will look to build on a high-volume performance as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Swift was, for the most part, stymied by a tough Seattle front in Week 8, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry, but he still put together a monster game with three touchdowns and 69 yards off a season-high 27 rushes. The veteran has directly benefited from the absence of position mate Kyle Monangai in the last four weeks, which can especially be seen through his seven touchdowns in that stretch. With or without Monangai active, Swift should have a tough time, especially if he can't find the end zone, against a Tampa Bay front that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: D'Andre Swift will look to bounce back from a tough showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Swift was shelled by a tough Tampa Bay front before Chicago's Week 10 bye, rushing the ball 12 times for 31 yards. The veteran still racked up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games without Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) out, so there is still hope for him to deliver moving forward. Even if Monangai returns, New Orleans ranking 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs could allow for an entire backfield to eat.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bhayshul Tuten scored two receiving TDs against the Texans in Jacksonville's last action prior to a Week 7 bye. The well-rested lead back is a high-end fantasy RB2 for his return to action in Week 8 against the Colts, who are allowing 134 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Tuten is averaging 86 scrimmage yards on 18 touches per game and has scored four total TDs through six outings. His well-rounded skill set gives him a high touch floor regardless of how the game unfolds.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bhayshul Tuten played through foot and ankle injuries in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens. He scored his fifth touchdown in the past three games but was held to a season-low 29 scrimmage yards, less than half of his previous low of 62 yards from Week 2. Tuten has had a few extra days to recover since last Thursday's win and should be ready to assume his usual role as Jacksonville's top RB for a juicy Week 10 road matchup against the Titans, who are allowing 135 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. He profiles as a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 in fantasy for Week 10, especially if his practice participation levels indicate that Tuten's injury scare is behind him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bhayshul Tuten has scored six times during his current four-game TD streak, and he has mustered at least 87 scrimmage yards in seven of Jacksonville's nine games this season. The second-year stud has crept into fantasy RB1 territory ahead of Jacksonville's Week 11 road game against the Giants, who have allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs but also three receiving TDs to the position through nine games. Tuten has five rushing TDs and three receiving scores this season while notching at least 12 carries in every game and two-plus receptions in all but two outings. His well-rounded skill set allows Jacksonville's lead back to maintain a prominent role regardless of the score.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam LaPorta should remain a complementary option as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam LaPorta will look to build on a season-best showing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. LaPorta impressed even in a Week 4 loss to Carolina, reeling in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year tight end has now registered a 22-228-2  receiving line this season, and he remains a consistent option for Jared Goff, especially in important situations. LaPorta will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam LaPorta will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. LaPorta recorded another statement performance in Week 5 over the Cardinals heading into Detroit's bye, bringing in all five of his targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The featured tight end has now surpassed 50 yards in three of his last four games, and he's found the end zone in each of those outings as well. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Sam LaPorta will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. LaPorta was silenced in a Week 7 win over the Packers, catching one of two targets for 18 yards. The starting tight end's performance will hopefully be an anomaly, and he still has a 28-334-3 receiving line through six outings this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. LaPorta had another quiet performance in Detroit's Week 8 win over the Vikings, bringing in three of five targets for 33 yards and logging one rush for two yards. After an impressive stretch heading into a Week 6 bye, the starting tight end has now logged just four catches for 51 yards in the last two weeks. LaPorta will face a Miami defense that's ranked a favorable 30th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. LaPorta was quiet again in Week 9 versus the Dolphins, amid a struggling Detroit passing offense, recording four catches for 32 yards. The starting tight end has totaled just 83 receiving yards in his last three games after going back-to-back weeks with 80-plus receiving yards and a touchdown heading into the Lions' bye. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Sam LaPorta will aim to get back on track as the Lions return home against the Patriots in Week 11. LaPorta has had an extremely dry stretch ever since Detroit's bye week, failing to reach 40 yards in four straight games. The starting tight end has now recorded 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, with most of his volume coming from the first five outings of the season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Parker Washington leads the Jaguars with a 26-416-4 receiving line on 46 targets through the Week 7 bye, and he has a nice opportunity to add to his team-best receiving totals in Week 8 against a Colts defense that may remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf) for a second consecutive game. Indianapolis ranks in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 142 yards per game to the position, though the Colts give up 25.7 points per game overall, ranking among the league's 10 most generous scoring defenses. Washington is on the fantasy WR1/WR2 borderline for this Week 8 home game.
outlooksByWeek.9: Parker Washington has been held to a single catch twice in Jacksonville's last four games but is averaging a team-high 61.7 receiving yards per game and has four TDs through seven games. His occasional down games keep Washington out of the set-and-forget WR1 range, but he's a high-end fantasy WR2 for a Week 9 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Baltimore has given up plenty of yards to the position but has held wideouts to just five TDs. There are numerous mouths to feed in Jacksonville's high-octane passing game, but Washington continues to have the most upside among the team's pass catchers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Parker Washington has had some quiet second halves with the Jaguars building big leads lately, and a similar scenario could be on the table in Week 10 against the 1-8 Titans. Washington remains a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside for this matchup, as Trevor Lawrence's top target should feast as long as this game is competitive against a Titans secondary that has surrendered some big individual performances to WRs, allowing at least 117 yards to six different players this season, including a combined 296 yards and three TDs to Cincinnati's WR duo of Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in Tennessee's most recent game. Washington has failed to exceed two catches in three of his last five games but easily leads the Jaguars with 493 receiving yards and five touchdown catches.
outlooksByWeek.11: Parker Washington capitalized on a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Titans, dissecting Tennessee's league-worst secondary for seven catches, a season-high 152 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Heading into a Week 11 road game against the Giants, Washington leads the Jaguars in all major receiving categories with a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets. He has had some down games with Trevor Lawrence spreading the ball around, as Washington has finished with a single catch on two occasions this season. That lower floor, compared to some of the elite wideouts around the NFL, makes Washington more of a fantasy WR2, but he offers weekly WR1 upside. The Giants are holding wideouts to 127 yards per game but have allowed 11 touchdown catches to the position in nine games.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Purdy and the 49ers will look to remain perfect with a Week 6 win over Washington. Purdy was sacked for the first time this season and threw his first pickoff since Week 1 this past Sunday against Seattle, but he also threw two touchdowns to help guide San Francisco to victory. He was especially synched up with veteran wideout Mike Evans, with whom he connected seven times for 113 yards and a score. Purdy could feast on a Commanders defense that has given up 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most in the NFL) and 27.9 fantasy points per game (second-most in the league) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Purdy and the 49ers travel to take on the Falcons in Week 7. He completed 21 of 29 pass attempts for 264 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Purdy found seven different receivers as the 49ers improved to 6-0 on the season, but it sounds like they could be without Mike Evans (Achilles) for an extended period of time. Purdy will take aim at Atlanta's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Purdy should be well-rested off the 49ers' bye week for a Week 9 clash against Las Vegas. Purdy will be looking to bounce back from his first multi-turnover game of the campaign, as he threw two interceptions in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons. Despite that performance, Purdy still ranks in the top five leaguewide with a 110.1 QB rating in 2026. He could also be getting a big boost Week 9, as injured wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) all have a chance to return from absences. Purdy should be able to find success against the Raiders, who have allowed a 103.2 QB rating this season, third-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brock Purdy will continue to push toward MVP consideration when the 49ers face Dallas in Week 10. Purdy helped San Francisco improve to 7-1 this past Sunday with a win over the Raiders during which he threw for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception despite working without the team's top two wideouts, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Purdy also ran for 40 yards and a score in the victory, and he currently ranks sixth among NFL quarterbacks with 201 rushing yards on the campaign. Even if Evans and/or Samuel remain out for Week 10, the addition of Keenan Allen at the trade deadline should provide him with a reliable fallback option. Purdy is primed for a big day against a Cowboys defense that ranks 25th in the league by allowing a 99.1 quarterback rating this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brock Purdy is coming off one of the best performances of his career as the 49ers prepare to host Minnesota in Week 11. Purdy threw for a career-best 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. The star quarterback now ranks second among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in QB rating (115.2) and has posted an impressive 20:5 TD:INT. However, Purdy faces a tough test in the Vikings, who lead the NFL with 37 sacks and have allowed only six passing touchdowns while recording 10 interceptions.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: KaVontae Turpin continues to flash his versatility for the Cowboys. In addition to his standard role as the primary returner for Dallas, Turpin also rushed for a nine-yard touchdown and even caught a nine-yard pass. Despite this, Turpin remains a boom-or-bust candidate in an offense with so much firepower ahead of him on the depth chart. In Week 4, the Cowboys face a Texans defense allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt through the air, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: KaVontae Turpin remains buried on the depth chart for the Cowboys, at least in terms of receiving. Turpin is the primary returner but has just two catches for 17 yards through four contests. Barring injury, Turpin's impact will mostly be felt on special teams. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KaVontae Turpin saw a season-high four targets last game for the Cowboys.  CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to the additional looks for Turpin. However, Turpin managed just two catches for 22 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Turpin back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: KaVontae Turpin left the last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury, leaving his status in question for Week 7 versus the Eagles. Tyler Goodson handled kick return duties, while Jonathan Mingo caught punts in Turpin's absence. His targets on offense appear to have been gobbled up by No. 3 wideout Ryan Flournoy. If Turpin can return in Week 7, he would face an Eagles defense allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: KaVontae Turpin did not suit up last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury.  Turpin has been more of an ancillary part of the offense even when healthy, as he has just four catches and two carries on the season. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy handle most of the targets from quarterback Dak Prescott.  However, if Turpin somehow can suit up, he could have a favorable matchup if targeted. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: KaVontae Turpin missed last game for Dallas with a rib injury. In fact, it was the second-straight absence for Turpin. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus the Colts. If he can somehow suit up, the Colts defense is allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: KaVontae Turpin has missed each of the last three games for Dallas due to a rib ailment. His status remains up in the air for Week 10 versus the 49ers. If Turpin does suit up, his opportunities will likely be limited against a Niners defense allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: KaVonte Turpin returned from a three-game absence due to a rib ailment, but failed to make much of a mark in the passing game. Turpin was targeted three times, though managed just one catch for 10 yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers in Week 10. Meanwhile, the trio of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy combined for a staggering 38 targets in the high-scoring affair. In other words, Turpin is largely depth at the position, even in Week 11 versus a Titans defense allowing the most passing yards in the NFL per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keaton Mitchell's role in the Chargers' backfield continues to grow. The former Raven handled a season-high 15 touches in a Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, turning them into 63 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton produced 53 yards and a rushing TD on 11 touches, and Kimani Vidal added 36 yards and a receiving score on seven touches. That split points toward offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel moving into a full-blown backfield committee, and while Mitchell's volume has been trending up, he hasn't done much yet to make a case for the No. 1 spot on the depth chart. He'll look to make his own trip to the end zone in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keaton Mitchell is coming off a disappointing Week 5 performance against the Broncos, as he turned nine touches into a modest 29 scrimmage yards. He was outgained by both Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal as the Chargers' backfield devolves into a full committee, but none of the three have made a strong case to seize the clear No. 1 role. Mitchell flashed big-play potential during his time with the Ravens, but working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line won't generate many holes. He'll try to produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keaton Mitchell's usage declined in Week 6, prior to the Chargers' bye. After averaging nearly 12 touches per game in the preceding two weeks, Mitchell had two carries for just four yards, while Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal handled bigger workloads. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is scrambling to find answers, so Mitchell is expected to get more chances to prove he deserves a consistent role. However, so far in 2026, he hasn't produced more than 52 rushing yards or 63 scrimmage yards in a game. In Week 8, he will take on a Rams defense that is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keaton Mitchell remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Omarion Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Mitchell is still looking for his first rushing TD of the season, and his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Keaton Mitchell made a bit of noise as a pass catcher in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, catching three of four targets for 34 yards while turning seven carries into 33 yards. He remains mired in a backfield committee, with Omarion Hampton gaining a team-high 60 rushing yards on 13 carries while Kimani Vidal chipped in 36 scrimmage yards on eight touches. There have been few signs that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will shift away from the arrangement, either due to individual performance or game script, which limits the ceiling of all three backs. Mitchell will try to take advantage of what opportunities he gets in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Keaton Mitchell nearly disappeared from the Chargers' game plan in their first win of the season. During a Week 10 victory over the Ravens, he failed to catch his only target and eked out just four rushing yards on three carries, after handling 17 total touches in the prior two contests. Omarion Hampton, meanwhile, broke out for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, potentially ending the team's backfield committee in decisive fashion. Mitchell will try to make a splash on what touches he gets in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to battle the Buccaneers in Week 6. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Over his last three outings, Boswell is 6-for-7 on field goals while making all eight of his PATs. He's on the fantasy radar with the recent strong performances by the Steelers offense, as they've averaged 29.3 points during this three-game stretch. Boswell will try to make an impact against a Tampa Bay defense allowing 22.4 points per game in 2026, but just 15.0 PPG over their previous two.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 clash against the Saints. He converted four of five field-goal attempts, including a season-long 58-yarder, and both of his PATs during Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. Boswell missed his first kick from 48 yards out, but he made up for it by making four in a row, with three of those makes coming in the fourth quarter to help send the game to OT. He'll get another chance to make an impact versus a New Orleans defense that allows 29.7 points per game, which is tied for the most in the NFL in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Boswell and the Steelers play host to the division rival Browns in Week 8. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory over the Saints in Paris. Boswell is looking to avenge his underwhelming performance against Cleveland in Week 4, as the 35-year-old missed one of two FGAs in the 27-24 defeat. Since then, Boswell is 9-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-7 on extra points. He'll try to keep rolling versus a Browns defense allowing 20.9 points per game, the 12th-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 10 AFC North showdown against the Bengals. In Week 8, he went 2-for-3 on field goal attempts and connected on all three of his PATs to help Pittsburgh win its fourth straight game. Boswell misfired on a 57-yarder to end their first offensive possession, as the 35-year-old is now 4-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards out in 2026. However, he's had three or more FGAs in three consecutive outings, a trend that is likely to continue versus a Cincinnati team scoring the second-most points per game (30.0).
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chris Boswell and the Steelers are back on the road to face the 2-7 Eagles. He connected on his only field goal attempt and lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. The Steelers offense struggled mightily to gain any traction until the game was well out of reach, leaving Boswell on the sidelines while his team opted to go for two on their final touchdown. He'll look to get more involved against a Philadelphia defense giving up 24.6 points per game this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Seth McGowan got seven touches in the Week 4 win over the Commanders, as the Colts built a big enough lead to give Jonathan Taylor some late-game rest for the first time this season. Those seven touches equaled McGowan's touch total from his first three games combined. The rookie seventh-round pick remains a distant second behind Taylor on the Colts' RB depth chart heading into a Week 5 road game against the Steelers. McGowan has minimal standalone fantasy value as long as Taylor is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.6: Seth McGowan has 20 touches for 71 yards through five NFL games with the Colts. The rookie seventh-round pick is a distant second on Indianapolis' RB depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. There is a greater chance than usual of the Colts pulling away and resting Taylor in a Week 6 home game against the 0-5 Titans, but banking on a lopsided game is an unreliable strategy, so McGowan is best left out of fantasy lineups in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Seth McGowan has turned 21 carries and four targets into 98 scrimmage yards through six NFL appearances with the Colts. With starter Jonathan Taylor healthy heading into a Week 7 trip to Minnesota, McGowan projects to remain in a low-volume, change-of-pace role. The rookie seventh-round pick has minimal standalone fantasy potential and isn't a recommended option against the Vikings, who boast the league's stingiest scoring defense at 12.8 points allowed per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Seth McGowan set career highs with 48 scrimmage yards on 12 touches in the Colts' Week 7 loss to Minnesota, but the rookie seventh-round pick has yet to score a TD and is averaging a meager 21 scrimmage yards per game as Jonathan Taylor's backup. McGowan has become a popular fantasy waiver target as the possibility of Taylor being traded comes into focus, but McGowan is nothing more than a speculative bench stash as long as Taylor stays put and is healthy. The rookie's standalone appeal for Week 8 is minimal against a league-best Jaguars run defense that's yielding just 72 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.9: Seth McGowan is averaging fewer than five carries per game while posting just four catches in his first eight NFL games. The rookie seventh-round pick won't be a recommended fantasy option for Week 9 against the Cowboys if it's business as usual in the Colts' backfield, but trade rumors have been brewing around star RB Jonathan Taylor. If Taylor is traded or held out in anticipation of a trade, McGowan or DJ Giddens would be the next man up. Should McGowan garner a starter's workload, he would be a serviceable fantasy RB2 in Week 9 against a dreadful Dallas defense that's allowing 144.5 scrimmage yards per game to RBs and has given up 11 TDs to the position in eight games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Seth McGowan is poised to remain the Colts' No. 2 RB with Jonathan Taylor staying with the team. The rookie seventh-round pick is averaging a solid 4.8 yards per carry, though he has exceeded six rushing attempts in a game just once in his young career. It would have been a juicy introduction to the lead role in a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Dolphins defense that has allowed nine TDs to RBs in eight games en route to a 1-7 record. Now, he's only a deep-league flex option.
outlooksByWeek.11: Seth McGowan set career highs with 12 carries and 77 rushing yards in the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins while scoring a touchdown for the second consecutive game. Indianapolis has deployed McGowan as the 1B option behind Jonathan Taylor over the past couple of weeks, and the rookie seventh-round pick is quietly averaging an impressive 5.2 yards per carry in his young career. McGowan has yet to catch multiple passes in a game and has just nine career receiving yards, so he'll be tough to trust as a flex option, even in deeper formats, until he shows more receiving capabilities. He'll face a Texans defense in Week 11 that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground, limiting RBs to 89 rushing yards per game.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bo Nix contributed most with his legs in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, throwing one TD and running for another. The second score came in the second quarter on a 62-yard scamper, the longest rushing touchdown by a QB in an NFL regular-season game since 2022. Nix's 73 rushing yards on the day nearly doubled his total from the first six weeks combined. Despite that performance, Nix is still on pace for a career-worst campaign, and things won't get easier for him in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bo Nix put together another fourth-quarter comeback in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. While the third-year QB's own numbers are nothing special this season, he's led his team to a 6-2 record and first place in the AFC West. Week 8 was only the second time in eight games he's thrown for multiple touchdowns, and his 59.6% completion rate and 6.0 yards per attempt are both career lows. Nix could be poised for his best game of the season in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bo Nix comes out of the Broncos' bye having built up a bit of momentum, producing multiple touchdowns in three straight games prior to the break while turning the ball over only once during that stretch. The third-year quarterback didn't get any reinforcements at the trade deadline, but the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman in the backfield gives Denver a legitimate running option to help balance the offense, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant returned from IR right before the bye. In Week 11, Nix will take aim at a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are set to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in Cincinnati's 35-13 Week 7 victory. Tee Higgins garnered the same number of looks from Joe Burrow, but Chase turned his into six receptions for 148 yards and a score. The good news is that the concussion appears to be behind Chase, and he'll be ready to exploit a Tennessee defense tied for 24th in fantasy points allowed per game (35.8) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. He brought in 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 8 overtime victory. Chase eclipsed 100 receiving yards for the first time all season while pacing the team in receptions and targets, but fellow wideout Tee Higgins (10-155-2) finished slightly ahead in yardage. Chase owns a 43-492-6 line on 61 targets through seven contests and will look to build upon that versus Atlanta's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Steelers in an AFC North showdown on Sunday Night Football. He caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's 34-17 win in Week 9. Chase led his team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, and he has now turned in two consecutive games with 10-plus catches, 140-plus yards, and a score. Chase will aim to keep rolling against a Pittsburgh defense he burned for a 9-98-1 line on 12 targets back in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals face the Commanders in an interconference clash on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He corralled 11 of 14 targets for a season-high 231 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. After failing to eclipse the 100-yard mark through his first six outings, Chase has done so in three consecutive contests, gaining more than 140 receiving yards in each. He'll take a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets into a matchup against Washington's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Loveland commanded nine targets in Week 4 against the Jets, which allowed him to finish with six catches for 57 yards. The second-year tight end has now increased his yardage from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of the year. He'll aim to find the end zone for the first time of the campaign against a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colston Loveland will look to do more as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Loveland wasn't able to build on a solid six catches for 57 yards in Week 4, reeling in just two of five targets for 19 yards versus the Packers in Week 5. The second-year pass catcher has been thrown to by three quarterbacks of varying skill so far this year, which could add to the struggles of his output. He'll take on an Atalnta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best outing as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 6. Loveland caught six of seven targets for 65 yards and a touchdown in Caleb Williams' return to the field. The second-year tight has now caught six passes in two of his last three games, and he sits in a favorable spot after a rough start to the year. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colston Loveland will aim to continue producing as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Loveland stayed hot in a Week 7 win over New England, finishing with season highs in catches (7), targets (12), yards (69) and tacking on a touchdown. The second-year tight end has had a promising turnaround to the season, with 50 or more yards in three of his last four games and back-to-back outings with a score. He'll face a Seattle defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Colston Loveland will look to remain a high-volume option as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Loveland was solid again in a Week 8 win over the Bears, bringing in seven of nine targets for 65 yards but losing a fumble. The second-year tight end has now brought in six or more receptions in four of his last five games, and he's found the end zone in two of his last three. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Colston Loveland will remain a top option in Chicago's passing game against the Saints in Week 11. Loveland has seen success lately after a shaky start to the season, surpassing 50 yards in his last four games and finding the end zone twice in that stretch. The second-year tight end has now posted a 37-363-2 receiving line off 57 targets in the first nine outings of the season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Waddle caught his second touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but his overall numbers remain disappointing, The former Dolphin has just a 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through eight games, and the struggles of quarterback Bo Nix have prevented Waddle from finding a rhythm in his new offense. Waddle has been targeted 10 or more times only once in those eight games, while last season's No. 1 wide receiver for Denver, Courtland Sutton, handled double-digit targets six times in 2025. Waddle will look for more volume in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' final game before their bye, winding up with just a 22-yard reception on his only target. The former Dolphin has struggled to adjust to his new offense, and through nine games this season he's produced a 30-337-2 line on 52 targets, putting him on pace for a career low in receiving yards.
