Assuming he clears the concussion protocol in time to suit up in Week 11, he'll be facing a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Evans is expected to return from a one-game absence for the 49ers' Week 9 matchup against Las Vegas. Evans was held out of the Week 7 loss to Atlanta due to a lingering Achilles issue, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye enabled him to get some much-needed rest. It still bears monitoring the veteran wideout's practice participation throughout the week, though, as Achilles injuries can be tricky. Should Evans indeed suit up, he'll face a struggling Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game (23.9) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Evans continues to tend to an Achilles injury and is iffy to suit up for San Francisco in Week 10 against Dallas. The injury has prevented Evans from playing in each of the 49ers' past two games despite the team's bye being sandwiched between those contests. Fellow starting wideout Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has also been out, but the 49ers did add depth at the trade deadline by bringing in Keenan Allen. If Evans can return in Week 10, he'll square off against a Cowboys defense that ranks a poor 25th in the league with 23.4 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Evans reportedly has a chance to return from an Achilles injury for San Francisco's Week 11 tilt against the Vikings. Evans has missed the 49ers' past three games while dealing with right Achilles tendinitis. San Francisco recently acquired veteran Keenan Allen to bolster the wideout corps, and Deebo Samuel returned in Week 10 from a multi-game absence caused by a hamstring injury, but Evans' ability to get back on the field would still be a big boost given his chemistry with QB Brock Purdy this season. The 49ers can use all the help they can get on Sunday Night Football, as Minnesota has been tough on opposing passing games this season and has allowed just 16.2 fantasy points per game to wideouts -- fourth-best in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jared Goff will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Goff's story stayed the same in a Week 7 win over the Packers, completing 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in three of six games, and he's also dished out two or more touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll have his biggest test of the season this week, though, as Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jared Goff will aim to return to dominance as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Goff finished Week 8 against a tough Minnesota defense with his worst fantasy performance of the season, completing 18 of 25 passes for 176 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. The veteran quarterback still has excellent figures this year with 1,964 passing yards 15 touchdowns and one pick across seven games. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jared Goff will look to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Goff was stuffed again in a narrow Week 9 win over the Dolphins, completing 17 of 25 passes for just 170 yards with zero touchdowns and an interception. The veteran quarterback has now thrown for a disappointing 346 yards and a 1:2 TD:INT in the last two weeks. He'll face a New England defense that ceded 372 passing yards and three touchdowns to Jordan Love in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jared Goff will aim to take some momentum into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. Goff broke a two-game stretch of struggles in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, completing 65 percent of passes for 303 yards with a 3:2 TD:INT. The veteran has now dished out 18 touchdowns with 2,437 passing yards across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference clash in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for nine yards during Cleveland's 13-10 Week 6 win. Following a three-game stretch in which he recorded a 15-132-3 receiving line on 20 targets, Fannin has now gone two straight outings with one reception and fewer than 10 yards. The second-year TE will try to bounce back versus a Titans defense allowing 10.5 fantasy points per game (T-7th) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns visit the Steelers for an AFC North battle in Week 8. He brought in six of nine targets for 91 yards and also lost a fumble during Cleveland's 27-24 Week 7 win. Fannin finished second behind KC Concepcion (8-129-0 on 10 targets) in receptions, yardage, and targets while setting a new season high in receiving yards. Fannin will look to exploit the Pittsburgh defense again after he recorded a 3-27-1 line against them in a Week 4 victory.
outlooksByWeek.10: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns welcome the Texans to town for a Week 10 AFC clash. He caught both of his targets for 42 yards, including an impressive 39-yard touchdown in overtime, during Cleveland's 23-22 OT loss in Week 9. Fannin was quiet until the extra frame, a disappointing development after he erupted for a 10-154-0 line on 12 targets in his previous outing. He'll look to stay hot despite a difficult matchup versus Houston's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (10.1) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Little has attempted 23 PATs compared to just 12 field goals this season, a testament to Jacksonville's high-octane offense. His ceiling remains immense given the frequent scoring opportunities and Little's elite range, making him a viable fantasy starter for Week 9. Little will face a reeling Ravens team in Week 9 that has dropped three consecutive games while allowing at least 35 points in each of the last two. Overall, Baltimore has given up 16 made field goals in eight games while allowing 25.4 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Little connected on a season-high four field goals in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens, bringing him up to 14-for-16 through eight games this season. He has attempted 10 more PATs than FGs behind Jacksonville's efficient offense, but Little should enjoy plenty of kicking opportunities in Week 10, as the Titans are surrendering 24.9 points per game while the Jaguars are scoring 28.6 points per game. Tennessee has allowed 17 successful field goals, which is tied for 10th most in the NFL, so Little is a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 10.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Little has gone 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts in each of Jacksonville's last two games, with that two-game stretch accounting for nearly half of his 18 made field goals this season. The Jaguars are consistently moving the ball into scoring range, and while they have been adept at scoring TDs rather than settling for FGs, the team's offensive prowess coupled with Little's big leg keeps Jacksonville's kicker safely in the set-and-forget starter range. In Week 11, Little will face the Giants on the road. MetLife Stadium is one of the tougher kicking environments in the NFL, and the Giants' opponents have made just nine field goals in nine games, but the surging Little has the potential to make fantasy managers who over-index on the matchup look silly given his high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonah Coleman had the biggest share of the backfield workload in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, handling 11 touches to J.K. Dobbins' six and RJ Harvey's five. Coleman's 69 scrimmage yards led the trio, but the other two each made trips to the end zone while the rookie RB was held out. It was still an impressive effort in his return from an IR stint due to an ankle injury, and Coleman might be the most likely player from the group to emerge as the lead back. A messy committee is the more probable arrangement, however, heading into a Week 8 clash with a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonah Coleman may be emerging as the Broncos' lead running back. The 2026 fourth-round pick topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in a comeback win over Kansas City in Week 8, and he scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run after getting Denver into the red zone with a 51-yard catch-and-run. J.K. Dobbins logged seven carries, compared to Coleman's 15 total touches, and with RJ Harvey on injured reserve, the path is clear for the rookie to handle a significant workload. Coleman could be headed for a true breakout performance in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonah Coleman captured the No. 1 job in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the team's last two games, the rookie running back amassed 192 scrimmage yards and two rushing TDs, with his yardage split almost equally between the ground and the air. Coleman's usage as a pass catcher could decline once RJ Harvey gets healthy in a couple of weeks, but he's clearly surpassed J.K. Dobbins as the preferred ball carrier in all situations, including at the goal line. Coleman will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omarion Hampton remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Hampton hasn't found the end zone since Week 4, and while he's nominally at the top of the depth chart, his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Omarion Hampton turned 13 carries into a team-high 60 rushing yards in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, his second-highest total of the season. Keaton Mitchell handled 10 touches, and Kimani Vidal got eight, as offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel continues to deploy a backfield committee that limits the ceiling of all three players. Hampton appears to be first among equals for now, but the struggles of the entire offense present an extra obstacle for him to overcome. He'll try to build on last week's modest numbers in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Omarion Hampton is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, topping 100 rushing yards for the first time and scoring his first touchdown since Week 4. It was a big step toward Hampton regaining the clear No. 1 job in the backfield, as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combined for just seven touches and 18 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.9: Devin Duvernay could be in line for an expanded role in Arizona's offense beginning with a Week 9 clash in Seattle. After being limited to special-teams duties over the first seven weeks of the campaign, Duvernay logged a 42% offensive snap share against Dallas in Week 8 and caught both of his targets for 14 yards. Kendrick Bourne suffered a fractured tibia early in that game and will miss the rest of the season, so Duvernay could be asked to take on a larger role in the wideout corps moving forward. However, a matchup against Seattle isn't ideal, as the Seahawks are allowing the fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Devin Duvernay could be called upon to take on a larger role in the Cardinals' Week 10 matchup versus the Rams. Duvernay played only on special teams over the first seven weeks of the campaign, but he's logged over 40% of Arizona's offensive snaps over the past two weeks and has tallied four catches for 22 yards on four targets. He could be asked to do more beginning in Week 10, as both Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are expected to miss the rest of the season. Duvernay faces a tough opponent in the Rams, who have allowed a modest 116.4 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ranking in the top five leaguewide.
outlooksByWeek.11: Devin Duvernay may have an opportunity to seize the No. 1 wideout role for Arizona in Week 11 against Kansas City. Duvernay logged a modest 2-35-0 receiving line this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, but his reception, receiving yardage and target (three) totals all paced Cardinals wideouts. If Duvernay can show continued rapport with rookie quarterback Carson Beck, he could begin to see more than the 29 percent offensive snap share he logged against Los Angeles. With that said, KC is a tough draw, as its secondary has given up the second-fewest receptions per game (10.1) to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Stafford will try to help the Rams move above .500 for the first time this season with a win in Week 9 against Washington. Stafford was pretty quiet against the Chargers this past Sunday, throwing for just 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception, but his performance was good enough to lead his team to a second straight victory. The veteran quarterback continues to rely heavily on star wideout Puka Nacua with Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to remain sidelined for multiple more games. Stafford has a prime matchup against the Commanders, who have given up the third-most fantasy points per game (24.6) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Stafford will have to operate without his favorite target in the Rams' Week 10 tilt against Arizona. Puka Nacua, who Stafford has targeted at least 10 times in five of his past six games, has a knee injury that is expected to require a stint on IR. The Rams are also still without Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), so Stafford will have to look to other wideouts, as well as the tight-end corps, more often moving forward. He'll at least have a promising matchup in Week 10, as the Cardinals have allowed the third-most fantasy points (23.9) to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson has underwhelmed relative to his usual standards over the last two weeks, accounting for 175 total yards and no touchdowns on 36 touches. Despite the lack of scoring, Robinson has still managed to accumulate 4.3 yards per carry during that span. It will likely be tough for Robinson to have a bounce-back performance in Week 8 as well, with Tampa Bay's defense allowing just 18.2 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Bijan struggled along with the rest of the Falcons' offense in a Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, rushing 19 times for 76 yards while failing to haul in his lone target. Despite this poor performance, Robinson ranks third in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and fifth in total yards per game (122.9), so the production will likely follow. He's could thrive against a Bengals defense that just allowed Tony Pollard to account for 137 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Titans.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Robinson was one of Atlanta's few bright spots during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, accumulating 147 yards and a touchdown on 25 touches. The Texas product is currently averaging the third-most touches per game (22.2) in the NFL, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs despite a tough matchup. Kansas City's defense has given up just 20.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through eight games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.10: Jordyn Tyson's role in the Saints' offense is expected to continue growing during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Tyson was sidelined for New Orleans' first seven games this season due to a hamstring. He was relatively underwhelming in his NFL debut, catching four of five targets for 30 yards while also losing a fumble in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns. Despite this, Tyler Shough is tied for the league-lead in pass attempts per game (38.5) and Tyson is expected to get more involved in the Saints' offense as the season continues, so his fantasy outlook remains positive. He could find success against a depleted Carolina secondary that's given up 145.6 receiving yards per game to opposing WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordyn Tyson will look to build on his breakout performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Tyson was one of New Orleans' few bright spots in the Week 11 loss to the Panthers, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in his second NFL game. He's clearly established himself as one of the Saints' top two receiving options but could struggle if Chris Olave is more involved in Week 11. Tyson could thrive against a solid Bears secondary, however, as they have allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Luther Burden will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Burden stayed hot in a Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, bringing in seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets across the last three games, and he's surpassed 50 receiving yards in all but two games this season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Luther Burden will aim to recover from a concussion ahead of Chicago's Week 11 game against the Saints. Burden got concussed in the fourth quarter of a Week 9 win over the Buccaneers before the Bears' bye week, so hopefully he's had enough time to heal. The second-year star has now posted a 49-644-4 receiving line across nine games with career highs in catches and touchdowns, with one more game likely to get him over the hump in yards as well. If he's active, Burden will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked a tough eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Patrick Mahomes is coming off one of the worst performances of his career in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. The two-time MVP threw for a season-low 165 yards with zero touchdowns and failed to get his team into the red zone for the first time in 153 career starts, including regular season and playoffs. With his wide receiver room thinned by injuries, Mahomes is again having a tough time stretching the field or taking advantage of a defense's focus on Kenneth Walker. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos defense playing below expectations, which sits tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Patrick Mahomes bounced back from a two-game touchdown drought to throw three TDs in Week 8, but it wasn't enough as Kansas City lost to the Broncos and ceded first place in the AFC West. Despite a lack of consistent help at wide receiver, something that could be addressed at the trade deadline, Mahomes is on pace for his best passing yards total since 2021. With a 12:4 TD:INT ratio through seven games, he could produce 30-plus touchdowns for the first time since 2022. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Patrick Mahomes put together another strong performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, completing 74.2% of his 31 pass attempts with two touchdowns and zero interceptions, but he suffered an elbow injury during the contest. He finished the game, but the team is awaiting the results of testing to determine the severity. For now, Mahomes has been deemed day-to-day. If he's cleared to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Falcons defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs but just traded starting safety Jessie Bates. If Mahomes is held out, Justin Fields would get his first start of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Patrick Mahomes is coming off a huge performance in a Week 10 win over the Falcons, as he threw five touchdown passes for the first time since Week 1 of the 2022 season. The trade-deadline addition of Josh Downs revitalized the passing game, as four different Kansas City players had receptions of 30-plus yards. Mahomes has a 10:0 TD:INT ratio over the last three games with two 300-yard performances, giving him significant momentum heading into a Week 11 clash with a Cardinals defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Spencer Shrader has emerged as an elite fantasy kicker through five weeks, converting all 12 of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last three games. He's 16-for-16 overall this season, including a perfect 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Indianapolis' offense generated plenty of field-goal opportunities in the first half of last season before falling off a cliff in the second half, so the risk of regression is substantial. However, Shrader has an excellent opportunity to keep rolling in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who have allowed 13 field goals through five games, tied with Pittsburgh for the most in the NFL. Keep starting Shrader if you have him.
outlooksByWeek.7: Spencer Shrader has been one of the few bright spots for the 2-4 Colts, converting all of his league-high 18 field-goal attempts through six weeks, including six from beyond 50 yards. His lone blemish on the season is a missed extra point. Indianapolis could struggle to consistently reach scoring range in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game, but Shrader has been too good recently to bench, and the Colts could find themselves kicking more field goals than PATs once again in this difficult matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made (19) and attempted (21), but he was just 1-for-3 in the Week 7 loss to Minnesota after starting 18-for-18 through six games. The Colts' kicker will attempt to bounce back in Week 8 against the Jaguars, who boast the league's third-stingiest scoring defense, allowing just 17.3 points per game. Shrader has earned some goodwill from fantasy managers with his hot start, but he could find himself back on the waiver wire before long if the misses start to pile up.
outlooksByWeek.9: Spencer Shrader is quickly losing his luster as the reeling Colts continue to struggle on offense. He still leads the league with 19 made field goals, but Shrader has slowed down significantly after an 18-for-18 start through Week 6. Shrader has gone just 1-for-3 on field goal attempts over the past two games while the Colts have been outscored 58-17 in that span. It's tempting to cut bait given his recent downturn, but fantasy managers should give Shrader one more chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Cowboys, who are giving up 26.6 points per game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made and attempted, even with his volume and effectiveness dropping off in recent weeks as the 2-7 Colts continue to struggle as a team. He's 22-for-24 this season but just 4-for-6 over the past three games. Indianapolis faces a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed 15 made field goals in eight games and 25.0 points per game. If you have Shrader on your roster, you may as well keep starting him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Spencer Shrader has made no more than one field goal in three of the last four games. His recent downturn has knocked Shrader out of first place in field goals made and attempted, though he's still top-three in both categories thanks to a torrid start that has the Colts' kicker at 23-for-25 through 10 games. That strong start included a 4-for-4 Week 3 performance against the Texans, whom Shrader will face again in Week 11. The Colts' offense has been depleted by a few trades and will likely struggle to generate consistent kicking opportunities moving forward, but Shrader is viable in Week 11 since Houston ranks in the middle of the pack with 24.3 points allowed per game and 18 made field goals against. If you see an enticing alternative on your league's waiver wire, it may be time to move on from Shrader.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: CeeDee Lamb is said to be dealing with a bruise of his quadriceps, but he is not expected to miss any time for the Cowboys. Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards last game as he was dealing with the issue. That snapped a three-game streak for Lamb of at least 112 yards receiving. He will look to get back on track in Week 6 versus the Packers. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: CeeDee Lamb was targeted a staggering 18 times last game for Dallas. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly had a difficult time. Despite the bevy of looks, Lamb managed just 70 yards on nine catches in the 23-13 loss. Lamb has an absurd 44 targets over his last three contests. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: CeeDee Lamb scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Lamb led the Cowboys receivers in all categories, snagging five passes for 74 yards and the two touchdowns. He has found the end zone six times in seven contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: CeeDee Lamb led the Cowboys in receiving last game. Unfortunately, he managed just 58 yards and failed to find the end zone in the 33-30 OT loss to Arizona. Lamb has accumulated a staggering 41 targets over the last three contest, though has failed to cross 75 yards receiving in any of those contests. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: CeeDee Lamb took advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. While Lamb is always the top target in the offense, with Pickens out of the lineup Lamb was targeted even more frequently than usual, a total of 16 times against the Colts. Lamb responded with 10 catches for a staggering 195 yards and a touchdown. Lamb has double-digit targets in four-straight games, and Pickens remains questionable for the Week 10 clash with the 49ers. However, the Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: CeeDee Lamb continues to pile up statistics for the Dallas Cowboys. Lamb found the end zone for the second-straight game and eighth time overall in 2026 in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Lamb finished with seven catches for 72 yards and the score. Lamb has drawn double-digit targets in five-straight contests, a trend that should continue in Week 11 versus the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127.
