Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Travis Kelce made history again in Week 7, moving into fifth place on the NFL's all-time reception list with 1,104 as Kansas City fell to the Seahawks. The veteran tight end remains Patrick Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, and through six games, Kelce's delivered a 24-343-2 line on 35 targets. The 37-year-old is no longer as dangerous with the ball in his hands, but he can still move the chains consistently. Kelce will take on a Broncos defense in Week 8 that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Travis Kelce caught five of seven targets for 67 yards in Kansas City's Week 8 loss to the Broncos, his best performance since delivering a 9-101-1 line in Week 2. The veteran tight end remains one of Patrick Mahomes' most trusted options, and Kelce has a shot at his first 1,000-yard effort since 2022 if he can maintain his current pace. He could be poised for solid numbers again in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Kelce produced his highest yardage total since Week 2 in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, hauling in four of six targets for a team-high 72 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2021 on a one-yard plunge. Kelce has delivered a 33-482-2 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his outlook would suffer if Patrick Mahomes ends up missing time due to an elbow injury he picked up against the Jets. Regardless of who's under center, Kelce will face a Falcons defense in Week 10 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Kelce is coming off his least productive game of the season, catching both his targets for 30 yards in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons. The veteran tight end hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 3, and he hasn't hauled in more than five passes or 72 receiving yards since Week 2, but his role as Patrick Mahomes' most reliable security blanket gives him a fairly secure floor. Kelce will look to make a bigger contribution in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: KC Concepcion and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a Week 8 divisional clash. He caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and had three carries for another 23 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 7. The rookie broke out with season highs in receptions, yardage and targets while leading the Browns in every category. Concepcion will aim to score his first touchdown of his career versus the Steelers 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for the first time since Week 6 to host the Texans. He grabbed four of six targets for 85 yards, including a 64-yard touchdown, during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. The score was the rookie wideout's first of his young career, and he now sports a 37-437-1 receiving line on 55 targets to go along with 10 carries for 37 yards through nine games. Concepcion will aim to take advantage of a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for a divisional clash in Week 7. He rushed 17 times for 58 yards and caught his lone target for two yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6, also losing a costly fumble in the fourth quarter. The outing marked Henry's first this season without a touchdown, and his 60 scrimmage yards were his lowest output through six games. He will aim to bounce back at home in Week 7 versus a Cincinnati defense that allows 19.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.8: Derrick Henry and the Ravens aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they visit Buffalo in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 45 yards and caught one of two targets for four yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Henry has averaged fewer than 3.5 yards per carry (YPC) in two straight outings, rushing 34 times for 103 yards (3.0 YPC) during that stretch. He'll look to turn things around versus a Bills defense allowing 28.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 29th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Derrick Henry and the Ravens hope to snap a three-game losing streak when they host the Jaguars in Week 9. He had 11 carries for 53 yards and Baltimore's lone TD while catching both of his targets for seven yards during Week 8's 36-10 loss. Henry has failed to top 60 rushing yards since Week 5, and things likely won't be any easier for him moving forward with Lamar Jackson (thumb) possibly done for the season. Henry will face a Jaguars defense that ranks second-best in the league at defending opposing RBs, allowing 17.3 fantasy points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Chargers to town for a Week 10 clash on Monday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 57 yards and did not record a target during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Henry has struggled mightily over his last four outings, gaining 213 yards on 62 carries (3.4 yards per carry) with just one touchdown. Jacoby Brissett, who's expected to start under center in Week 10, should provide some relief for the passing game, so the hope is that this will begin to have a positive effect on Henry.
outlooksByWeek.11: Derrick Henry and the Ravens take to the road in Week 11 to battle the 4-5 Panthers. In Baltimore's Week 10 loss, he rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 10 yards. Henry was able to salvage an otherwise miserable outing with two scores, the 32-year-old's ninth and tenth rushing TDs on the season. The Ravens attempted 49 passes with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center. The hope is that Brissett will allow Henry more breathing room between the tackles versus Carolina's 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (27.3) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Barion Brown will likely have minimal offensive impact in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Brown played just seven offensive snaps in his NFL debut, suggesting he's clearly behind fellow rookie Bryce Lance (62 snaps) in the Saints' receiving corps. With Tyler Shough attempting 56 passes in the Week 1 loss, it's tough to imagine a better scenario for Brown to make an impact as well. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup against a Ravens defense that's given up just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Barion Brown is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Brown has logged just nine offensive snaps through New Orleans' first two games, suggesting he's not a part of head coach Kellen Moore's offensive game plan. It appears as if the rookie's primary role is in the return game, as he's accumulated 34 punt-return yards and 128 kick-return yards already. Additionally, Brown is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 6.8 yards per pass attempt thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Barion Brown (hamstring) is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Brown was sidelined for the Week 3 loss but played a minimal offensive role prior to his absence, rushing once for three yards on nine offensive snaps. He's firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in New Orleans' WR room but will likely contribute on special teams when healthy. Despite this, Brown is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons secondary that's given up 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Barion Brown is expected to remain largely uninvolved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Brown has played just five offensive snaps over his last three games, suggesting he's assumed more of a special-teams role early in the season. The rookie wideout is expected to remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes unless finding the end zone in the near future. Additionally, he's in for a tougher matchup against a Giants defense that's given up 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Barion Brown is expected to remain a depth option in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Brown played a season-high 25% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the Week 6 win over the Giants, catching his lone target for five yards. Despite this, he remains firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in the WR room and likely won't be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, Brown is in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 6.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.9: Barion Brown is expected to play a reserve role in the Saints' receiving corps during the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Brown caught a career-high three passes for 57 yards in the Week 7 loss to the Steelers, which could suggest his role is growing in New Orleans' offense. However, Brown remains firmly behind both Chirs Olave and Devaughn Vele in the team's WR room, so he'll likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. He could find the end zone in Week 9, however, as the Cleveland's defense has allowed seven touchdowns to opposing WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance. He'll begin the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.9: Corey Kiner has had a minimal role in the Patriots' backfield entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Kiner has rushed for 38 yards or more in three of the last four games, despite Rhamondre Stevenson leading the way in touches and TreVeyon Henderson factoring in when healthy. If Henderson were sidelined again in Week 9, Kiner may still not gather enough volume to be an option against a defense that's allowing 3.96 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.10: Corey Kiner could be in line for a significant role for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions, with both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) uncertain to play. While Detroit is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing backs, volume remains king, and Kiner could serve as the No. 1 RB for Week 10 in Munich. Kiner figures to be a popular play in what could be a high-scoring game, despite Detroit allowing just 3.9 yards per carry.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyren Williams will likely continue to share the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against Washington. Williams tallied a modest 56 yards on 16 carries against the Chargers in a win this past Sunday, but he managed to get into the end zone for the fifth time over his past five games. He's faced competition for carries of late from Blake Corum, who has tallied 28 totes for 166 yards and two TDs over the past two weeks. Both Williams and Corum could battle for running room against the Commanders, who are yielding just 3.63 yards per carry to running backs, which ranks seventh-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kyren Williams may be asked to log a heftier workload than usual for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Williams rushed for just 45 yards -- his second-lowest mark of the season -- on 15 carries against Washington in Week 9, adding 16 yards on three catches. However, Los Angeles is going to be without wideout Puka Nacua (knee) for multiple weeks, and with Davante Adams (hamstring) still on IR, the team may turn more to its ground game  -- led by Williams and Blake Corum -- to carry the load. Arizona's defense has been middling against the run this season, allowing 18.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, tied for 18th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the Buccaneers' main offensive weapon in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Irving was largely ineffective against the Packers in a Week 4 loss, rushing for 61 yards on 16 carries. Additionally, the Oregon product was held without a target after accumulating 15 in Tampa Bay's first three games, suggesting Irving is likely in for less pass-catching opportunities while Jalon Daniels remains the starting quarterback. Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Irving was phenomenal in the Week 5 upset win over the Cowboys, totaling 175 yards and two touchdowns on 23 touches. Despite this, Irving is seeing less receiving work since Jalon Daniels took over for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback, getting just three targets over his last two games. Even so, Irving should remain productive in Week 6 against a Steelers defense that's allowed 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was relatively quiet in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, totaling 49 yards on 22 touches. Despite this, he remains firmly ahead of Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker in Tampa Bay's backfield and could thrive in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has allowed 25.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season. Additionally, Irving could benefit from the possible return of quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), as Irving averaged 5.0 targets per game while Mayfield was healthy (just 2.0 since Mayfield's injury).
outlooksByWeek.8: Bucky Irving will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Irving carried the load for Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing for 106 and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for four yards. Irving has been the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense over the last three weeks, averaging 111.3 total yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game during that span. He's in for a very favorable Week 8 matchup as well, with Atlanta's defense allowing 26.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has rushed for over 100 yards in three of his last four games, averaging a whopping 121.8 rushing yards per game during that span. He now ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards per game (91.0) while scoring six total touchdowns in eight appearances this season. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is expected to continue leaning on the run game, which has led the Buccaneers to a 3-1 record over the last four weeks-a positive sign for Irving's outlook. However, he is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Chicago defense that has given up just 18.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through seven contests this year
outlooksByWeek.11: Bucky Irving will likely remain the focal points of the Buccaneers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Irving has carried Tampa Bay's offense throughout the season, ranking sixth in the NFL in touches per game (21.0) and 10th in total yards per game (103.4). However, head coach Todd Bowles said that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following the team's Week 10 bye, suggesting he could see less work going forward. Additionally, Irving may struggle in Week 11 against a Lions defense that's held opposing running backs in check this season, allowing just 17.5 fantasy points per game.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
outlooksByWeek.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Garrett Wilson seeks a rebound in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns. After collecting seven or more targets in each of his first three games, Wilson bottomed out with only four looks in Week 4, finishing with a season-low 27 yards. Cleveland's secondary has allowed at least 291 passing yards in each of the last two weeks, and three opposing wideouts have topped 70 yards. With his usual volume, Wilson appears to be in a favorable Week 5 spot.
outlooksByWeek.6: Garrett Wilson commands a heavy volume of targets in the Jets' passing game heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Wilson collected 11 looks in Week 5, topping 100 yards for the second time this season, and has now garnered at least seven targets in four of five outings. New England's secondary is banged up, and the availability of star CB Christian Gonzalez remains uncertain. While the Jets don't want to pass heavily, when they do, targets should be funneled toward Wilson. He has a great chance to exploit a defense that has allowed two 100-yard receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Garrett Wilson plays a steady role in the Jets' middling passing game and enters a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson managed just 44 yards in Week 6, his second-lowest output of the year, but still enters Week 7 with seven or more targets in four of his first six games. Miami has been stingy against wideouts, allowing just two touchdown catches and only two receivers to record more than 55 yards, but Wilson's volume should allow him to flirt with the upper end of that production.
outlooksByWeek.8: Garrett Wilson's high-volume role has faded over the last two weeks as the Jets prepare to host the Raiders in Week 8. After recording 57 or more yards in four of his first five games, Wilson has just 70 total yards over the last two weeks, coinciding with Omar Cooper's emergence. While the Raiders are allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts, smaller, shifty receivers have given them fits (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Xavier Worthy), suggesting Wilson carries ample volatility into Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Garrett Wilson's usage has been inconsistent ahead of the Jets' difficult Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs. After showing frustration following a three-target Week 7, Wilson was peppered with 12 looks in Week 8-the third time he's amassed double-digit targets. However, he's drawn only 27 total looks in the Jets' other five games. Kansas City has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers but was without corners Mansoor Delane and L'Jarius Sneed in Week 8. Week 9 absences would help Wilson's potential.
outlooksByWeek.10: Garrett Wilson needs to clear the concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Bills in Week 10. Wilson has seen sporadic usage when healthy, amassing double-digit targets three times while averaging 5.8 looks in five additional outings. Assuming he receives a clean bill of health, he'll face a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts. With the Jets likely falling into an early hole, a pass-heavy game flow is probable, with Wilson being an active participant.
outlooksByWeek.11: Garrett Wilson continues to dominate targets in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. He garnered a season-high 14 targets in Week 10, his fourth outing with double-digit looks, while topping 100 yards for the third time. Wilson has only three touchdowns on the year and faces a bit of quarterback uncertainty with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury, but the Chargers have allowed 11 receivers to score in nine games and have surrendered 340-plus passing yards in consecutive weeks. With steady volume, Wilson profiles as a safe lineup cog in Week 11.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for eight yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Judkins returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury and posted his best performance of the year, setting season highs in rush yards and yards from scrimmage (104). He'll aim to stay hot against a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to face the Saints in Week 9. He rushed 11 times for 25 yards and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during Cleveland's 27-6 Week 8 loss. Judkins handled 11 of 12 carries out of the backfield but took a backseat to Dylan Sampson in the passing game. Judkins will aim to bounce back against a New Orleans defense that ranks last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.8) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns return home for the first time in three weeks to host the Texans. He rushed 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards during Cleveland's overtime loss in Week 9. Judkins and the entire Browns offense struggled to make much happen on the ground, registering 95 yards on 34 carries for a meager 2.8 yards per attempt. Judkins has been underwhelming in 2026, racking up 385 yards on 116 carries (3.3 YPC) with three TDs and a 22-136-0 receiving line on 25 targets. He'll try to turn things around versus a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Gainwell was given few opportunities in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, accumulating 24 total yards on just three touches. Additionally, Gainwell was on the field for just 15% of Tampa Bay's offensive plays, his lowest mark of the season. It appears as if Gainwell is trending toward receiving less work as the season progresses, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed 5.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Gainwell had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing 14 times for 88 yards. Despite his productive day, Gainwell still tallied 10 fewer carries than Bucky Irving (24 rushes for 106 yards and two touchdowns), suggesting he remains firmly behind Irving in Tampa Bay's backfield. However, Gainwell could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's given up 10 total touchdowns to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenny Gainwell will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He racked up a career-high 140 rushing yards on 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Falcons, bringing his season total to 289 yards (5.0 yards per carry). Despite Gainwell's huge performance, he still remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. Gainwell could struggle, especially against a strong Bears defense that has allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs all season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Despite Gainwell playing behind Bucky Irving, he's tallied 304 yards from scrimmage over the Buccaneers' last three games. Additionally, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday that the team will aim to lessen Irving's workload going forward, suggesting Gainwell's role on the offense could expand as the year progresses. However, Gainwell may struggle against the Lions in Week 11, as the Detroit has allowed just 3.7 yards per carry to opposing running backs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rachaad White has scored in back-to-back games for Washington. White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. White has found the end zone in each of the last two contests since taking over the starting running back job for the injured Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Jeremy McNichols also left this game with an injury, leaving Austin Ekeler as the only other healthy option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rachaad White continues to operate as the top back for the Commanders, though has found little room to roam on the ground. White has failed to rush for more than 55 yards in any game this season. However, he does have at least two receptions in three-straight contests. In Week 10, White will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rachaad White is averaging at least four yards per carry over his last three games with the Commanders. Though White is technically the starting running back, he has only had double-digit carries twice this season. Moreover, Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return soon from Injured Reserve. For now, though, White remains the top dog in the backfield heading into a Week 11 clash with the Bengals. Cincy has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. The Bengals are allowing 123.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.7: Myles Price will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Price mostly contributed on special teams to start the season, but he's seen an uptick in usage, with five catches for 45 yards in his last two outings. While more targets will be needed to make him an attractive target beyond his return abilities, he's worth keeping an eye on, especially against an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Myles Price remains a depth option heading into Minnesota's Week 8 matchup at Detroit. Price didn't log a full game in Week 7 against the Colts as he was being evaluated for a concussion, and this translated to zero targets. The sophomore remains a return guru at this point in the season, but it remains to be seen if his five catches for 26 yards across Weeks 4 and 5 before Minnesota's bye were a fluke. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Myles Price will remain a depth option in the passing game in Minnesota's travel to Green Bay in Week 10. Price reeled in one of four targets for six yards in the Vikings' Week 9 loss to the Bills, which was his first grab since Week 5. The second-year wide receiver has now recorded six catches for 32 yards this campaign. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Myles Price could benefit from an uptick in usage again as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. With teammates Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) both out in Week 10, Price caught four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown and rushed the ball once for 12 yards, which were all season highs or tied season highs. With Addison set to be out for multiple weeks and Jennings not showing much when on the field, Price could be the flashy target opposite Justin Jefferson that Minnesota needs. Price look to keep his success going against a San Francisco defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to his position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Aaron Jones will aim to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jones shook off a knee injury and ended up playing in Week 8 against the Lions, but he logged a season-low five carries and 22 rushing yards, with two catches for 18 yards as well. The veteran's output moving forward is likely to remain capped with Jordan Mason sharing the backfield, but the pair could carve out some success versus a Buffalo defense that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Aaron Jones will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Jones saw just five carries and one target in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, and he took them for 16 yards and five yards, respectively. The veteran running back has now seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, logging 18 carries in total during that stretch. He's not likely to see crazy value with Jordan Mason active, but a Green Bay defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.11: Aaron Jones will look to build off a solid showing as the Vikings travel to San Francisco in Week 11. Jones did well against his former squad in Week 10, logging 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, along with catching one pass for eight yards. The veteran remains in a timeshare with Jordan Mason, but he still holds some value moving forward. The 49ers have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Allgeier may be lined up for a big role for Arizona in Week 5 against the Lions. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and if he can't suit up Sunday, Allgeier will likely lead the team's backfield. Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's backfield seems to be fading ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Allgeier logged just three carries for seven yards this past Sunday against Detroit while adding nine yards on two catches. The veteran running back has logged three or fewer totes two of the past three weeks and seems to be far behind rookie Jeremiyah Love, who got 12 carries versus the Lions, in the pecking order. With that said, he could get some opportunities as a pass catcher against the Rams, who have given up the fourth-most receiving yards per game (42.6) to running backs through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Allgeier could continue handling a significant share of Arizona's backfield workload in Week 7 against Denver, regardless of whether Jeremiyah Love remains sidelined with an ankle injury or returns after a one-game absence. Allgeier has rushed 53 times for 157 yards and a touchdown through six games, but he's averaging just 3.0 yards per carry, so he needs to be more efficient when he gets the ball. Bam Knight's emergence adds another obstacle to consistent fantasy production. However, Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, so Allgeier should have flex appeal if he has an expanded role for a second consecutive week.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's background is looking shaky ahead of a Week 8 battle in Dallas. Rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice this week and could return from a two-game absence, which would likely push Allgeier down in the pecking order. Even if Love doesn't return, Bam Knight has outperformed Allgeier during Love's absence and could take over the lead-back role. Still, Allgeier at least has a good matchup, as the Cowboys rank 25th in the league in giving up 4.36 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Allgeier may be asked to log a heavy workload for the Cardinals in Week 9 against Seattle. Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) are both dealing with injuries, leaving Allgeier to potentially carry the run game on his shoulders versus the Seahawks. Allgeier thrived with that responsibility this past Sunday in an overtime win over Dallas, logging 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five catches. However, he could find the sledding tougher against a Seattle defense that is allowing just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, the second-best mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Allgeier should remain Arizona's lead RB against the Rams in Week 10. Allgeier took on that role this past Sunday in a loss to Arizona and finished with 46 yards on 17 carries along with zero yards on two catches while drawing three targets. It was a quiet performance against a premier defense, but Allgeier seems likely to continue to lead the Cardinals' backfield while Jeremiyah Love (ankle) remains sidelined. Allgeier faces another tough draw in Week 10, as the Rams have yielded the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (14.2) to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Allgeier and the Cardinals will face a tough Kansas City defense in Week 11. Allgeier struggled in this past Sunday's loss to the Rams, gaining only 14 yards on five carries and failing to catch his only target.
