What's more, he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share despite the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who's slated to miss several more weeks. Allgeier may be splitting backfield work with Bam Knight against a sturdy KC run defense that is yielding the second-fewest yards per carry (3.46) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Pickens was held to just 48 yards receiving last game for Dallas. This was his lowest receiving total since the second week of the season. Pickens has just 10 targets combined over the last two games and was seen leaving the field early following the OT loss to Arizona, meaning there could be trouble in paradise. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Pickens did not suit up last game for Dallas due to a hamstring ailment. His status for Week 10 versus the 49ers remains up in the air. Even if Pickens is able to play, he will face a difficult task. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: George Pickens snagged three touchdowns last game for the Cowboys. Pickens racked up an incredible 18 targets, parlaying those looks into 11 grabs for 145 yards and the three scores. The targets and receptions set career highs, while the yardage total was his best on the season. In Week 11, Pickens has a delectable matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Daniels could return in Week 5 for the Commanders from a dislocated elbow. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left Washington's last game with a knee injury, which could hasten the need for Daniels to return versus the Giants. if neither quarterback can suit up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would get the nod. The defense for the Giants looks totally revamped in 2026, allowing 205.3 yards per tilt through the air, which is 10th in the league. The Giants are tied for the league-lead with six interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Daniels returned from injury and appeared to show no ill effects regarding his previously dislocated elbow. Daniels rushed for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, while also passing for 199 yards against the Giants. Unfortunately, poor game management at the end of overtime cost the Commanders the win, and overshadows what was otherwise a solid return to the lineup for Daniels. Unfortunately, a tall task lurks in Week 6 on the road versus the 49ers. San Francisco is undefeated and allowing just 297.2 scrimmage yards per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jayden Daniels produced one of his best games of the season before the bye for the Commanders, and will look to build off of that performance in Week 8 versus the Eagles.  Daniels completed 72.5-percent of his passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a narrow loss to the 49ers. In fact, it was the first time in 2026 that Daniels threw for even 200 yards in a contest. Daniels will face an Eagles defense that has been better against the run than the pass this season.  Philadelphia is allowing 244.5 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.  However, Philadelphia is still surrendering 119.3 yards per game on the ground, which is just 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jayden Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in each of the last two games for Washington. He also has three touchdown passes over that span. However, in Week 9, Daniels will face a stellar Rams pass defense.  Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jayden Daniels threw for 274 yards and a touchdown last game for Washington. He has passed for at least one touchdown in three-straight outings, and thrown for at least 270 yards in two of those three contests. In Week 10, he will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league, and Daniels ran for 103 yards and two scores when the two teams met earlier this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jayden Daniels tossed three touchdown passes last game for the Commanders. He also threw his first two interceptions of the season in the thrilling 24-21 win over the Giants. Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in four-straight contests. He may be more successful with his legs than with his arm in Week 11 versus the Bengals, though. Cincinnati is allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. By contrast, Cincy is surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Javonte Williams was largely held in check last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 56 yards rushing on 24 carries. He was also held out of the end zone for just the second time all season. The workload remains stellar, though, as Williams now has a staggering 49 carries in the last two contests alone. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Javonte Williams got back into the end zone last game for Dallas. Williams scored his ninth rushing touchdown of the season in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Williams also crossed the 100-yard rushing plateau for the second time in 2026. Williams has at least 20 carries in each of the last three outings. However, in Week 10, he will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 80.9 rushing yards per game, which is second in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Javonte Williams was held out of the end zone for the second time in three games for the Cowboys. Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Williams was also held under 65 yards rushing for the second time in three contests. However, his usage remains high, as he has received double-digit carries in every game in 2026. In Week 11, Williams will face a Titans squad that has been lackluster against the run. Tennessee is allowing 124 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 22nd in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 9 matchup versus the Raiders well-rested following his team's Week 8 bye. Kittle had his snaps managed each of the first two weeks following his January surgery to repair a torn Achilles tendon, but amid multiple injuries to the 49ers' WR corps, the star tight end logged at least an 85% offensive snap share (and at least six targets) in each of his past five games. San Francisco could get multiple of the injured wideouts back for Week 9, but Kittle should still be a big part of the passing game, as he ranks fifth among NFL tight ends with a 22.4% target share this season. He'll face a Las Vegas defense that has given up eight touchdowns to tight ends, tied for second-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Kittle's health and productivity have been huge this season for the 49ers heading into a Week 10 tilt against Dallas. After undergoing surgery in January to repair a torn Achilles, Kittle has played in every one of San Francisco's games this season and leads the club with 38 receptions, 483 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns. His role in the passing game has been especially important of late, as Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined due to injuries, and the addition of veteran possession receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline isn't likely to impact Kittle's routes down the seams. Kittle will look to find success against a Dallas defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against tight ends, yielding 7.7 fantasy points per game to the position (tied for 12th in the league).
outlooksByWeek.11: George Kittle continues to be one of the NFL's most consistent tight ends ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 clash with Minnesota. Kittle tallied six catches for 74 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, marking his eighth straight contest with at least four receptions. He's also registered at least 58 yards seven times during that span, giving him a very reliable weekly floor. Kittle could find the sledding tough against Minnesota, though, as the Vikings have given up the fewest fantasy points per game (5.1) to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cameron Dicker's volume increased for a second straight week in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs. While the team's offense continues to struggle, Justin Herbert is at least putting together longer drives, and during those two contests Dicker has gone 6-for-7 on FG tries with all of his attempts coming from inside 50 yards. He likely won't be able to squander many chances in Week 5 against a Broncos team allowing 23.5 points per game, 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cameron Dicker's opportunities continue to be inconsistent due to the struggles of the Chargers' offense. The kicker hasn't attempted more than two PATs in any of the team's first five games, going a perfect 9-for-9, and he's seen one or fewer field goal attempts in three of those five contests. With the offensive line in shambles and Justin Herbert running out of healthy targets, Dicker's volume doesn't seem likely to pick up anytime soon. He'll face a Kansas City squad in Week 6 that's allowing 19.3 points per game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cameron Dicker failed to get an extra-point attempt in Week 6 for the first time this season, accounting for all the Chargers' points with two field goals in a 22-6 loss to Kansas City. Coming out of a bye, the offense will hopefully be a bit healthier and energized, providing Dicker with more opportunities, but he has kicked multiple field goals in three of the last four contests. In Week 8, he'll take aim at a Rams team that's allowing 22.7 points per game, 16th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick in four straight games, converting all three of his field goal attempts in a Week 8 loss to the Rams but failing to even see a PAT for a second straight contest. The Chargers' offensive struggles limit Dicker's opportunities despite his accuracy, and the advantage of playing his home games indoors. Dicker will look for a little more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans team that's giving up 24.3 points per game, 18th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cameron Dicker continues to benefit from the Chargers' inability to finish drives. The 26-year-old kicker has booted multiple field goals in five of the last six games, going 15-for-16 on FG attempts over that stretch but attempting just six extra points, converting them all. The steady volume gives Dicker a solid floor heading into a Week 10 clash with a Ravens team allowing 26.2 points per game, tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cameron Dicker booted three field goals for a third straight game, and the fifth time in the last seven, as the Chargers recorded their first win of 2026 in a Week 10 victory over the Ravens. The team's offensive struggles have created extra FG opportunities for its kicker, and Dicker has yet to kick more than two PATs in a game even as his field goal volume remains steady. That gives him a somewhat reliable floor, but a questionable ceiling, heading into a Week 11 clash with a Jets team allowing 25.4 points a contest, 22nd in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Allen has his work cut out for him when the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9. He ran for his ninth touchdown in seven games during Week 8 and tossed two touchdown passes for the fourth time this season. He's matchup-proof, but Allen will face constant pressure from Minnesota's heavy blitzing scheme that's allowed only four touchdown passes and 81 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Allen will seek a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. In Week 9 at Minnesota, Allen, in the face of constant pressure, had his first game of the year with just one touchdown while being held under 250 yards for the fourth time. The Jets have allowed a 16:1 TD:INT ratio through nine games, but Allen threw for only 148 yards and no scores against them in his lone 2025 matchup, suggesting a lower-than-usual ceiling for arguably the league's best quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.11: Josh Allen faces potential workload limitations in the Bills' Week 11 game against the Dolphins. Allen completed only 11 of 21 passes against the Jets in Week 10, his second-lowest volume of the season, as Buffalo was able to get out to a comfortable lead and not challenge the Jets through the air. Another potentially uncompetitive game seems to be looming, and while Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns to go with his 13 passing scores, Miami has allowed quarterbacks to run for just two touchdowns all season. Allen routinely gets his fantasy points, but Week 11 expectations can be tempered slightly.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jadarian Price is coming off an inefficient return from IR heading into Seattle's Week 9 clash against the Cardinals. Price moved past a chest injury to lead Seattle's backfield in carries against Chicago on Monday Night Football, but he garnered just 29 yards on 10 totes and eight yards on two catches. He shared RB snaps fairly equally with Zach Charbonnet, and if the duo continues in a timeshare, both players may have a limited week-to-week fantasy ceiling. The Cardinals do present a relatively favorable matchup, as they're middling or worse in most statistical categories versus running backs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jadarian Price looks to be settling in as Seattle's No. 2 RB ahead of a Week 10 clash against Las Vegas. The rookie running back handled 13 touches this past Sunday in a win over Arizona while Zach Charbonnet logged 17 touches. However, Charbonnet had 16 carries to Prize's nine, suggesting that the former may be leaning more toward a change-of-pace role. Both Charbonnet and Price could be utilized heavily against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most fantasy points per game (23.1) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tucker Kraft will look to do more with his targets as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Kraft stayed involved in Week 6 against the Cowboys, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has continued to get opportunities with a 25-249-1 receiving line off 37 targets, but he still sits behind the two-man punch of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson at this point in the year. Luckily for Kraft, the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (31.9) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tucker Kraft will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Kraft found the end zone once again in Week 8 against the Panthers, finishing the game with six catches for 53 yards and his score. The tight end has now posted a 35-350-3 receiving line on 49 targets this season, and he's found the end zone in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Kraft didn't get to join in on any of the fun of Green Bay's offensive explosion in Week 9 over the Patriots, as he brought in just one of his three targets for one yard and rushed the ball twice for eight yards. He's now posted a 36-351-3 receiving line across the first nine games of the campaign. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he logged three catches for 65 yards against in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Jacobs will again have an asterisk next to his name as the Packers face the Patriots in Week 9. Jacobs has been active the last two weeks, and while he's averaged an inefficient 2.3 yards per carry on 32 attempts, he's salvaged his performances with three total touchdowns in this stretch. The veteran ball carrier also could be at risk of not playing in the near future, as the NFL continues to investigate his alleged physical incidents. This makes him an uncertain play, especially against a New England defense that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in Week 10 as the Packers take on the Vikings. Jacobs hurt his finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, and he's now set to undergo surgery, which will keep him out for a maximum of three weeks. The veteran ball carrier has now recorded 36 rushes for 80 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns as well. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong, and banged-up Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd will be Green Bay's available running backs against a tough Minnesota defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and three extra points for Dallas last game. Unfortunately, Aubrey also missed a kick from 50-plus yards out, and the Cowboys ended up losing to Arizona by three points in overtime. Still, Aubrey has now made three field goals and three extra points in each of the last two games for the Cowboys. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 9 versus the folding Colts. Indy is allowing 27.8 points per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brandon Aubrey missed yet another long field goal last game for Dallas. Aubrey did make two other tries, though pulled a 50-yarder wide left in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Aubrey is now 3-for-8 on attempts from 50-plus yards out this season. In Week 10, the Cowboys will face the 49ers. Points may be hard to come by, as San Fran is allowing just 19.5 points per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points for the Cowboys in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Aubrey did miss an extra point, his second of the season. However, both of Aubrey's field goals came from 50-plus yards out, giving him five such field goals on the season to date. In Week 11, Dallas will face a bumbling Titans squad. Tennessee is allowing 26.6 points per contest, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and the Seahawks welcome the Chiefs to town for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He's been on the physically unable to perform (PUP)/reserve list to begin 2026, but Seattle opened his three-week practice window back on Oct. 1. With that being said, Charbonnet will need to be activated by Thursday in order to avoid him being out for the rest of the season. He's expected to join the official roster after practicing in a limited fashion the last couple weeks. However, Charbonnet will likely be eased into the backfield rotation if he is indeed able to make his debut, so it would be wise to wait until after the meeting with Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a chance to return to Seattle's backfield in Week 8 against Chicago. Charbonnet has yet to play since tearing his ACL in January, but he was activated off the reserve/PUP list last week and logged a trio of full practices. Though he ultimately didn't play Sunday against Kansas City, another week of practice could be enough for Charbonnet to make his return Monday against the Bears. Should that happen, he'll face a Chicago defense that has given up five total touchdowns (three rushing, two receiving) to running backs through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zach Charbonnet will look to build upon an uneventful season debut when the Seahawks host the Cardinals in Week 9. Charbonnet logged his first game action since January this past Monday against Chicago and finished with 23 yards on six carries along with six yards on three catches. He shared the backfield primarily with Jadarian Price (12 touches), and that arrangement may cap both players' weekly production moving forward. Arizona does present a decent matchup, as the Cardinals are tied for 20th in the NFL with 18.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zach Charbonnet seems to be emerging as Seattle's No. 1 running back heading into a Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. In his second game back from ACL surgery, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 16 carries and 77 receiving yards against Arizona this past Sunday while adding one catch for nine yards. Rookie Jadarian Price still managed 13 touches, so Charbonnet doesn't seem likely to have the backfield all to himself. Both tailbacks could thrive against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed a league-worst 5.21 yards per carry to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Skyy Moore should be a depth option in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Skyy Moore was unable to catch his one target, but he also did play on offense more than was expected. The fifth-year wideout should remain a secondary choice, but he could start to garner more looks given the pass-heavy offense that Green Bay has operated with. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Skyy Moore should remain a secondary option in Green Bay's passing game against the Falcons in Week 3. Moore was utilized more in Week 2 against the Jets after Jayden Reed went down with an injury, garnering three targets and bringing in two of them for six yards. The former Kansas City wideout is the top kick returner for the Packers, but his playmaking abilities make him an interesting target for Jordan Love if he gets more involved in the offense. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Skyy Moore should continue to get opportunities as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Moore recorded three catches for 31 yards on a career-high seven targets in Week 3 against the Falcons. While a pass-heavy game script definitely helped the fifth-year wideout's cause, he has seen more of an offensive role with Jayden Reed sidelined due to a neck injury. Moore will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers in the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Skyy Moore will seek to stay involved as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Moore caught another pass in Week 5 against Tampa Bay, but it went for minus-two yards. The veteran remains an asset for Green Bay on special teams, but he'll need to do more in the coming weeks to hold any value fantasy-wise. He'll face a Chicago team that's ranked top five against fantasy wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Skyy Moore holds a questionable tag ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 matchup against the Cowboys. Moore suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter of the Packers' Week 5 blowout win over the Bears, and he was unable to return. The utility player has seen more usage with Jayden Reed out for the season with a neck injury, but he'll need to stay healthy himself if he hopes to capitalize. Moore, who has a 7-35-0 receiving line, will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Skyy Moore will remain out as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next three weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen and J. Michael Sturdivant busy on the return fronts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Skyy Moore will remain sidelined as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next  two weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton busy on the return fronts.
outlooksByWeek.9: Skyy Moore will remain inactive as the Packers play New England in Week 9. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next week. His absence should keep Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton busy as returners.
outlooksByWeek.10: Skyy Moore will look to return as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so his first chance to return will be this Sunday. If he's unable to play yet again, Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton should stay busy on the return fronts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenneth Walker continues to shine as the new focal point of Kansas City's offense. Through his first five games with the team, Walker has piled up eight total touchdowns-six rushing and two receiving-while topping 100 rushing yards in four of those contests. He leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, despite already having had his bye and having played one fewer game than Bijan Robinson and James Cook, the only other two backs with more than 600 yards. Walker will try to deliver a revenge game in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenneth Walker was on the receiving end of a revenge game by the Seahawks' defense in Week 7, getting held to a season-low 36 rushing yards and zero TDs. Last season's Super Bowl MVP is still second in the NFL in rushing yards with 701, just three behind Bijan Robinson, and Walker has played one fewer game thanks to Kansas City's early Week 5 bye. Walker will try to stay on course for the 2026 rushing crown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenneth Walker has been held out of the end zone and below 100 scrimmage yards in back-to-back games, both Kansas City losses. The star running back still sits third in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs' 773 yards, but he might need more help from Patrick Mahomes and the passing game to get defenses to stop loading up against him. Walker will look to bounce back in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kenneth Walker is coming off a massive performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, scoring three touchdowns (one rushing, two receiving) while racking up 143 scrimmage yards. The star running back is second in the NFL in rushing yards with 872, just behind Bijan Robinson's 880. He is fourth in scrimmage yards with 1,044, and tied for first with Jahmyr Gibbs in total TDs from scrimmage with 11. Walker could be leaned on even more heavily in Week 10 if Patrick Mahomes' elbow injury keeps him on the sideline, against a Falcons defense that's tied for 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kenneth Walker didn't suit up for Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons due to a minor groin injury. In his place, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. Walker is expected back in Week 11 against Arizona, but Johnson's performance could lead to more volume for the team's backup RB as the focus shifts toward making sure Walker still has something left for the playoffs, given KC's 7-2 record. Assuming Walker is cleared to return, he'll be facing a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zavion Thomas will seek to stay involved as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Thomas was on the field for a season-high 22 percent of offensive snaps in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, and he was able to bring in his sole target for 11 yards. The rookie remains a return specialist first at this point in the season, but he could continue to see opportunities in the passing game. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zavion Thomas will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Thomas logged a season-best performance in Week 6 against the Falcons, bringing in all three of his targets for 25 yards. The rookie wide receiver had just two catches to his name in the first five games of the season, so his output could continue to grow with Caleb Williams situated in the pass-heavy offense. New England has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zavion Thomas will seek to stay involved as the Bears take on Seattle in Week 8. Thomas logged a season-best performance in Week 6 against the Falcons, bringing in all three of his targets for 25 yards, but he went on to not garner a target in Week 7. The rookie has now totaled five catches for 37 yards this season. He'll aim to get back in the mix against a Seahawks defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.11: Zavion Thomas remains a depth option heading into Week 11 as the Bears play the Saints. Thomas logged another catch in Chicago's Week 9 win over the Buccaneers, and he's now recorded seven catches for 54 yards in his rookie season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked a tough eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliable fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Wright hopes to come out of the Dolphins' bye with a larger role in Week 7 against the Jets. Wright has only amassed 11 carries over his last two outings, finishing with 18 yards while not being targeted in the passing game. Ollie Gordon has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane (knee) went down for the season, leaving managers in a wait-and-see mode with regards to Wright against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, ranking near the middle of the pack league-wide.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Wright has not played a meaningful role out of the Dolphins' backfield and is uncertain to play in Week 8 against the Patriots due to a quad issue. He had five or six carries in each of his last three games, failing to average better than 1.8 yards per carry, and has not caught a pass all season. Facing a middling New England run defense seems less important than considering Wright's continued lack of clean health and the potential that Miami falls behind early and abandons the run.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Wright continues to play a minor role in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Wright has logged a 12% to 14% snap share over the last three weeks, not topping six offensive touches in any outing, with Ollie Gordon dominating carries. Detroit is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, which is in the middle of the pack, but they allow the third-fewest fantasy points to the position. Barring an injury to Gordon, Wright's usage is unlikely to change, keeping him off most fantasy radars.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jaylen Wright didn't factor into the Dolphins' backfield even before a quad injury cost him Week 9. He'll need to overcome that issue if he's to take aim at Indianapolis' vulnerable run defense in Week 10. Wright has just 19 total carries across his last four games, with Ollie Gordon dominating touches. The Colts are allowing 4.8 yards per carry and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing rushers, but Wright hasn't been afforded enough chances to take advantage of those deficiencies.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Wright continues to be on the wrong side of rushing attempts as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Wright hasn't logged more than six touches in any game this season and has reached 11 rushing yards just twice. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Ollie Gordon dominating carries and Miami's likely need to pass from behind as the game moves along, Wright doesn't offer much appeal.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Josh Downs has been outplayed by Keenan Allen since the Colts lost Alec Pierce to a heel injury. After exceeding 70 receiving yards twice through Week 3, Downs has compiled a meager 103 receiving yards over the the past three games combined, topping out at 47 yards in a game over that span. His role as a locked-in starter at WR for the Colts makes Downs a viable Week 7 flex play against the Vikings, though he has now gone nine consecutive games without a TD dating back to last season. Minnesota is allowing 133 yards per game to WRs but has limited the position to three TDs in five games, so Downs looks unlikely to end his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Downs has opened his fourth season in Indianapolis on a seven-game touchdown drought, and he has reached the 50-yard threshold just twice this season, with the last such performance coming in Week 3. It has been Keenan Allen rather than Downs stepping up during the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve. Despite his disappointing production so far, Downs leads the Colts with 46 targets and is a decent flex option for Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that's allowing a league-high 210 receiving yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Downs scored his first TD of the season, accounting for the Colts' lone score in their 42-7 Week 8 loss to Jacksonville, but he fell short of 50 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive game. Downs continues to start in Indianapolis' low-octane passing game and has drawn at least four targets in every game. Ahead of a Week 9 home game against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 164.1 receiving yards and one TD per game to wide receivers, Downs' consistent involvement, coupled with Dallas' defensive struggles, makes him a viable fantasy WR3 or flex option for Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs where he'll be catching passes from Patrick Mahomes, assuming the QB is healthy after hurting his elbow in Week 9. Downs will enjoy a QB upgrade, but he'll face more competition for targets from Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce.
