With Worthy also nursing an injury, Downs could log a big workload in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Josh Downs made an immediate difference in his Kansas City debut, catching four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Falcons despite running just eight routes and playing only 10 snaps. Picked up from the Colts at the trade deadline, Downs' efficiency on a limited workload bodes well, but he'll still be the No. 2 wide receiver behind Rashee Rice, with Travis Kelce and the team's running backs also factoring significantly into the passing game. Downs will try to build on this performance in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.7: Dylan Laube has begun to find a niche in the Raiders' offense under Klint Kubiak. All nine of Laube's touches this season have come in the last two games, and he's turned them into 24 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown. The third-year running back's primary role is still as a kickoff returner, but with Ashton Jeanty struggling to be a consistent threat on the ground, his backups have gotten more work. Laube remains the No. 3 option on the depth chart, though, behind Jeanty and Mike Washington, and he's unlikely to break out in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Mims has yet to get significant work as a pass catcher this season for the Broncos, but that could soon change. The speedster missed two games with a foot injury, and in the two games in which he's been healthy, he sat behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and Pat Bryant on the depth chart. Bryant left a Week 4 loss to the 49ers with an ankle sprain, however, and Mims garnered his first targets of the season, catching one of three for 10 yards. He's always capable of producing in the return game, but Mims could contribute on offense in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Mims' role in the Broncos' offense has increased with Pat Bryant sidelined. Over the last two weeks, Mims has caught three of five targets for 16 yards while adding three rushing yards on one carry. Those numbers are modest at best, but the fourth-year speedster is a big-play candidate every time he gets the ball in his hands, whether as a pass catcher or as a kick returner. Mims isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Mims continues to fill a secondary role in a lackluster Broncos offense. The fourth-year speedster has logged nine targets over the last three games while Pat Bryant has been injured, turning that volume into a 5-29-0 line while also taking one carry for three yards. Mims has also handled kick return duties during that time, but it would likely take an injury to Jaylen Waddle or Courtland Sutton for him to move into a significant role in the passing game. Mims could get a chance to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 in a Week 7 clash with a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Marvin Mims is coming off his best performance of the season, catching both his targets for 53 yards, gaining three yards on his only carry, and adding 111 kick return yards. While the production on offense was modest, Mims has been the wide receiver to benefit most from the absence of Pat Bryant in the Broncos' underpowered passing game. Bryant will miss at least one more game with an ankle injury, but Mims will struggle to take advantage in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Marvin Mims caught exactly two passes in each of the Broncos' last four games, producing an 8-82-0 line on 11 targets over that stretch while also chipping in 25 rushing yards on four carries. The fourth-year speedster's primary role remains as a kick returner, and he's amassed 276 return yards in those four contests. With Pat Bryant likely to return soon from an ankle injury, Mims' usage on offense is set to decline, but he might still be able to contribute in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Marvin Mims logged multiple touches for a fifth straight game in Week 9, the Broncos' final contest before their bye. During that stretch, the speedy wide receiver has managed a 9-82-0 line on 13 targets while adding 30 rushing yards on five carries. That modest production has come while both Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle have missed time, with Waddle suffering a concussion in Week 9. Assuming both are healthy and in the lineup coming out of the bye, Mims' role could be limited. He'll try to take advantage of any opportunities he does get in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chig Okonkwo has posted back-to-back 60-plus yard outings for Washington, and could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season.  No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Okonkwo has amassed 13 targets in the last two games alone. In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season. Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chig Okonkwo made a dazzling one-handed catch last game for Washington. The highlight-reel grab is a candidate for one of the top receptions of the NFL season to date. Okonkwo finished with two catches for 32 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. He was targeted four times. In Week 9, Okonkwo will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chig Okonkwo has been targeted at least six times in three of the last four contests for the Commanders. Okonkwo caught six passes for 57 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams last game. Okonkwo has at least 55 receiving yards in three of the last four games for Washington. However, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants in Week 10. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chig Okonkwo has been a frequent target of quarterback Jayden Daniels since returning from injury for the Commanders. Okonkwo has at least six targets in four of the last five contests for Washington.  In fact, Okonkwo has been targeted 15 times over the last two games alone. Okonkwo is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, though. In Week 11, he will face a fairly stingy Cincinnati pass defense. The Bengals are allowing only 216.2 passing yards per clash, which is 11th in the league. Likewise, Cincy has given up just 11 throwing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.
